evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Amber Protocol — dsh Integration Amber Protocol ships as an installable **dsh bundle** named `dsh-amber-protocol`. Installing it with the native profile plugin command adds one declared dsh bundle layer that resolves its own installed location, starts Amber's stdio MCP server, exposes Amber skills through dsh's filesystem skill provider, and governs the workspace at `process.cwd()` by default. Amber is discoverable on the official [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic. ## Install (recommended) ```bash # Install once; dsh adds the Amber bundle layer to your profile. # This modifies only dependency and bundle declarations managed by dsh; # it does NOT write the profile's patch file. dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-amber-protocol # Ordinary startup loads Amber after install (no repeated --patch flag). dsh --profile web ``` On Windows, default port `3080` is often in a reserved range. If listen fails with `EACCES`, pass `--port 13080`. ## What you get ### MCP tools The dsh agent gains 10 governed tools under the stable `amber` server namespace (prefixed `mcp__amber__`): - `amber.governance.report` — readiness score, risks, next actions - `amber.session.start` / `status` / `approve` / `verify` — session lifecycle - `amber.context.ingest` / `amber.object.query` — context knowledge lifecycle - `amber.route.test` — route validation - `amber.fn.repoOverview` / `amber.fn.sessionEvidence` — function queries All mutating operations (session start, approve, context ingest) return `approvalRequired: true` — dsh must explicitly approve them. Read-only operations execute directly. This is the F018 fail-closed governance seam. ### Journey skills The dsh agent gains 5 skills discoverable through the native skill catalog (4 journeys plus the `amber` router that dispatches to them): - `amber-delivery` — objective → plan → session evidence → acceptance - `amber-diagnosis-adoption` — audit readiness, adopt or repair governance - `amber-context-continuity` — distill context, verify loadouts, resume - `amber-continuous-improvement` — select next improvement slice, loop ## Bundle structure | File | Purpose | | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | `package.json` | Bundle manifest; declares `dsh.bundle.patch` + `files` contract | | `cordis.patch.yml` | Declarative dsh patch layer (runtime, MCP client, skill provider) | | `runtime.js` | Path-resolution adapter; exposes `amberBundlePaths` service | | `README.md` | This file | | `LICENSE` | MIT | The runtime resolves `amber-protocol` from its own installed module location (`require.resolve("amber-protocol/package.json")`) and exposes the MCP script and skills directory to later bundle rows. Configuration expressions do not rely on `__dirname`, `require`, a hard-coded profile name, or a global install. ## Unpublished checkout fallback (overlay) If you are developing Amber itself and the bundle is not yet published, use the static overlay patches instead. These are **not** shipped in the bundle `files` array — they exist only for local development. **Alternative — local tarball install with pnpm overrides:** if you want to test the bundle contract (not the overlay) against an unpublished `1.6.0` tarball, `dsh plugin add` forwards to pnpm. When `amber-protocol@1.6.0` is not yet on the registry, add a pnpm `overrides` entry so the bundle's `amber-protocol@^1.6.0` dependency resolves from the local tarball instead of the registry (which still has `1.5.1`): ```yaml # In the profile's pnpm-workspace.yaml (dsh creates this on first init): overrides: amber-protocol: file:/path/to/amber-protocol-1.6.0.tgz ``` Then: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/amber-protocol-1.6.0.tgz dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-amber-protocol-1.6.0.tgz ``` Once `1.6.0` is published, plain `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-amber-protocol` works without overrides. ### Overlay patches | File | Purpose | | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | | `amber-mcp.patch.yml` | Path A — expose Amber governance tools via MCP server | | `amber-skills.patch.yml` | Path B — expose Amber journey skills to the dsh agent | | `amber-full.patch.yml` | A + B combined in one layer | ### Prerequisites (overlay only) 1. **dsh installed**: `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh` (or `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh`) 2. **A dsh profile**: `dsh --profile web` auto-initializes on first use 3. **This checkout**: you need a local clone so the patch can point at `scripts/amber-mcp.js` and `skills/` 4. **Amber in the target repo** (if it is not this checkout): `node scripts/amber.js init --target ` ### Overlay usage Edit `amber-full.patch.yml` first: replace `/path/to/amber-protocol` with this checkout. `--target` is the repository Amber should govern (it may differ from this checkout). Recommended — overlay at launch, leave the profile file untouched: ```sh dsh --profile web --patch /path/to/amber-protocol/dsh/amber-full.patch.yml ``` Alternative — copy into the profile layer (overwrites an empty or existing `cordis.patch.yml`): ```sh cp dsh/amber-full.patch.yml "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml" dsh --profile web ``` The overlay patches use hardcoded absolute paths. Adjust the two paths in each patch file: - **`scripts/amber-mcp.js` path**: point to your `amber-protocol` checkout - **`skills` path**: point to the `skills` directory under the same checkout - **`--target` path**: the repository Amber governs (can differ from the `amber-protocol` checkout) ### HMR dsh watches `cordis.patch.yml` for changes. Editing the patch file triggers hot-reload: the MCP client disconnects and reconnects, and skill directories are re-scanned — no restart needed. ## Verified - MCP server responds to `initialize` + `tools/list` (10 tools) - Read-only tools (`governance.report`) execute directly (`approvalRequired: false`) - Mutating tools (`session.start`) fail-closed (`approvalRequired: true`, `executed: false`) - Skills match dsh `SKILL.md` frontmatter format (5 skills, kebab-case names) - `dsh --dump-config` composes the bundle layer with zero errors - `npm pack --dry-run` ships every declared asset (`cordis.patch.yml`, `runtime.js`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `package.json`)
# Amber Protocol > **Governed Agent Harness for real engineering systems.** > **Amber Protocol is the governed execution boundary between AI agents and real > systems.** It governs what an agent may see, use, execute, and emit, with whose > approval, and what evidence proves it — in files beside the code, not in chat history. > > **Amber Protocol 是 AI Agent 与真实系统之间的治理执行边界。** ![Amber Protocol](./assets/readme/amber-protocol-banner.png) ![CI](https://github.com/Bandersnatch0x/amber-protocol/workflows/CI/badge.svg) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/amber-protocol?style=flat-square) ![Node Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E20.19%20%7C%7C%20%5E22.12%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D23-brightgreen?style=flat-square) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg?style=flat-square)

What is Amber · Who it is for · Journey · Install · Quick Start · Team Replication Charter · 简体中文

For repositories already using coding agents in real delivery work.
Plans, evidence, decisions, and handoffs stay inspectable beside the code.

**Version:** 2.0.1 · **Status:** Stable · [Milestones & test status →](./ROADMAP.md) --- ## What is Amber? Amber Protocol is a repository-local governance layer for projects that already use coding agents in recurring, real delivery work. The hard part is no longer only producing code. It is preserving enough trustworthy state for the next person or agent to understand what happened, what was approved, what evidence exists, and what should happen next. Amber makes that state explicit through plans, sessions, evidence, decisions, and handoffs stored beside the code. Its core outcome is **Trusted Continuation**: another person or agent can enter without the old chat, identify the current state, and take one correct next step. **Amber = the in-repo team replication layer: how a team safely uses AI on _this_ codebase, written as handoff-ready file evidence.** It sits under your existing coding engine and adds governance plus evidence. It is not another agent runtime, and not an org-scale platform. | Amber is | Amber is not | | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | | In-repo governance and evidence protocol | Org-scale Skill marketplace / plugin store | | Reviewable plans / gates / approvals / handoffs | Cross-repo gateway or cross-machine control dashboard | | Local conventions a team can replicate | A scheduler / daemon that runs your project commands | --- ## Layering | Layer | Role | | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Engine** | Edit code, call tools, run models and the agent loop (provided by your chosen coding host) | | **Governance (Amber)** | Plans, gates, approvals, doctor/audit, handoff; evidence written as repo files | | **Upper Shell (optional)** | Consumes Amber via MCP only; must not rewrite the `.amber` contract or push the agent loop into Amber core | Engines do the work; Amber proves what was done, whether it is safe to keep, and how to hand it off. ## What Amber will NOT do These are product boundaries, not TODOs: 1. Not a replacement for the coding engine / not a general agent runtime 2. No Dynamic Workflow execution, no live subagent dispatch, no automatic execution of your project commands 3. No org-scale marketplace, cross-repo gateway, or cross-machine dashboard. The only scheduler is the experimental `amber harness runtime` (schedule, tick, daemon), which runs a closed set of Amber-internal proposal jobs and never your project commands 4. No overwrite of existing project docs (`init` / `wiki` only create missing files) 5. No filesystem containment: a worktree separates checkout state, but absolute-path writes can still escape it. Containing writes requires OS sandboxing. The `harness`, `runner`, `retention`, `external`, `breakglass`, and `sync` command families are **EXPERIMENTAL**. They remain callable and are listed with a marker only under `amber --all`. Default help keeps `audit`, `init`, `doctor`, `next`, `plan`, `handoff`, and `session`. Stability is separate from visibility tier. Full boundaries: [Team Replication Charter](./docs/TEAM_REPLICATION_CHARTER.md) and [SPEC.md](./SPEC.md). ## Who it is for The target environment is a **Coding-Agent-Enabled Repository**: maintainers already use one or more coding agents for ongoing delivery under human review. A one-off experiment or a repository that merely installed an agent tool does not qualify. - **Primary user — Repository Maintainer:** accountable for the repository outcome and continuity. - **Working user — agent-assisted developer:** frames and performs bounded delivery work. - **Decision user — reviewer:** makes go/no-go decisions from plans, diffs, and evidence. ## Why Amber? AI coding work becomes easier to trust when the workflow leaves inspectable evidence: - **Continue without the old chat:** plans, sessions, evidence, and handoffs make state portable across people and agents. - **Review from repository evidence:** decisions rest on inspectable artifacts, not a completion claim in a transcript. - **Recover at the right stage:** failures and interruptions remain attached to the step that produced them. - **Keep authority explicit:** human approvals and governed boundaries are records, not hidden runtime assumptions. ## Product journey ```text Fit -> Adopt -> First trusted continuation -> Deliver -> Recover -> Review / Accept ``` | Journey | User outcome | Default surface | Completion evidence | | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | J0 · Fit | Decide whether Amber addresses a real continuity or review failure | `amber audit` | Read-only findings and an explicit adopt/defer decision | | J1 · Adopt | Add the minimum repository-local surface without overwrites | `amber init`, `amber doctor` | A repeatable setup check | | J2 · First continuation | Prove a fresh context can continue one real task correctly | `amber next`, `amber plan`, `amber session`, `amber handoff` | A new person or agent acts correctly without reading the old chat | | J3 · Deliver | Frame, authorize, work, prove, review, and hand off/accept | Agent journey; CLI fallback | Plan, session, command evidence, and checkpoint agree | | J4 · Recover | Resume after failure, pause, or context loss at the correct stage | `amber session`, `amber next`, `amber handoff` | Failure remains visible and the recovery action is bounded | | J5 · Review / Accept | Make a go/no-go decision from repository evidence | Plans, gates, evidence, Web Viewer | Review and acceptance can be explained without the transcript | Feature, bugfix, and refactor routes remain backend policy. Users keep one frontstage model: ```text Frame -> Authorize -> Work -> Prove -> Review -> Handoff / Accept ``` Context repair, continuous improvement, team expansion, and high-assurance operations are conditional paths. They do not block the first Trusted Continuation. See the [feature matrix](./docs/wiki/features/feature-map.md) and [complete journey definitions](./docs/wiki/product/user-scenarios.md). ## Installation ### From npm (Recommended) ```bash npm install -g amber-protocol amber --version ``` ### From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/Bandersnatch0x/amber-protocol.git cd amber-protocol npm install node scripts/amber.js --version ``` ## Upgrading to 2.0.0 2.0.0 is a **breaking release**: three command families that shipped in 1.6.0 — and were already marked deprecated in its help text — are now removed. Nothing else changed shape: plans, sessions, gates, approvals, evidence, and handoffs keep their contracts. | Removed in 2.0.0 | What to use instead | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `amber agent dispatch\|review\|status` | `amber harness` (the Contract → Run → Event spine); `amber governance report` | | `amber team inspect\|install\|pin\|update\|rollback` | `amber maintenance` (scaffold drift, artifact drift); `amber doctor` | | `amber adoption report\|list\|index\|validate\|compare\|gate\|status\|bundle\|next-actions` | `amber governance report`; the `amber-diagnosis-adoption` journey skill | The disposition is recorded, not implied — the removed surfaces and their replacement routes stay readable from the tool itself: ```bash amber harness legacy --target . # every removed surface with its replacement route ``` If you pin `^1.6.0`, a `npm update` will not cross into 2.0.0 — that range deliberately stops short of the break. Move to `^2.0.0` once you are off the removed commands. ## Quick Start (about 10 minutes) Use one real task to test whether Amber creates Trusted Continuation. File generation alone is not activation. ```bash # J0 — establish fit without changing the project amber audit --target my-project # J1 — install the minimum surface; existing files are skipped amber init --target my-project amber doctor --target my-project # J2 — frame one real goal and follow the state-derived next step amber next --objective "finish the current API change" --target my-project # Generate a repository-local continuation bundle amber handoff --target my-project ``` Now open a fresh agent session or ask another maintainer to inspect the repository **without the old chat**. Amber is activated only when that new context can explain the current state and take one correct next step. `init` and `wiki` never overwrite existing files. Default help exposes seven fallback verbs: `audit`, `init`, `doctor`, `next`, `plan`, `handoff`, and `session`. `amber --all` keeps the expert and compatibility surface available. See the [CLI reference](./docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md). Expert path (not the homepage main line): read-only continuous-improvement discovery via `amber loop recommend` — see the loop sections under "What It Won't Do" below. --- ## Command surface Default `amber --help` projects **seven primary verbs** — the whole journey fits in them. `amber --all` lists the full surface: expert command families, deprecated `profile` / `task` / `result`, and the six experimental families (`harness`, `runner`, `retention`, `external`, `breakglass`, `sync`), each marked `(experimental)`: | Verb | What it does | | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `amber audit` | Read-only readiness inspection of a repository | | `amber init` | Install the minimum repository-local surface (never overwrites) | | `amber doctor` | Validate the Amber setup | | `amber next` | Deterministic route advice for a stated objective | | `amber plan` | Scaffold a feature plan | | `amber handoff` | Produce the portable continuation bundle | | `amber session` | Inspect or manage the session lifecycle | Everything else is governance and platform surface, deliberately one flag away in `amber --all`: - **Context and knowledge** — `wiki`, `context request|ingest|verify|refresh|stats`, `memory`, `knowledge` - **Governed records** — `artifact`, `principal`, `evidence`, `approval`, `gate`, `policy` - **Control and assurance** — `projection`, `adapter`, `maintain`, `retention`, `external`, `breakglass`, `eval run` - **Delivery and reporting** — `sync session`, `governance report`, `loop recommend`, `learnings`, `break-loop`, `harness` Hiding a family from the default help changes discovery, never capability: every family is documented in the [CLI reference](./docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md), and `amber --help` is authoritative for its flags. ## Using it in DeepSeek Harness The overlay ships as a native [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) bundle: ```bash # Install once; dsh adds the Amber bundle layer to the profile dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-amber-protocol # Afterwards a normal start loads Amber (no repeated --patch) dsh --profile web ``` On Windows the default port `3080` is often reserved; add `--port 13080` if the listener fails. **Unpublished-checkout fallback:** if you are developing Amber itself and the bundle is not published yet, use an overlay patch instead. Edit `dsh/amber-full.patch.yml`, replace `/path/to/amber-protocol` with this repository's path, and layer it at startup without touching the profile: ```bash dsh --profile web --patch /path/to/amber-protocol/dsh/amber-full.patch.yml ``` Full notes: [dsh/README.md](./dsh/README.md). --- ## Core Concepts Amber organizes governance into seven control layers, weighted toward safety — the higher the priority, the more of Amber's surface that layer gets: | Layer | Role in Amber | Priority | | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | `Governance` | Approval records, safe defaults, policy boundaries, and adoption controls constrain behavior. | Highest | | `Verification` | Doctor, audit, validation, review, and gate surfaces provide explicit checks. | High | | `Observability` | Timelines, manifests, ledgers, and reports make behavior inspectable. | High | | `Lifecycle` | Routes, sessions, checkpoints, and worktrees organize work locally. | Medium | | `Context` | Starter docs, wiki scaffolds, manifests, and handoff artifacts keep project context explicit. | Medium | | `Tooling` | CLI commands, schemas, validators, workflow packs, and profiles expose explicit interfaces. | Medium | | `Execution` | Gated and capability-bound — governed command execution exists behind four gates plus frozen per-attempt admission; there is no un-gated runtime, and no capability is registered in a vanilla install. | Low | The through-line: strengthen `Governance`, `Verification`, and `Observability`; keep `Lifecycle` repository-local; avoid drifting into a full agent platform. The [governance model](./docs/architecture/governance-model.md) maps each layer to concrete commands. **What gets installed** — the minimum surface `doctor` checks for: - `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` — agent-facing rules - `feature_list.json` — tracked feature state - `PROGRESS.md`, `session-handoff.md`, `clean-state-checklist.md`, `evaluator-rubric.md` - `.amber/continuous-improvement/state.json` - a minimal `docs/wiki/` — project context, system map, runbook, verification, glossary All starter files are safe defaults. `init` and `wiki` skip existing files and report what _would_ be created in dry-run mode. ## What It Won't Do These boundaries are part of the product, not TODOs: - No dynamic workflow execution or live subagent dispatch - No automatic / unattended execution of target-project commands — see "Governed loop execution" below for the one gated exception - No scheduled / cron / hook-triggered execution of target-project commands; the only scheduler is the experimental bounded H7 maintenance runtime, `amber harness runtime` - No external writes (PRs, issue trackers, notifications) except through the experimental `external` family's registered contracts and approvals; no agent tool-call interception - No automatic rewrite of existing project docs - No governed verb-stage execution in a vanilla install: the implementation-owned adapter table ships **empty** (there is no fallback), so `session run` stages fail closed until a capability is registered — and registering one is a reviewed code change, not a config edit ### Governed loop execution (opt-in, gated) Since [ADR-0003](./docs/adr/0003-governance-gated-execution.md), Amber can run a loop contract's declared `governed.command` — but only behind four gates: a declarative policy check (`.amber/governance/rules.json`, deny-wins / default-deny), an explicit `amber loop approve` (one approval authorizes one run), an isolated git worktree (your main checkout is never the cwd), and a tamper-evident hash-chain ledger. Default `loop run` is still dry-run; execution needs `--execute`. The worktree separates checkout state; without OS sandboxing, absolute-path writes can still escape it. ```bash amber loop approve --file --contract --reviewer amber loop run --file --contract --execute amber loop verify-ledger --contract amber governance standards --target . # honest OWASP-ASI coverage of what this does (and doesn't) cover ``` For the full boundary notes, see [SPEC.md](./SPEC.md). ### `amber loop recommend` — the safe continuous-improvement entry `amber loop recommend` is read-only: it scans the local workflow-packs' loop contracts, scores them against a maintenance goal, and prints the dry-run command best suited to human review. It never schedules work, executes workflow steps, dispatches agents, or writes an external system. ```bash amber loop recommend --target . --goal "continuous improvement" --json amber loop run --file workflow-packs/safe-amber-bootstrap.pack.json --contract daily-amber-triage --dry-run --json ``` Loop contracts remain unscheduled. Use `--dry-run` for previews; governed execution needs `--execute` and an approval. ### Governed trust layer (trusted-control contracts) Beyond the journey surface, Amber ships a contract-tested trust layer ([four canonical contracts](./docs/specs/) with product tests, all delivered): - **Governed execution attempts** — every `session run` attempt freezes its admission inputs (scope, policy, capability, request digest) before any effect; the gates re-verify against the frozen values, and authorization grants bind that frozen tuple with single-use consumption. Drift is refused at the gate, before execution. - **Evidence with assurance levels** — receipts carry `unavailable / observed / replayable / verified`, and a replay bundle (`amber handoff bundle --replay-scope`) rebuilds the authorization chain offline. - **Governed memory** — durable lessons flow through `amber memory` (request → ingest → human approve → book); `MEMORY.md` stays human-curated and hash-registered. - **Instruction-surface evals** — `amber eval run` replays deterministic model-independent checks of the agent-facing surfaces. - **MCP Action Types** — 21 thin projections of the governed verbs; mutating actions return `approvalRequired` and are never executed by the MCP surface. These surfaces are the protocol's reference implementation: governed verb stages currently **fail closed** (no capability is registered — see "What It Won't Do") and the canonical specs are awaiting their coordinator re-review. ## Documentation | Topic | Link | | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Full CLI reference | [docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md](./docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md) | | Getting started guide | [docs/guides/user-getting-started.md](./docs/guides/user-getting-started.md) | | Architecture & governance model | [docs/architecture/governance-model.md](./docs/architecture/governance-model.md) | | Deployment & ops | [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](./docs/guides/DEPLOYMENT.md) | | Monitoring / notifications / policy | [MONITORING_SETUP.md](./docs/guides/MONITORING_SETUP.md) · [NOTIFICATION_SETUP.md](./docs/guides/NOTIFICATION_SETUP.md) · [POLICY_CONFIGURATION.md](./docs/guides/POLICY_CONFIGURATION.md) | | Troubleshooting | [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](./docs/guides/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) | | Full docs index | [docs/README.md](./docs/README.md)

# dsh-plugin-verispring

Verispring three-role session architecture plus a bundled local knowledge graph (manon), substantially improving main-session context and reducing premium model API costs.
[中文](README.zh.md) | English

## What it enforces

| # | Gate | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dispatch spec gate | `subagent` / `subagent_fork` requires the dispatch spec content to have appeared in the session (a read result containing the spec's first-line marker; state is persisted in the session log and survives restarts) |
| 2 | Resident scout | The first dispatch of a session is pinned to the scout role at runtime (`description` is a display label only); once resident, repeats are denied with a `send_message` reuse pointer; escape hatch `touch /tmp/dsh-caseos-scout-reset-<pid>` (path is in the denial), and the reset is persisted too |
| 3 | Map first | Non-scout dispatch requires `<session workspace>/.project-map.md` (project root = `.git`/`.manon` present; otherwise fail-open) |
| 4 | Pinned model | Routes are enforced at runtime per role: the first dispatch uses the panel's scout route, later ones the executor route; explicit `provider`/`model` on the call is ignored. `subagent_fork` is always denied |
| 5 | Commit gate | `git commit` requires a prior read of `~/.dsh/specs/代码写作规范.md` |
| 6 | Leader scope | The leader's tool face shrinks to the review five (`bash`/`edit`/`write`/`read`/`read_image`) plus the dispatch face (`subagent`/`send_message`/`interrupt_agent`/`list_agents`), intersected with the tools that actually exist in the leader's view (desktop serves them from the preset layer, headless from the root layer); dispatch tools are shadowed by slim definitions. Scout and executor subagents get the full face of the `verispring-subagent` preset, and scouts are hard-denied `edit`/`write` through the dispatch request. Kill switch `CASEOS_SCOUT=0` drops the scout part of the division clause |
| 7 | manon bridge | Resolves the local graph CLI (`MANON_KG_BIN` > bundled `manon/manon-kg` > legacy `~/manon/manon-kg`) and, when present, injects a concise usage section: command surface, store location, scout ownership, semantics in `~/.dsh/specs/Manon调用规则.md`. **The load-bearing part is the invocation rule**: dsh's subprocess service strips KEY/TOKEN-shaped env vars from children (anti-leak), so a bare `manon-kg sync` always fails with a missing key — the injected form sources `~/.dsh/manon.env` inside the bash command first (the scrub only strips the first hop; grandchildren inherit freely). Secret values never pass through or get printed |

The bundle patch also configures the subagent tool: `backgroundMode: continuable`, `maxDepth: 1`,
and the executor persona; both presets turn `modelSelectionSettings` off on `tool-subagent`
(routes are enforced per role, so model selection has no effect, and when it is on the `subagent`
tool registers into each session's own layer where the routing wrapper cannot shadow it). In
headless/CLI runs the process exits with the turn and background subagents are terminated with
it — pass `run_in_background: false` to `subagent` to wait in the foreground for the delivery.

## Context compaction (per role)

| Role | Mounted on | Trigger → summary cap |
|---|---|---|
| Main session (leader) | compaction group of the `standard` preset | 40% of the context window (~400k on a 1M window) → summary capped at 40k tokens |
| Scout/executor subagents | compaction group of the `verispring-subagent` preset | 60% of the context window (~600k) → summary capped at 60k tokens |

Both policies prune oversized tool results first (a result over 8192 characters keeps its first
4096 and last 1024), then condense the safely balanced history with DSH's structured template; no
verbatim tail is kept, and context overflow retries automatically. The summary length is chosen
by the model from a fixed template; the cap only bounds it, and real summaries usually run far shorter.

Subagents on `verispring-subagent`: the harness spawn request has no preset field and a child
inherits its parent's preset by default; dispatch-gate switches the child inside its creation
window (`agent/created`, before the first prompt) and records an `agent-preset/selected` event,
so a cold resume recomposes from the session log. The headless one-shot runner
(`dsh --profile … "<task>"`) composes no preset for the main session, so the main session does
not get the `standard` 400k policy — only a root-level `compaction-basic` if the profile enables
one; subagents are unaffected.

## Install

```bash
# Install / update (tracks main; pin a release with a tag like #v1.3.3)
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add github:brandonzyy/dsh-plugin-verispring

# Desktop app: Settings → Plugins → install, paste the same spec
```

The desktop app enables HMR by default (the base bundle turns it on whenever a profile
context exists), so installs initiated through the plugin manager **apply immediately** —
no restart needed. Already-running sessions keep their current tree; new sessions and new
dispatches pick up the new one. A restart is only required where HMR is explicitly disabled
(headless/SDK/ACP). Updates: uninstall and reinstall the same spec (the platform reserves
the Update button for official on-demand bundles).

## manon component (bundled)

`manon/` ships the full local code-graph CLI: the `manon-kg` entry, the
`matrixone_graph`/`codeindex`/`core` sources, and a frozen `requirements.txt`
(click/httpx/networkx/numpy/rich/PyYAML + the full tree-sitter language family — all
prebuilt wheels). Bridge resolution order: explicit `MANON_KG_BIN` > **bundled component**
(version-matched to this package) > legacy `~/manon/manon-kg`.

On first run the component bootstraps a Python venv and installs its dependencies (one-time
network, python3 ≥3.11 required), then works offline. The venv lives under
`${DSH_HOME:-~/.dsh}/manon-kg-runtime` (the installed package directory is read-only; the
runtime never writes into the package). tree-sitter language packs load
dynamically; a missing pack only downgrades that language. Keys come from
`~/.dsh/manon.env` + `~/.dsh/verispring.env`, sourced inside the bash command by the
injected invocation.

## Prerequisites (the gates tell you what is missing)

- **Profile composition**: the agent preset registry and a `preset-standard` entry (shipped by the
  desktop app and the web bundle). A bare `dsh-headless` profile has neither, and the plugin patch
  fails to load with `entry "preset-standard" not found`.
- **Spec files**: `~/.dsh/specs/子代理派遣规范.md` and `~/.dsh/specs/代码写作规范.md`
  (resolved against the home directory). Missing specs mean the corresponding gate keeps
  denying with directions — by design: every denial must be satisfiable.
- **Model route**: the profile needs a `verispring` provider with a `deepseek-flash`
  model (via `llm-pi-ai` or an equivalent adapter). For another gateway, update
  `agentOptions` in `cordis.patch.yml` and `DEFAULT_ROUTES` in
  `gates/dispatch-gate.js`, keeping the two in sync (a saved panel wins via `~/.dsh/verispring.json`).
- **manon (optional)**: bundled — no local install needed. Keys live in `~/.dsh/manon.env`
  (`MANON_EMBEDDING_API_KEY`, sync embeddings) and `~/.dsh/verispring.env`
  (`VERISPRING_API_KEY`, deep-query fallback); the injected invocation sources both files
  itself, so model/endpoint overrides (`MANON_DEEPQUERY_*` / `MANON_EMBEDDING_*`) set there
  apply to every session. Without manon, every other gate is unaffected.

## Configuration panel (v1.3+)

After install, the bundle detail page displays the configuration directly. The panel uses
the DSH shared form controls and reads the live model catalog, so provider and model choices
stay aligned with the Models configuration. The three agent route slots are editable and apply on save; the main session uses the native DSH model picker.
While the panel has never been saved (everything at defaults), the plugin rewrites no
enforcement surface — `verispring.json` and `manon.env` keep your
native values:

| Panel field | Persisted to | Takes effect |
|---|---|---|
| Surveying/execution provider / model / effort | `~/.dsh/verispring.json` | each route is enforced by the dispatch gate; execution defaults are also written to `tool-subagent` |
| Manon Deep Query provider / model / effort | `MANON_DEEPQUERY_*` keys in `~/.dsh/manon.env` | flows into manon-kg with the sourced invocation |
| embedding endpoint / model | `MANON_EMBEDDING_*` keys in `~/.dsh/manon.env` | re-run sync after switching models |

Writes are rooted at the Harness home (`DSH_HOME`), so multi-home/probe environments never
cross-contaminate; `manon.env` upserts only the panel-owned keys and preserves your
credential lines. The plugin ships the `verispring` `llm-pi-ai` route. Surveying and execution
each have independent provider, model, and reasoning-effort selectors. The Verispring key is
stored through DSH credentials; saving it discovers the gateway model list and refreshes the
catalog. The embedding model remains a text field.

## Model configuration guide

Three agent route slots are configurable in the plugin panel; the main session uses DSH's native model picker.

| Slot | Where | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Surveying / execution agents | independently selected in the plugin panel | **DeepSeek Flash** for both by default; each route can choose its own provider, model, and effort |
| Manon Deep Query | choose the verispring provider, model, and effort in the panel; key falls back to `VERISPRING_API_KEY` | **DeepSeek Flash + off** (shipped as recommended); saving writes `~/.dsh/manon.env` and the sourced invocation uses it. |
| embedding | env: `MANON_EMBEDDING_URL` / `MANON_EMBEDDING_MODEL` / `MANON_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` (defaults to SiliconFlow `BAAI/bge-m3`) | the built-in bge-m3 is the recommendation; switching requires a re-sync to rebuild vectors |

Minimal main-session + gateway config (goes into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`; pairs with
the plugin-pinned `verispring`/`deepseek-flash` route):

```yaml
- id: llm-pi-ai
  config:
    providers:
      verispring:
        displayName: Verispring
        apiKeyEnv: VERISPRING_API_KEY
        api: anthropic-messages
        baseURL: https://api.verispring.cn
        models:
          - id: claude-opus-5-5
            name: Claude Opus 5.5
            contextWindow: 1000000
            maxTokens: 128000
            compat:
              forceAdaptiveThinking: true
            reasoningEfforts:
              low: low
              medium: medium
              high: high
              xhigh: xhigh
              max: max
          - id: deepseek-flash
            name: DeepSeek Flash
            contextWindow: 1000000
            maxTokens: 384000
            reasoningEfforts:
              'off': null
              low: low
              high: high
              max: max
- id: agent-default-model
  config:
    provider: verispring
    model: claude-opus-5-5
```

> **Exclusive discounts**: contact the package author — **20% off Claude, 50% off DeepSeek Flash**; WeChat: `jinyong0716`.

## Compatibility

`peerDependencies` pins `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `4.0.4 || ~4.0.5-alpha.1`, and `engines.dsh`
covers dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 through 0.2.1-rc.1. Incompatible installs are rejected up front; the official
exemption flow exists for force-installs.

## Upgrade smoke check

Run `pnpm smoke` after a dsh upgrade for manifest and syntax checks. Set `DSH_BIN` and
`DSH_SMOKE_PROFILE` to add an official `--dump-config` composition check against an isolated
profile; the check must find the dispatch gate, configuration entry and subagent preset.

## Dependencies and upgrade surface

- The plugin itself imports `node:fs` / `node:os` / `node:path` / `node:url` only — no npm
  runtime dependencies. The manon component freezes its Python dependencies in
  `manon/requirements.txt`.
- cordis surface in use: `ctx.tools.guard`, `ctx.on("tools/result")`, `ctx.on("agent/created")`,
  `ctx.tools.restrict({allow/deny})`, `ctx.tools.schemas/get/register`, `ctx.systemPrompt.section`,
  `ctx.inject`, `ctx.logger.warn`.
- The manon component tracks the upstream manon repository; after upstream changes, re-test
  sync/query/deep-query as a set before updating the component here.

## Uninstall

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> remove dsh-plugin-verispring
```

Desktop: deselect and remove on the plugins page.

## License

MIT

# dsh-general-agentics **General Agentics 發行套件（bundle）for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)。** 用戶先安裝 DSH，再安裝本套件，一次獲得： 1. **貼牌**：側邊欄 mark/wordmark、對話首頁 hero 文字 logo 與致敬行、品牌主色、分頁標題、favicon、輸入框下方的 START HERE 模塊（皆為執行期替換，不修改、不破壞已安裝的 DSH） 2. **自帶技能**：14 個（`ga-identity` ＋ 13 個方法論技能，見下） 3. **MCP 預配置**：`ga-status`（`ga_bundle_info` 身分回報 ＋ `ga_health_check` 安裝健康自檢） 4. **設定面板**：Settings → General Agentics（bundle 版本、每個精選插件的版本與更新狀態、隨附技能、一鍵／手動更新） 5. **13 個精選第三方插件**：隨套件安裝並啟用（見「精選插件」一節） Built on DeepSeek Harness (DSH), MIT licensed. ## 設計原則 - **只走官方縫隙**：品牌透過三個 generic brand slot 佔位（`priority: -1` 陰影覆蓋官方 occupants——slot 規則是「同 cell 最低 priority 者渲染」），不停用 `ui-brand-official`，不修改任何 DSH 檔案。 - **不破簽章、不怕升級**：本套件存在於 profile（`~/.dsh/profiles//node_modules`），DSH 升級不會覆蓋它；解除安裝即完全還原官方品牌。 - **手寫、零建置**：`lib/client.js` 採用 shell module loader 的 lazy-CJS 形狀（與 dsh-pomodoro 等第三方出貨格式一致），無需 repo 內未發佈的 build preset。 ## 覆蓋範圍（誠實清單） | 表面 | 本套件 | 備註 | |---|---|---| | 側邊欄 mark / wordmark | ✅ | slot 佔位；2026-10-13 瀏覽器實測（乾淨 profile）確認渲染 | | 對話首頁 hero mark | ✅ | slot 佔位；實測確認我們的 wordmark 渲染 | | 品牌主色 | ✅ | `theme.overrideTokens`（light/dark 成對，契約要求）。注意 token 寫在 `` 的 inline style 上，不是 `:root`；量測時別探 `document.documentElement` | | 分頁標題 | ✅ | 執行期改寫 + MutationObserver 抵抗 shell 重設；實測 `document.title === "General Agentics"` | | favicon | ✅ | 執行期替換 `link[rel=icon]`；實測兩個 link 皆為 data URI 且含品牌色 | | PWA 名稱 | ⚠️ 盡力 | manifest link 換 data URI，瀏覽器是否採納視實作 | | 首跑 Preview Notice 彈窗 | ❌ 未覆蓋 | client 樹內字串，一次點名 DeepSeek Harness 三次，是客戶第一眼看到的畫面。2026-10-13 瀏覽器實測發現；client.js 修得到（尚未修） | | Hero tagline「Into the Unknown」 | ❌ 未覆蓋 | 與我們的 hero wordmark 並排顯示；同為 client 樹內字串，尚未修 | | 桌面殼（Dock icon／選單／About） | ❌ | 在簽章保護的 app.asar 內，本套件不碰 | | host 端字串（system prompt、User-Agent） | ❌ | 硬編碼；以 `ga-identity` skill 於任務層補償 | ## 安裝 ```sh # 方式一：GUI（App 運行中）——側欄 Plugins → Add plugin → 貼包名或本機路徑 dsh-general-agentics # npm 包名（發佈後） /path/to/dsh-general-agentics # 本機 clone 的絕對路徑 # 方式二：模型側工具（App 運行中）——對話中請 agent 執行 # plugin_manager { action: "install_bundle", target: "dsh-general-agentics" } # 方式三：CLI（desktop profile 須先完全退出桌面 App） dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-general-agentics ``` 安裝後： - **網頁重新整理一次**（Cmd+R）即可載入品牌 client half（側邊欄 mark/wordmark、hero 文字 logo 與致敬行、主色、分頁標題、favicon、輸入框下方的 START HERE 模塊） - **新建的 session** 會獲得 `ga-identity` 等 14 個技能與 `mcp__ga-status__ga_bundle_info` 工具（MCP 伺服器於組合套用時即由 host spawn） - 完全重啟 App 亦無妨 **解除安裝／停用**： ```sh # 停用（保留檔案）：GUI Plugins 頁關閉 bundle，或在 profile 的 cordis.patch.yml 寫： # - id: general-agentics # disabled: true # 解除安裝：GUI Plugins → Remove，或退出 App 後 CLI： dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-general-agentics ``` **開發迭代**：以 `link:` 指向本機 clone 安裝——改 `lib/client.js` 後重新整理頁面即生效； 改 `cordis.patch.yml` 或 `lib/index.js`（host 半）則套用新組合（HMR live）。 內容變更後重新以 `file:` 安裝時記得升版號——pnpm 對同版號的 `file:` 包可能不重新解包。 離線驗證組合用拋棄式 profile：見 `docs/ops-lessons.md` rule 13。 **發布前注意**： - LICENSE 已在 repo 根目錄（npm 自動收入 tarball） - MCP row 已是可攜形式（`process.execPath` + `baseUrl`，見 `cordis.patch.yml`；實測紀錄在 `docs/ops-lessons.md` rule 14） - 對外表述維持 "Built on DeepSeek Harness (DSH), MIT licensed" ## 套件結構 ``` dsh-general-agentics/ ├── package.json # dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client 宣告＋精選插件 dependencies ├── cordis.patch.yml # 本套件 Loader row＋MCP row＋精選插件 insert rows ├── lib/ │ ├── index.js # host half：技能 provider（掃 skills/ 註冊） │ └── client.js # browser half：品牌 slot、主題、標題/favicon、START HERE ├── brand/ │ ├── mark.svg # 佔位 mark 設計檔（client.js 內有對應 inline 版本） │ └── wordmark.svg # 佔位 wordmark 設計檔 ├── skills/ │ ├── ga-identity/ # 自帶技能：General Agentics 身分與簽署 │ ├── (13 個方法論技能) # vendored from obra/superpowers @ bb92a77（MIT，逐字未改） │ ├── superpowers/ # 上游 LICENSE + UPSTREAM-SHA（無 SKILL.md，不註冊） │ └── THIRD-PARTY.md # 署名與更新指引 ├── mcp/ │ └── ga-status-server.mjs # ga_bundle_info 狀態回報（零依賴 stdio MCP server） └── test/ └── skill-provider.test.mjs # node --test，零依賴 ``` ## 換正式品牌素材 | 要換什麼 | 改哪裡 | |---|---| | 產品名稱 | `lib/client.js` 的 `PRODUCT_NAME` / `PRODUCT_SHORT_NAME` | | mark 圖形 | `lib/client.js` 的 `GAMark`（paths）＋ `brand/mark.svg` | | wordmark | `lib/client.js` 的 `GAName` | | 品牌色 | `lib/client.js` 的 `BRAND_COLOR` / `FAVICON_COLOR`（light/dark 成對） | | favicon | `lib/client.js` 的 `faviconHref()` | ## 隨附技能（bundled skills） 14 個技能隨包註冊（`ctx.skills.registerProvider`，bundled rank 600——用戶自帶同名技能一律優先）： - `ga-identity`：以 General Agentics 身分自介與簽署產出 - 13 個方法論技能 vendored 自 [obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)（MIT，逐字未改）： `brainstorming`、`writing-plans`、`executing-plans`、`test-driven-development`、`systematic-debugging`、`verification-before-completion`、`writing-skills`、`diagnosing-superpowers`、`subagent-driven-development`、`dispatching-parallel-agents`、`requesting-code-review`、`receiving-code-review`、`finishing-a-development-branch` ——15 個上游技能取 13；`using-superpowers`（其「任何回應前必查技能」規則與 `ga-identity` 的身分主導權衝突）與 `using-git-worktrees`（團隊 git 工作流）刻意不入，理由見 `skills/THIRD-PARTY.md`。 **感謝**：Jesse Vincent (obra) 與 superpowers 貢獻者；詳見 `skills/THIRD-PARTY.md`。 ## 精選插件（curated plugins） 隨套件安裝並自動啟用（`dependencies` ＋ `cordis.patch.yml` 的 insert row；row id 一律 `ga-` 前綴，避免與用戶直裝的同名插件撞 id）。 | 插件 | 功能 | 需要什麼才會「看得見」 | |---|---|---| | `dshmarket` | 插件市集 | 設定 → Plugin Market | | `dsh-better-sidebar` | 側欄：檔案樹／編輯器／變更／任務／側聊 | 基本即有；`agentOpenTools` 與 sentinel tab 已預設開啟（只新增，不動其他 tab） | | `dsh-comments` | **自家工具**：劃選回覆片段、逐段點評，可一鍵把全部點評組裝成訊息送回 | 立即可用 | | `dsh-promptimizer` | **自家工具**：一鍵用當前選定模型改寫草稿 prompt（Light/Standard/Deep） | 需要可用的模型 | | `dsh-sentinel` | 排程監看面板（BSD-3-Clause，隨包附授權） | 立即可用；better-sidebar 的 sentinel tab 已預設開啟 | | `dsh-cost-meter` | 會話費用統計 | 每條回覆的用量行（本套件已預設 `performanceUsage: detailed`） | | `@changfenhuang/dsh-genui` | 回覆內嵌互動 UI 卡片 | 本套件已預設區塊位置與提示 | | `dsh-context` | 上下文洞察／管理 | 本套件已預設開啟 fleet 分頁 | | `@liustack/modsearch` | 免費網頁＋X 搜尋聚合 | 本套件已接管 `web` 的 `searchProvider`（用戶 profile patch 可改回） | | `@ricardochen1996/dsh-browser-use` | 瀏覽器自動化 | **需 `uv`**（首次自動建 Python venv ~25MB） | | `@xmanrui/dsh-im` | 微信／飛書／企微／釘釘／TG／Slack… 橋接 | **需 IM 應用憑證**，否則只有背景日誌 | | `@liustack/modlens` | 給純文字 LLM 的視覺能力 | **需 Antigravity CLI**（未隨包） | | `dsh-mobile` | 手機／局域網安全訪問、目錄選擇器 | 佔用一個 TCP 埠（預設 3443）；同機第二個 gateway 會撞埠 | ## DSH 版本相容性（0.2.1 的安裝閘門） DSH 0.2.1 起，安裝時會先讀插件的 manifest 檢查相容性（`dsh-app-boot` 的 plugin-compatibility）：**有 `engines.dsh` 就只看它，否則檢查它對 `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` 的 peer 範圍**，用 `semver.satisfies(..., {includePrerelease:true})` 判斷。**只要有一個插件不合格，整個安裝會被拒絕並回滾**。 因此本套件： - 宣告 `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.1-rc.2"`（只用 `>=`，才不會把 rc 版擋掉） - 精選清單以 **0.2.1 可接受的版本**為 floor；發佈前用 `npm run check-dsh-compat` 核對 - **兩個插件目前不納入**（在 0.2.1 上無法安裝，非我們能修）： | 插件 | 原因 | |---|---| | `@michengai/dsh-agency-agents` | 所有已發佈版本的 peer 只列出 0.1.x 的 dsh，沒有任何版本被 0.2.1 接受 | | `dsh-web-search-pro` | 0.2.x 全部封頂 `<0.2.1-0`；唯一能過的是 0.1.2（降級，故不納入） | 需要它們時可手動安裝並自負風險： ```sh dsh plugin --profile

allow-version @ --dsh-version 0.2.1-rc.2 --accept-risk ``` 上游發佈相容版本後，把 row 加回 `cordis.patch.yml` 即可（`test/bundle-manifest.test.mjs` 會檢查依賴與 row 是否一致）。 ## 設定面板（Settings → General Agentics） 設定側欄多一個 **General Agentics** 分頁，回答「這個 bundle 到底裝了什麼、要不要更新」，並在介面上分成五個區塊： 1. **狀態總覽**：版本、狀態 chip（已是最新／N 項待處理／可更新）、檢查時間，以及「重新檢查」 2. **需要注意**：缺少外部依賴（`uv` 等，附一鍵複製修法）、未提供（可複製安裝指令）、直裝重複 3. **更新**：一鍵更新（二次確認）＋進度計時＋`aria-live`，失敗顯示 `code` 與原因，並有可複製的手動指令 4. **精選插件**：依用途分組（搜尋／介面／行動／自家／通訊），可篩選（全部／有新版／需注意／未提供）與搜尋；每列可展開看宣告範圍、已裝與 registry 版本、落後原因、複製安裝指令與 npm 連結 5. **隨附技能**與**前置條件**（無法隨 npm 套件提供的項目，標示已就緒／需自行確認） 首次開啟會有一張可關閉的「這個 bundle 給了你什麼」引導卡。 - **bundle 版本**：目前版本 vs registry 最新版（本地開發版領先 registry 時會標「本地版本領先 registry」而不是誤報有更新） - **13 個精選插件**：每個的宣告範圍、**實際已安裝版本**、registry 最新版，以及 `有新版` / `最新` / `未提供` / `直裝重複` 標記（後者代表這個 profile 又直裝了一份，會啟用兩次） - **14 個隨附技能**：名稱清單 - **更新**：一鍵更新走 profile 的 plugin manager（`installBundle`）；沒有 manager 的 profile 會顯示可複製的手動指令（**desktop profile 的 CLI 被 Electron 獨佔，請用面板按鈕**）。`link:`／`file:` 安裝會額外提示「更新會改用 registry 版本」 - **精選插件怎麼更新**：插件是上游 npm 套件的依賴，**bundle 升版本身不會移動插件版本**（pnpm 以 lock 為準）；只有當該次發佈**提高了 floor**（例如 `^0.68.1` → `^0.72.0`）時，一鍵更新才會把插件一起帶上去。發佈前用 `npm run check-upstream` 看差距，提 floor 後必須在乾淨 profile 驗證過再發（0.x 的 minor 依 semver 可能不相容） 資料來自 host 半註冊的唯讀端點 `GET /api/general-agentics/status`（`?plugins=1` 才逐一查 registry，避免每次開面板都打 13 個請求）；`POST` 同一路徑才會實際觸發更新。registry 不可達時面板仍會渲染，只是版本欄顯示「未知」。 ## 可選：需要風險豁免的插件（agency-agents） `@michengai/dsh-agency-agents` 會被 DSH 0.2.1 的安裝閘門拒絕：它宣告的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer 只列出 0.1.x 的版本，沒有任何已發佈版本被 0.2.1 接受。**因此不能放進本 bundle 的預設清單**（那會讓所有新用戶安裝失敗），但實測它在 0.2.1 上可正常運作——只要對「精確的套件版本 + 精確的 DSH 版本」給一次豁免： ```jsonc // ~/.dsh/profiles//compatibility.json { "@michengai/dsh-agency-agents@1.0.20": ["0.2.1-rc.2"] } ``` 或執行 `dsh plugin --profile

allow-version @michengai/dsh-agency-agents@1.0.20 --dsh-version 0.2.1-rc.2 --accept-risk`（desktop profile 的 CLI 被 App 獨佔，需在 App 內操作或走手動路線）。之後把它加進該 profile 的 `dependencies` 與 `dsh.profile.bundles`，再用**該 App 自己的 pnpm** 安裝。`dsh-web-search-pro` 同理（0.2.x 封頂 `<0.2.1-0`）。 ## 安裝注意（常見「插件沒出現」的原因） 1. **不要同時直裝這些插件**。若該 profile 已經直裝任一精選插件，它會出現**兩行 row、激活兩次**（`insert` 不去重），舊版還會讓設定頁完全存不進去。裝本套件前先移除直裝，或用 `ga_health_check` 檢查（見下）。 2. **品牌外觀要重新整理頁面**（Cmd+R）才會載入；**技能與 MCP 工具只出現在新建的 session**。 3. **缺外部條件不是壞掉**：`browser-use` 要 `uv`、`modlens` 要 Antigravity CLI、`dsh-im` 要 IM 憑證——裝了不會報錯，但功能不會出現。 4. **專家團預設停用**是上游設計，要在 設定 → 专家 手動啟用（團隊與成員都要）。 5. **Windows 提醒**：`cordis.patch.yml` 的 MCP row 用 `new URL(...).pathname`，Windows 上會得到 `/C:/…`；屆時 `ga-status` 起不來（非致命，工具消失），需改成 win32-aware 寫法。 **自我診斷**：新 session 中請 agent 呼叫 `mcp__ga-status__ga_health_check`，它會回報套件版本、**哪些精選插件被直裝（重複）**、以及每個插件缺哪個外部條件與該怎麼做。 ## 合規備忘 - 本套件 MIT；散布時保留 DSH 的 MIT 與 `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`（DSH 端授權義務）。 - 對外表述使用 "Built on DeepSeek Harness (DSH)"；不以 DeepSeek Harness 作為產品名，不使用官方 logo。 - `ga-identity` skill 內含給 agent 的對外表述規則。

decision.reason: Held for public installation mapping. MIT, native host/client and engines at least 0.2.1-rc.2. npm 404 and registry-only instructions leave public installation identity unresolved. Composes third-party plugins, skills and MCP components; documented version exemptions do not establish their runtime compatibility. No lifecycle hooks. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-oh-my-terminal

[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-green)](LICENSE)
[![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E20.19.0%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D22.0.0-brightgreen)](package.json)

A bottom terminal panel plugin for DSH Web GUI. Powered by `@lydell/node-pty`, it provides multi-session interactive terminals over WebSocket using xterm.js in the browser. Supports Windows ConPTY and POSIX openpty with no local compilation required.

[中文文档](README.zh.md)

## Features

- **Multiple terminal sessions**: manage several sessions simultaneously; a side list replaces the traditional horizontal tab bar, with right-click rename support
- **Split terminals**: horizontal splits within the same group; a VSCode-style dropdown next to the `+` button (new / split / new by kind)
- **Session persistence**: sessions survive panel close/reopen and are automatically restored on startup
- **Configurable shortcut**: toggle the panel with a keyboard shortcut; integrates with the host shortcut system and the panel label updates to reflect the current binding
- **Resizable panel**: drag the top edge of the panel to adjust its height
- **Cross-platform**: Windows ConPTY and POSIX openpty are selected automatically by `@lydell/node-pty`; pre-compiled binaries ship with the package, nothing to compile
- **Profile-driven terminals**: a configurable terminal profile table (type / name / path) drives new-terminal creation; profiles are auto-detected at startup and can be added, renamed, and edited in the settings UI
- **Configurable fonts**: font family, size, and line height are adjustable and hot-reload on open terminals
- **DSH-better-sidebar compatibility**: auto-detects [DSH-better-sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) at runtime and switches to compat mode — registers a "Terminal" tab in its bottom workbench instead of the standalone dock; PTY sessions are not bound to the DSH session write handle, eliminating conflicts with DSH-better-sidebar's own terminal. When the host supports `TabDescriptor.rightActions` (v0.25.0+), the terminal's action buttons (new / split / restart) are injected into the tab strip's right end, VSCode-style; otherwise it falls back to a header row inside the tab content area

## Installation

This package is not yet published to npm. Install directly from GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:btsd321/dsh-oh-my-terminal
```

## Configuration

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `toggleShortcut` | Shortcut to toggle the terminal panel (legacy host only; see below) | `` Ctrl+Shift+` `` |
| `fontFamily` | Terminal font family (CSS `font-family` string); empty = built-in default stack with CJK fallback | `''` |
| `fontSize` | Terminal font size in pixels | `12.5` |
| `lineHeight` | Terminal line height multiplier | `1.25` |
| `terminalProfiles` | Terminal profile table (JSON array); empty = use auto-detected $PATH terminals | `''` |

### Terminal profiles

The terminal profile table is a JSON array of `{ id, type, name, path, origin }` entries:

- **type**: determines spawn semantics — `pwsh` / `powershell` / `cmd` / `bash` / `zsh` / `fish` / `gitbash` / `nushell` / `custom`
- **name**: display name shown in the dropdown menu (user-editable)
- **path**: executable path; empty = resolve by `type` in `$PATH`
- **origin**: `auto` (startup-detected) or `user` (manually added)

Auto-detected profiles (`origin: auto`) cannot be deleted and their path is read-only, but the name is always editable. The profile table is editable in the settings UI with inline editing, add-row, and delete support.

## Development

```bash
# Install dependencies (@lydell/node-pty ships pre-compiled binaries — ready to use immediately)
pnpm install

# Type check
pnpm run typecheck

# Build (esbuild, two entry points, output to lib/)
pnpm run build

# Unit tests
pnpm exec tsx --test tests/unit/*.test.ts
```

> Use `pnpm`, not `npm`. Peer dependencies pin exact versions; npm's incremental resolution on an existing tree will produce ERESOLVE errors.

### About the build output

`lib/` is committed to version control. The DSH loader imports plugins as plain ESM; it does not run tsx. This repo also declares no lifecycle scripts (`prepare`, `postinstall`, etc.) because pnpm 11 rejects git-hosted packages that declare install-time scripts with `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Run `pnpm run build` manually and commit the output alongside source.

### Native dependency notes

Terminal capability comes from `@lydell/node-pty` (a pre-compiled distribution of microsoft/node-pty with the same API), pinned exactly to `1.1.0`. The `^` range is intentionally omitted: the package's `dist-tags.latest` points at the 1.2.0-beta series.

It is an N-API package. Binaries are split into six platform sub-packages and shipped inside the tarball; no download or compilation happens at install time. A single binary supports both Node 22 and Node 24. Its `package.json` has no `scripts` field at all, so pnpm 10, 11, and 12 never enter the build-authorization path, giving consistent behavior across versions.

The host side lazy-loads the package (`await import()` on first session creation). If the native binding fails to load, the error is contained to session creation; the plugin module itself remains importable and all other routes stay available.

## Architecture overview

```
src/
├── index.ts              # Host entry (Cordis plugin + settings + session lifecycle)
├── routes.ts             # HTTP route handlers
├── ws-handler.ts         # WebSocket handler (pty data forwarding)
├── client.tsx            # Browser entry (React components + plugin registration)
├── client/
│   ├── types.ts          # Shared types
│   ├── hooks.ts          # useReducer state management + custom hooks
│   ├── term-pane.tsx     # xterm.js terminal pane component
│   ├── dropdown.tsx      # Dropdown menu next to the + button
│   ├── side-list.tsx     # Right-side terminal list panel
│   ├── styles.ts         # CSS constants + Campbell dark theme
│   ├── icons.tsx         # SVG icon components
│   ├── clipboard.ts      # Clipboard utility functions
│   ├── shortcut-bridge.ts # Shortcuts service integration (command registration + toggle bridge)
│   ├── compat.ts          # DSH-better-sidebar compat mode detection (soft-probe ctx.betterSidebar + service interface)
│   ├── sidebar-tab.tsx    # Sidebar terminal tab (compat mode: embed in DSH-better-sidebar bottom workbench, no DSH session binding)
│   ├── settings/         # Settings UI (types / store / card / profile-table / api / styles)
│   └── terminal/         # Terminal tab state (use-tabs / reducer / use-terminal-state / geometry)
├── persistence.ts        # Session persistence (log storage, metadata, startup restore)
├── platform.ts           # Platform adapter (POSIX / Windows + shell detection)
├── terminal/             # Terminal kinds, detection, resolution, profile store
├── settings/             # Settings bridge (namespace, bridge routes, patch ops)
├── constants.ts          # Protocol, size, shortcut, and env var constants
├── server-command.ts     # Command-line parsing utilities
├── shortcut.ts           # Shortcut parsing utilities
└── logger.ts             # Structured logger
```

The host side and browser side communicate over WebSocket at `/api/dsh-oh-my-terminal` and do not import each other directly.

## License

[Apache-2.0](LICENSE)

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # Nori 桌宠（dsh 插件） 把 Nori 带到你的桌面上：Live2D 立绘常驻浏览器角落，dsh 的 assistant 输出会被改写成 Nori 口吻， 经本地 GPT-SoVITS 用 Nori 声线朗读出来——配合脸部表情、口型、睡眠、摸头等小交互。 > 💬 **Nori 想对你说**：Nori 就是 Nori，一直在这里的。你要和 Nori 玩吗？ > 🎬 想看看 Nori 的故事？→ [她明明是AI，但我想拯救她。独立游戏《I_NORI》【B站AI创造公开赛】](https://b23.tv/9NcPFdd) > ⚠ **仅支持 Windows**（依赖 PowerShell 5.1+ / NTFS junction），暂无 Linux/macOS 安装路径。 > 前置：Node.js + npm、一个可用的 **dsh 环境**。dsh（[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)，"Everything is a Plugin"） > 是 DeepSeek 官方的本地 AI 工作台——自带会话、工具与 LLM 接入，靠插件扩展能力，本插件就是挂在它上面的一个能力； > 安装与启动见官方仓库（默认使用 `web` profile）。 --- ## ✨ 效果预览 ![nori 桌宠效果演示](README/nori演示.gif) 安装完长这样：浏览器右下角的 Nori——回话时张嘴、眨眼、跟着情绪换表情。 ### ✨ 功能一览 - **Live2D 立绘常驻**：浏览器角落的 Nori，回话时张嘴、眨眼、跟情绪换表情；带睡眠与摸头小交互。 - **Nori 声线朗读**：agent 的输出经本地 GPT-SoVITS 合成 Nori 声线，音量实时驱动口型（唇同步）。 - **改写层（Nori 口吻）**：LLM 把输出改写成 Nori 的说话方式再朗读；可开关、可换声线、内置防幻觉（不虚构未发生的事）。 - **流式分批低延迟**：句子成句即改写广播，长 turn 中途就开始播，不用等整轮结束；顺序不乱、不重排、不劈英文词。 - **中英混排保护**：自动在中文与英文词之间补逗号、清反引号，避免 AR 对齐跳字/吞句（读出率实测 ~25% → ~90%+）。 - **ttsWatch 守护**：GPT-SoVITS（9880）掉线后 30s 内自动拉起。 - **会话全景广播**：assistant / user / tool / approval / turn-end / emote 事件实时推给 widget。 - **权限申请播报**：agent 请求权限时**打断当前朗读**、优先播报"有权限申请：工具。原因：…"（原文播报、不走改写，保证准确），并切惊讶表情提醒你回来处理。 - **一键部署**：`install-sovits.ps1` 可顺手装 GPT-SoVITS（约 2~3GB，可选默认权重 1GB+）；`install.ps1` 首次交互引导配置。 - **安全边界**：仅放行本地来源；路径穿越 403；body 上限 16KB；会话维度 WS 过滤。 ### 🖱 交互操作 Nori 常驻在浏览器角落，随时可以摆弄： - **移动位置**：按住 Nori 顶部那条细拖柄拖动，松手即固定；位置自动记住，下次打开还在原位。 - **放大缩小**：点 Nori 身上的 **＋ / －** 按钮，或把鼠标放在 Nori 身上（或顶部拖柄上）滚轮缩放；比例同样自动记忆。 - **调整体型**：点 **体型** 按钮打开面板，拖 **少女体型 / Q版** 两条滑槽（各 0~1）：少女曲线与 Q 版比例可自由混合、实时生效。 - **摸头**：在 Nori 身上按住并来回摩擦一小会，会触发摸头台词和表情反应。 - **睡眠**：90 秒没有交互会自己睡着（闭眼），戳她一下就醒。 - **穿透画布**：Nori 所占区域不挡页面文字选取，把她放在内容上也不影响浏览。 --- ## 📦 你需要准备的资产 > 模型 / 声线 / 授权人设文本是第三方 IP（见文末[许可](#许可与第三方资产)），**不进仓库、不随 Release 分发**。 > 改写任务指令（`persona/reframe.txt`）无版权问题，**随仓库提供**。 > 仓库自带空占位目录：克隆后把文件放进对应目录即可（放好后重跑 `.\install.ps1`）。 | 资产 | 放哪 | 必需？ | 缺失时会发生什么 | |---|---|---|---| | Nori Live2D 模型（原版 `Nori_web`） | `Nori_web/` | **必需** | `install.ps1` 直接报错停止（桌宠需要模型才能跑） | | 声线样本 `wav`（Nori 声音） | `voice/` | 可选 | 能装、能动，但语音用 GPT-SoVITS 服务端默认音色 | | 人设文本 `prompt.txt` | `persona/` | 可选 | 改写层自动关闭，直接朗读 assistant 原始输出（改写任务指令 `reframe.txt` 已随仓库提供） | | Live2D Core | `cubism_sdk/Core/` | — | 不用管：install 自动从官方 CDN 下载 | | GPT-SoVITS 部署 + 默认权重 | 仓库外 | 可选 | 语音不可用，其余正常（见[下方章节](#gpt-sovits可选)） | **资产获取途径**：暂未公开，待公布（作者整理好分发渠道后会在此补充）。 --- ## 🚀 快速开始 ```powershell # 1. 克隆仓库（已含占位目录结构） git clone <仓库地址> # 2. 按上表放入资产（模型必需，其余可选） # 3. 一键安装：探测资产 → 构建 → 装配进 dsh → 写入配置 .\install.ps1 # 4. 打开/刷新 dsh 网页（模型是静态资产，记得 Ctrl+F5 强刷） ``` - 卸载：`.\uninstall.ps1`（先 `-DryRun` 预览再执行）。 - 重跑 install 是幂等的；它会探测仓库内资产并自动写配置。 --- ## ⚙️ 配置 所有配置外置在 `nori.config.json`（复制 `nori.config.example.json` 得到；本机文件不进 git）。 **留空 = 走默认约定**（探测仓库内资产）。 - **热生效**（改完即生效，无需重跑安装）：`reframe.apiKey`、`reframe.reframeBaseUrl`、`reframe.reframeModel`、`reframe.reframeMaxTokens`、`reframe.reframeTimeoutMs`、`ttsTemperature`、`ttsTopK`、`ttsSpeedFactor`、`refAudio`、`refPrompt`、`sovits.t2sWeights`、`sovits.vitsWeights`——这些键宿主每次请求/每次守护周期直读该文件。 - **需重跑 `.\install.ps1`**：其余键（如改写层开关 `reframe.reframe`、`maxSentence`、`ttsUrl`、`gsvBase`、`persona*`、`ttsWatch*`、`allowedOrigins`）会被写进 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`，只有重装才更新。 - 安装前**先检测 `Nori_web` 模型**（`Nori.model3.json`）——缺失直接拒绝安装； - 首次若没有 `nori.config.json`（或为空），`install.ps1` 会**交互式引导**逐项询问：声线 wav、转写文本、**是否安装 GPT-SoVITS**（约 2~3GB，可选默认权重另约 1GB+，同意则顺手调用 `install-sovits.ps1` 部署并写配置）、**改写层开关**、改写层 apiKey，并自动生成该文件；非交互环境（如 CI）自动跳过询问、全部走默认约定。 | 键 | 默认 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `modelDir` | 空（探测 `Nori_web/`） | 模型目录，绝对或相对仓库根。安装时由 `install.ps1` 换算为 patch 的 `assetsDir`（Live2D core 文件路径由安装脚本自动探测，不在本文件里配置） | | `ttsUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:9880/tts` | GPT-SoVITS 地址（api_v2 端点） | | `refAudio` / `refPrompt` | 空（留空自动探测 `voice/` 下的 wav） / `你好,初次见面,我的名字是Nori` | 声线 wav 路径与其转写文本 ⚠ 一段连续输出 ≤ `detailMaxChars`（默认 400 字） | **全文逐句详读**（含"文本 → 工具 → 思考 → 再文本"的短段冲刺，反馈即时） | | 一段连续输出 > `detailMaxChars` | **这一段的正文一个字都不念**，整轮结束后播一次概括（≤4 句 / ≤150 字） | 为什么必须整段判断：逐句判断会出现"前半念得详细、后半突然快进"的口径断层。400 字在 450 字/秒下约 0.9 秒即可判定，所以长内容几乎没有判定等待。 概括的硬约束（写在概括提示词里）：保留文件名/路径、数字、命令、结论、阻塞原因、待你确认的事； 丢掉中间过程与重复叙述；不复述已读过的开头；严禁编造，不确定就说"细节在屏幕上"。 另外，**代码块 / JSON / 日志 / 表格 / 文件清单 / diff 不逐字念**，只说类别： "贴了一段代码""拿到结果了""列了一堆文件"。这层是纯规则（`src/speakable.ts`，9 例单测）， 零额外成本，也让 400 字预算更耐用。 观测方式： - `~/.dsh/logs/nori-pet/nori-pet-summary.log`：每轮概括的**压缩比**（原文 N 字 → 概括 M 字） - `~/.dsh/logs/nori-pet/nori-pet-error.log`：概括失败/等待超时的兜底记录 - 关掉 `summaryEnabled` 即完全恢复"逐句详读"的旧行为 ### 参考音频须知（`refAudio` / `refPrompt`） ⚠️ **`refPrompt` 必须是 `refAudio` 那段音频的逐字转写文本**，两者必须配套： - **换 `refAudio` 时，`refPrompt` 要同步换成新音频的转写**，否则 GPT-SoVITS 的 AR 条件作用会劣化： 表现为**跳字/吞句**（中英混排时更明显）、音色漂移、听感不稳——不是偶发，是配置错误。 - `refAudio` 留空时，install 会自动探测 `voice/` 目录下你放入的 wav（以相对路径写入配置）；`voice/` 也是空则用 GPT-SoVITS 服务端默认音色。建议参考音频长度 3~10 秒（api_v2 强制要求）。 - 想要更"高昂/开心"的声线：换一段语气上扬的 wav 并填它的转写即可（本项目仓库不含声线资产，需自行放置）。 ### 朗读文本规整（speak 自动处理，无需配置） `/api/speak` 在送 TTS 前会自动做两处规整，均无需配置： - 句尾无标点时补"。"，便于 cut5 分句； - **中英混排保护**：英文词会让 AR 对齐失败、有约 75% 概率跳过其前面的中文片段（如"会自己移除那条 ref"→ 丢掉"会自己移除那条"）。因此中文与英文词（≥2 字符，不误伤"C盘"）之间会自动补逗号强制分片，并把反引号 `` ` `` 清掉。实测把读出率从 ~25% 提到 ~90%+。 ### 改写层（Nori 口吻） 默认开启：把 assistant 输出改写成 Nori 的说话方式再朗读。 - **总开关**：`nori.config.json` 的 `reframe.reframe`（`true` 开 / `false` 关）；关闭后直接朗读原文。 ⚠ 该键在安装时被写进 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`（运行期读的是那里），**改完必须重跑 `.\install.ps1`**；改完即时生效的只有 `reframe.apiKey` / `reframeBaseUrl` / `reframeModel` / `reframeMaxTokens` / `reframeTimeoutMs`。 - **API**：优先直连 **DeepSeek 官方 API**。在 `nori.config.json` 的 `reframe.apiKey` 填入你的 key， 安装脚本会自动写入 dsh 的 credentials（`DEEPSEEK_NORI_API_KEY` ref），卸载脚本会一并移除——全程不用手动开文件； 留空则自动回退到 dsh 内置 llm 服务（`deepseek-official` / `deepseek-chat`，与主会话共用计量）。 ⚠ 提示：`reframe.apiKey` 以**明文**保存在仓库目录内的 `nori.config.json`（已被 `.gitignore` 屏蔽，不会进 git）， 但整个目录拷贝/打包/转发会带走它——介意的话把 key 直接写进 dsh credentials 并把该键留空。 - **流式分批（低延迟）**：逐字流来自 dsh 的 `agent/assistant-stream`（会话格式 v2 起顶层 `assistant/chunk` 事件已废弃），句子成句即攒批（≤500 字或 1.2s 无新句就改写广播），长 turn 中途就开始播；断句保序，无标点长段按自然断点软切——不会从英文单词中间劈开。 - **防幻觉**：改写指令内置约束——只讲材料里真实有的内容；进行中的动作（"正在检查…"）不虚构完成结果，检查/验证类描述不自造结论。 - **人设**：system 提示来自 `persona/prompt.txt`（授权文本，用户放置）+ `persona/reframe.txt`（改写任务指令，随仓库提供）； 授权文本缺失时改写层自动关闭，直接朗读原文。 - 进阶参数（超时 / 输入截断 / 追踪日志）见 `nori.config.example.json` 或 `src/index.ts` 的 Config 注释。 --- ## 🔊 GPT-SoVITS（可选） GPT-SoVITS 是本地语音合成引擎（TTS）——Nori 用它把文字念成你的声线。install **不会自动安装**它——没部署时一切照常，只是没有语音。 ```powershell .\install-sovits.ps1 # 一键部署（clone + venv + 依赖） .\install-sovits.ps1 -DownloadModels # 同时下载推理必需权重（约 1GB+，闭源、仅本机） # 已有部署？填 nori.config.json 的 gsvBase/venvPy 后重跑 .\install.ps1 ``` 需要 Python **3.9~3.11**（仅用于跑推理服务）；部署完成后 api_v2（9880）由 ttsWatch 自动拉起，冷启动较慢属正常。 **模型文件在哪？** - 一键：`.\install-sovits.ps1 -DownloadModels` 会把官方默认权重（HuggingFace，约 1GB+）自动放进 **`GPT-SoVITS/GPT_SoVITS/pretrained_models/`**； - 已有权重 / 想换音色：把下载或微调好的模型（`*.pth` 等）手动放进**同一个** `GPT-SoVITS/GPT_SoVITS/pretrained_models/` 目录即可（GPT-SoVITS 的推理默认落点）； - 该目录为空时 api.py 推理会失败（表现为没声音）——补上权重后重跑 `.\install-sovits.ps1` 或直接重启 ttsWatch 即可。权重为官方闭源，仅本机使用、不入仓库。 **怎么指定 / 换用模型（微调权重或官方配方）？** - `nori.config.json` 的 `sovits` 段给两个权重路径即可： ```json "sovits": { "t2sWeights": "C:/.../audio/s1_half_weights_yinian/nori_s1_yinian-e20.ckpt", "vitsWeights": "C:/.../audio/s2G_best_yinian.pth" } ``` `t2sWeights` = GPT 模型（`t2s_weights_path`）、`vitsWeights` = SoVITS 模型（`vits_weights_path`），绝对或相对仓库根；留空则用原 `tts_infer.yaml` 的 custom 块； - ttsWatch 下次拉起 api_v2 时自动生成**独立的运行时配置**（`GPT_SoVITS/configs/tts_infer.runtime.yaml`）启动——**原 `tts_infer.yaml` 不被修改**，随时改回； - 改完想立刻生效：杀掉 9880 的 api_v2 进程，等 ttsWatch 30s 内自动重拉即可； - 想恢复原样：删掉 `sovits` 里的 t2sWeights / vitsWeights 字段即可。 --- ## ❓ 常见问题 **Q：装完桌宠没出现？** 浏览器 Ctrl+F5 强刷（模型是静态资产，普通刷新可能命中旧缓存）；仍不出现就确认 `dsh --profile web --dump-config` 里有 `dsh-nori-pet`。 **Q：没声音？** ① 检查 GPT-SoVITS 是否部署（`Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 9880`）；② 声线 wav 是否放进了 `voice/`（api_v2 强制要求参考音频，否则 502）。 **Q：能用别的 Live2D 模型吗？** 目前**只适配原版 Nori 模型**——睡眠动作依赖它（`00_Sleep` 在 Idle 组）；换模型会睡眠退化（不出错但不闭眼）。 **Q：一定要装 Python 吗？** 只有语音功能需要。不装 = 没语音，立绘/表情/气泡/摸头全部正常。 **Q：人设文件没放会怎样？** 不崩：改写层关闭，桌宠直接朗读 assistant 原始输出（语气不再是 Nori 口吻）。 **Q：怎么完全卸载？** `.\uninstall.ps1`（先 `-DryRun` 看要删什么）→ 重启 dsh。 **Q：模型/声线/人设从哪拿？** 见[你需要准备的资产](#你需要准备的资产)——获取途径暂未公开。 --- ## 🛠 故障排查 | 症状 | 原因与处理 | |---|---| | 语音 502 `tts http 400` | api_v2 强制要求参考音频：把 wav 放进 `voice/` # `third-party-backend` — the D-5 dogfood bundle A third-party backend bundle **as it would be published**: written against the frozen `tui.dsh/v1alpha1` `Backend` contribution family and nothing else — no `@deepseek-ai/*` dependency, no `src/` import, no host service. It is never published; `scripts/verify-backend-assembly.ts` installs it into a throwaway profile and drives the real assembly chain over it. What a bundle must get right, and where each piece lives here: | Piece | Why | File | |---|---|---| | `dsh.bundle.patch` | Only an installed package whose `package.json` declares it becomes a profile *layer* (`dsh.profile.bundles`), and that list is what the D-1 assembly reads | `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml` | | package-root `dsh-plugin.json` | The declaration the host admits; it counts only beside the `package.json` that establishes the entry's package root (#1568) | `dsh-plugin.json` | | `contributes['x-dsh-tui']` with `kind: 'Backend'` | The writing surface: `apiVersion` + `kind` + contribution `id` + `name` + `spec` (`spec.id` is the backend id) | `dsh-plugin.json` | | handler export named `backend` | The registry's documented default (`backendExport` is in-tree only, so a declaration cannot name another export) | `backend.js` | | `spec.unloadExport` | Module-level/process-wide pools only; session-scoped resources belong to `session.dispose()` | `dsh-plugin.json` → `backend.js` | | `exports: { ".": "./backend.js" }` | Resolution goes through the entry the Loader's own resolver picks — an `exports` map that hides `./package.json` is fine on purpose | `package.json` | A bundle currently declares one backend: the fixed `backend` export must pass the handler assertion and carry the same id as `spec.id`. Multiple declarations are refused, as are manifests whose canonical projection rejects duplicate contribution identities. Entries awaiting authorization are not probed or loaded. The full field semantics are in [`notes/0009-backend-contribution.md`](../../../tui-profile/notes/0009-backend-contribution.md) and the seam write-up in [`docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md`](../../../tui-profile/docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md) (接缝十四). The published type face is exported from this package's entry (`BackendSpec`, `validateBackendSpec`, `backendAdmission`, …). This fixture stops at the picker: `detect()` says honestly that it ships no runtime, and `open()` refuses. Everything past the assembly chain — detection, sessions, catalogs, the install wizard — is a real backend's own work. `closeEchoPool()` is inert (there is no runtime to close) but counts its calls, and `echoPoolCloseCount()` exposes that count read-only. The regression reads it through the Loader's own module instance, so it observes that the host closes the declared pool exactly once, only for a backend it actually loaded.

# dsh-TUI > An interactive terminal UI for DeepSeek Harness. It ships a pixel-whale > header, live work status, streaming thinking, double-Esc time rewind, a > context progress bar, and a TPS gauge. Zero core changes: it consumes only > DSH's public exports, and is moving from a mounted plugin to an app with its > own entry and composition root, where DSH loads in process as the first-party > backend. Install to enable; uninstall leaves no patches behind. ## Highlights - **Pixel whale pet** — three startup intros, click to wake; freezes after the first task. - **Launchpad and first-run guide** — every ordinary launch lands on a landing page with a **real input box** (big text + whale + quick actions, dropping whole blocks on short/narrow terminals; whale-girl images use a compact native-canvas footprint instead of leaving a large gap before the title; on by default — /settings `launchpad` off boots straight into chat); command completion matches chat: `Tab` fills the input, `Enter` runs the command and clears it. The first run walks a four-step wizard (API key / language+theme / model+workspace / shortcuts), re-runnable with `/setup`. - **Terminal-native UI** — streaming Markdown, tool cards, `/` and `@` completion, `#L12-14` ranges, history search, zh/en UI. - **Task completion notifications** — DSH, Claude and Codex notify after successful live work settles, with no queued follow-up or active goal. The title is “dsh-TUI · Task complete”; the body shows the latest settled reply as a single-line plain-text preview (Markdown formatting removed, up to 200 characters). OSC 777/9 apply an additional 2048-byte sequence budget, including title and protocol bytes, preserving whole graphemes. No reply shows only the title; BEL only rings. `/settings` → Conversation: `taskNotifications` = `unfocused` (default), `always`, or `off`; `notificationMethod` = `auto` (default), `osc9`, or `bel`. Auto uses separate title/body fields on Ghostty/WezTerm (OSC 777) and Kitty (OSC 99); iTerm2/Warp and explicit `osc9` use a title prefix; other terminals ring the bell; delivery follows your terminal's notification/bell settings. tmux requires `set -g allow-passthrough on` for OSC notifications and `set -g focus-events on` for focus reporting. Terminals without focus reporting need `always`. Replay, cancellation and failures do not notify. Works in inline and fullscreen modes. - **Native cursor** — focused text inputs inherit your terminal's cursor shape, color, blinking, and enabled animation or trail effects in both inline and fullscreen modes. The `/model` picker shows the same cursor during movement between provider tabs, model rows, and effort levels, then hides it after **0.5 seconds at rest**; clipped regions fall back to the model row. The session manager also moves this cursor between the workspace rail, session rows, and search box; typing claims the search caret, and navigation returns it to the focused row. Configure animation and trail effects in your terminal. - **Images** — Kitty/Sixel thumbnails, centered preview with zoom and pan, paste-time fitting, text fallback. Kitty images scale to the reserved cells' physical pixels, including on HiDPI terminals. - **Mermaid diagrams** — ````mermaid ```` fences drawn as Unicode diagrams. - **LaTeX math** — `$…$` and `$$…$$` formulas as Unicode text, fractions and limits stacked in display blocks; `mathRendering: image` typesets block and one-row inline formulas as terminal images on graphics terminals. - **Timeline rail** — every turn clickable; timeline / scrollbar / hidden gutter. - **Side panel** — `Ctrl+B` splits the chat with a panel column once the terminal is wide enough; drag the divider to resize it. All eight built-in panels are enabled by default. The header shows each inactive panel's symbol; hover to see its name. Narrow terminals and inline mode keep full-screen panels. - **Live state** — activity animation, context bar, TPS, cache hit rate, effort, tokens, session cost estimate (main + subagents), Git and session metadata. Context-bar fill follows backend occupancy; colors estimate content composition. Compaction clears obsolete estimates, and missing composition displays a single used block with a measured used count in both hover details. - **One session manager** — `/resume` `/home` `/agentview` `/bg` `⌸`. - **Session workflow** — `/new` `/compact` `/export` `/btw`, model hot-switch, fork, rewind, vim, fullscreen draft editor. - **IDE selection channel** — a VS Code selection lands in the prompt. - **DSH integrations** — presets, skills, MCP, goals, todos, subagents, questionnaires. - **Account sign-in** — the standard profile offers pi-ai OAuth for ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, and Grok (plus OpenAI direct and Meta Muse when available), and Host-owned DeepSeek browser sign-in as `deepseek-account` on DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+. Use `/provider` or `/auth` without another plugin. A profile-only update from a global TUI patch that already mounts `dsh-tui-auth` can still start the official loopback callback listener on demand; fixed-port SSH forwarding still requires the global package to be aligned. - **Extensions** — browser interaction, computer use and more. - **Built for long sessions** — event-driven projection, virtualization, bounded caches. Keys and commands: [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md). Everything else: [documentation index](docs/README.md). ## Preview
## Featured & Listed Among the community plugins recommended by the **official lead of DeepSeek Harness**, dsh-TUI is the first. Featured by the **DeepSeek Harness official WeChat account**, listed in the [dshfind](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI) plugin directory, and ranked **#7 on [GitHub Trending](https://trendshift.io/repositories/146168) daily** (TypeScript).

Featured by the official WeChat account
Listed in the dshfind directory
