evidence.readmeExcerpt: # 回答の日本語訳を表示し、履歴に反映する Issue #448（Step 1 + Step 2）。規模: 中（既存のDSHコマンドとWeb UIスロットをつなぐプラグイン）。 DSHが所有する会話・モデル実行のホストアダプターとして実装し、独自のエージェントループは追加しません。 完了した英語・中国語の回答のアクション行には、2つの明示的な操作があります。 1. 「日本語訳を表示」（Step 1）: 現在の会話で直近に使ったprovider/modelへ独立した翻訳リクエストを1回送り、 訳文ダイアログを開きます。原文、会話のsurface、次のモデル入力は変更しません。 2. 「日本語訳で置き換える」（Step 2）: 同じ翻訳リクエストを1回送り、対象回答のsurfaceノードを訳文で置き換えます。 新しいターンや追加指示のuserメッセージは追加せず、次のリクエストの`deriveMessages()`は元の回答ではなく訳文を読み込みます。 自動翻訳は行いません。どちらもクリックしたときのみ動作します。 生成中の表示、二重クリックの防止、失敗時の再試行に対応しています。 日本語のみ、コードのみ、または中断された回答にはボタンを表示しません。 かな比率による判定を行うため、日本語の漢字のみの文章などを誤判定する場合があります。 置換はDSHの`surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', startSeq, endSeq }`（`/compact`と同じ経路）で行います。 元の回答は追記専用のsession logと人間向けのtranscriptに残り、置換ノードは`source.kind: 'rdsh-translation'`を持ちます。 DSHが置換をモデル可視のsurfaceだけに適用する設計のため、画面上の回答表示そのものは差し替わりません （訳文はダイアログで確認できます）。画面表示の差し替えには、DSH側に置換を反映する表示APIが必要です。 ターン外のコマンドから追加できる置換は、開いているstepを要求しない`user/message`のみであるため、 モデルからは訳文がuserロールとして見えます（`assistant/message`での置換には開いているstepが必要です）。 DSHの通常の`command/run`・`command/done`ログには、操作と結果が記録されます。 置換後は`request/header`が再発行され、置換ノード以降のプロバイダーキャッシュの再利用が一度無効になります。 置換済みの回答や、`/compact`で隠れた回答への再置換に対しては、暗黙的に無視することなくエラーを表示します。 訳文表示と「置換済み」の表示はコンポーネントの一時的な状態であり、画面を再読み込みすると消えます（履歴の置換は残ります）。 自動翻訳、モデルの切り替え、翻訳結果の個別保存、置換ノードへのLike/Dislikeは対象外です。 ## 導入と操作 リポジトリの`plugins/install.sh`では、`PROFILE=web`または`PROFILE=desktop`を指定して導入します。 除外する場合は`TRANSLATION=0`を指定します。headless/TUIでは既定で導入されません。 個別に導入する場合は、Webプロファイルでは`dsh plugin --profile web add /絶対パス/plugins/rdsh-translation`、 Desktopでは`rdsh desktop install --package /絶対パス/plugins/rdsh-translation`を使用します。 導入後に対象のWeb UIを開き直してください。 `$DSH_HOME/rdsh.json`の`translation.kana_threshold`で表示のしきい値を設定できます。 既定値は0.08、許容範囲は0.01〜0.5です。変更後は画面を再読み込みしてください。 翻訳の呼び出しには、現在のモデルの通常の利用料金および利用枠がかかります。 表示文言、コマンドの説明、エラーメッセージは表示言語に追従します。Web UIはDSHのlocaleカタログ （`rdsh-translation`名前空間のen/zh/ja辞書）を使用します。日本語の言語定義はrdsh-settingsが 所有するため、このプラグインからは言語を追加しません。ホスト側の文言は`RDSH_LANG`、 `rdsh.json`の`general.language`、OSロケールの順で解決されます。プラグイン一覧の タイトル・説明には`locale/en.json`、`locale/ja.json`、`locale/zh.json`を使用します。 コードブロック、インラインコード、識別子・パスなどは保護トークンで保持します。 トークンの欠落や重複、空応答、途中終了、64KiBを超える入力/出力はエラーとして表示します。 60秒のタイムアウトとDSHの保守処理による排他制御を利用し、生成中の会話は変更しません。 ## 検証 `node --test tests/translation-preview.test.mjs`の実行により、表示ボタンからダイアログまでの動作、原文とsessionの不変性、 二重起動の防止、失敗・取り消し・上限の処理、導入リストの確認に加え、置換ボタンが`user/message`＋`surfaceOp: replace`を 対象seqへ1件だけ追記すること、`source.kind`と`sourceEventSeqs`の形式、表示操作が履歴を変更しないこと、 busy・対象なし・保護トークン欠落・session拒否時に追記しないこと、置換済みに対する専用エラーの発生を確認します。 同じテストはCIの既存プラグイン検証エントリーからも読み込まれます。 実providerを使った翻訳の品質や実DSH全体での受け入れは、合成境界での成功とは区別します。 隔離したDSHを用意した場合は、次のコマンドで実際のAgentLoop、LLM、CommandRuntime、実sessionと、 `dsh-session`/`dsh-compaction`の実invariant companionとの境界を確認できます。 providerのみが固定応答を返し、モデルAPIは呼び出しません。invariantの負の対照（開いていないturnの`turn/end`）が `InvariantError`で拒否されることを確かめてから、置換が通ることを検証します。 ```sh RDSH_NATIVE_MODULES=/path/to/dsh/node_modules npm run test:translation --prefix tests/e2e ``` 画面確認とは別の試験です。実行方法は[受入試験](../../tests/e2e/README.md)を参照してください。 実Webプロファイルでの操作前後のPNG・操作GIFと検証範囲については、 [画面の受入記録](../../docs/evidence/issue448-translation-preview/README.md)を参照してください。 # rdsh — a fast, safe Rust launcher for `dsh` [![ci](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![dashboard](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml) [![docs](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rdsh.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rdsh) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [日本語](README.ja.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) An independent community project; not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness project. `rdsh` is a fast, safe launcher for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond process launch**: `rdsh --version` starts in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak RSS, versus ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh --version`. This is process launch only: a booted agent profile still runs upstream Node.js, so conversation startup and session memory match upstream. See [Benchmarks](#benchmarks). - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` Or install the crate from crates.io (needs Rust 1.85+): ```sh cargo install rdsh ``` `cargo install` builds from source and installs the same binary as the release archives. Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL users can also install the release [`.deb`/`.rpm`](#native-packages-deb--rpm) with `apt`/`dnf`. ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Native Packages (`.deb` / `.rpm`) Linux x86_64 users on Debian/Ubuntu (and WSL) or Fedora/RHEL can install the same release binary with the OS package manager. Download the `.deb` or `.rpm` from the [latest release](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest) and install that file directly; no extra repository is configured. ```sh sudo apt install ./rdsh__amd64.deb # Debian, Ubuntu, WSL sudo dnf install ./rdsh--1.x86_64.rpm # Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux ``` `` is the release tag without its leading `v` (`0.6.0` for `v0.6.0`). The package installs `/usr/bin/rdsh` together with the licence and README, so `rdsh --version` works right after installation: no Rust toolchain, no `install.sh`. Like `rdsh-linux-x64.tar.gz`, both packages carry the glibc build, so the musl archive and `install.sh` stay the fallback for older distributions. ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ### Package Managers (Homebrew / Scoop / winget) Advanced users on macOS and Windows can let a package manager own the installed `rdsh` binary. The manifests in [packaging/](packaging/README.md) pin the exact release archives and their SHA-256 values; [docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md](docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md) lists the install commands and the update procedure. **macOS (Homebrew)** — installs the Apple Silicon or Intel archive: ```sh brew install --formula ./packaging/homebrew/rdsh.rb ``` **Windows (Scoop)**: ```powershell scoop install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/main/packaging/scoop/rdsh.json ``` **Windows (winget)** — winget 1.6 or newer reads the three manifests directly; submitting them to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` stays a manual step: ```powershell winget install --manifest .\packaging\winget ``` These channels track one release at a time, so a new tag is not served until `python3 scripts/update-packaging-manifests.py --version vX.Y.Z` refreshes them. ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. To invalidate the credential itself, revoke the OAuth grant or rotate the API key at its provider. That may also disconnect the source CLI. This controls rdsh copying, not DSH's own refreshes, inherited environment access or an OS sandbox. **Migration:** existing DSH credentials are retained. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=0 disables automatic imports while keeping the selection; an explicit auth --import still works. Invalid/unreadable policies fail closed instead of falling back to legacy sync. Consent changes and rdsh credential writes share a lock, so a completed unselect cannot be bypassed by a queued rdsh import using an earlier policy. After a crashed writer, check that no rdsh auth/setup writer is active before removing $DSH_HOME/.rdsh-auth-sharing.lock; the launcher skips copying while it is locked. setup --web issues a new local access key at startup in its #key=... URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features and the privacy-sensitive switches (`discord`, `telemetry`) stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast, telemetry-free dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | Needs SearXNG. | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Anything a provider changes afterwards is absent from the picker until that dependency is upgraded — and a profile that lists `models:` explicitly replaces the bundled catalog for the route anyway. `rdsh models` reads the provider's own catalog (the local Codex CLI, or Kimi Code's `/v1/models` endpoint with the profile's API key) and folds it into the profile: ```sh rdsh models # read-only: missing ids and stale names rdsh models --provider kimi-coding # one provider only rdsh models sync # add missing entries, refresh stale names rdsh models sync --profile web --dry-run # preview one profile ``` Nothing is deleted, an existing entry keeps every other byte (a name the provider's current one already contains is left as written), and a profile the command does not recognize is refused instead of rewritten. The harness picks the changes up on the next config reload or restart. ### Agent Tool Isolation Delegated agent tools keep normal file access by default: the model reads and writes the project like any other tool. `--share-file` isolates **`rdsh_inspect` only**. On Linux (with bubblewrap and prlimit) that tool sees just the files you explicitly share: ```sh rdsh --share-file README.md --share-file src/main.rs --profile tui ``` From `rdsh_inspect`, only the shared files are mounted read-only, host files stay out of reach and the sandbox has no network. Turn the same boundary on for every run with `rdsh features on agent_tool_sandbox` (off again with `rdsh features off agent_tool_sandbox`, or force it with `RDSH_SECURITY=1`). Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals. Startup prints `[rdsh security] rdsh_inspect is isolated; other DSH tools use upstream permissions`. ### Hook Guard (`rdsh guard`) Integrates with DSH `hooks.json` to inspect and block dangerous commands before execution: ```sh echo "$input" | rdsh guard --deny "rm -rf /*" --deny "*token*" ``` For an opt-in structured check of supported file tools, pass a policy file. This example permits `Read` only under one existing project directory: ```json { "schema": 1, "rules": [ { "id": "project-read", "tool": "Read", "access": "read", "roots": ["/absolute/project/path"] } ] } ``` ```sh echo "$hook_json" | rdsh guard --policy-file ./hook-policy.json --json ``` The structured classifier supports the `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` file-path schemas. It canonicalizes the working directory and target, checks the selected tool and read/write scope against existing policy roots, and reports `allow`, `deny`, or `unknown` with a non-sensitive reason. In JSON mode an `allow` is classification only and omits `decision`; the host still owns permission and approval. Unknown tools, shell commands, malformed input, and unsupported tool arguments fail closed. Shell parsing and network destinations are not implemented. Path checks are advisory and can race with later filesystem changes; this hook is not an OS sandbox. Use the actual execution sandbox for enforcement. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "rdsh guard --deny \"rm -rf /*\"" }] } ] } } ``` ### Context Injection (`rdsh context`) `rdsh context inject` assembles this turn's context — goal, constraints, decisions, working set, git state, retrieved code, and curated memory — and emits it in the DSH `UserPromptSubmit` hook contract, so the model sees it without any copy-paste: ```sh rdsh features on context_engine # the engine is opt-in rdsh context hook install # merges $DSH_HOME/hooks.json (idempotent) rdsh context hook status --json ``` The hook is fail-open: it never blocks a prompt and always exits 0. Only an unreadable settings document or an unparseable payload inject nothing at all; a corrupt index or a missed deadline drops just what depends on them — the graph or the code search — and still injects goal, constraints, and memory. Injection has its own budget (`context.inject_budget`, default 1200 tokens) and deadline (`context.inject_deadline_ms`, default 1200 ms); once the deadline passes the code search is skipped and only memory, goal, and constraints go out. Memory holds curated items, not a transcript dump: ```sh rdsh context remember "Keep the API compatible" --kind constraint rdsh context distill --session ~/.dsh/sessions///session.v4.jsonl.zstd --apply rdsh context memory --json # active and superseded entries rdsh context forget mem_ab12cd34ef56 ``` `distill` reads user turns only (zstd session logs included) and extracts decisions, constraints, and retractions with deterministic markers, superseding an older overlapping entry instead of guessing. `rdsh context build --require-stable` exits 3 unless the snapshot is provably stable: a file or git state that changed during assembly counts, and so does a git state it cannot read, so a stale or unknown snapshot is never reported as fresh. ### Dependency Graph and Change Impact (`rdsh deps`) ```sh rdsh deps build # incremental index under $DSH_HOME/rdsh-index rdsh deps query engine_score # where a symbol is defined and referenced rdsh deps impact src/context.rs # direct/transitive dependents + affected tests ``` The extractor covers Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Go and records imports, definitions, and static call sites per file. Unchanged files (same size and mtime) are reused, so repeated runs stay fast. It is a static approximation: dynamic dispatch, indirect calls, macros, and generated code remain explicitly `unknown` and are reported as unresolved counts rather than guessed, and a missing index means "no information", never "no dependencies". When the index exists, `rdsh context build` and `rdsh context inject` also pull in the graph neighbours of the files their search matched, so a retrieved excerpt arrives with the files it actually depends on. Native execution overhead is ~1 ms per invocation. ## Low-end hosts Default profile: `RDSH_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, then `general.default_profile` in rdsh settings, then local `tui`, else a guided error. Set the saved default with `rdsh settings set general.default_profile web`; an explicit `--profile ` keeps its precedence. rdsh aims to remain useful on modest machines: older x86-64 CPUs, older Linux distributions, and hosts without Node.js installed. - **Faster Node startup.** When rdsh launches dsh, it sets `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to `~/.cache/rdsh-node-compile-cache`, letting Node reuse compiled code across launches (Node 22.1 or newer; older versions ignore it). An existing `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` value is preserved. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=0`, or use `--passthrough` / `RDSH_PASSTHROUGH=1`, to opt out. - **Broad CPU support.** Prebuilt x86-64 binaries do not require AVX or BMI; the static musl build also runs on systems with older glibc. - **Session token estimates.** `sessions --tokens` reads a decompressed size from the zstd frame header when available. Most streaming frames need the `zstd -dc` fallback. Results are cached under `~/.cache/rdsh/sessions-tokens.json` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` takes precedence); set `RDSH_TOKENS_CACHE=0` to disable the cache. A `?` marks an estimate that could not be read, for example when the zstd CLI is unavailable. - **Bounded parallel work.** Search and session scans use at most eight worker threads. The zstd CLI fallback uses 8 to 32 parallel processes. - **Native commands without Node.** Commands such as `tokens`, `search`, and `sessions` keep working without Node. To delegate conversations, install `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or set `DSH_ORIG_BIN` (or `RDSH_ORIG_BIN`). - **Low-priority updates.** `sync-dsh.sh` updates dsh and rdsh, verifies archive bytes against that registry, and rolls back a failed update candidate. By default it uses the stable release selected by the reviewed repository digest registry; set `RDSH_SYNC_FROM_SOURCE=1` to build from `main` under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c3` when available. The systemd unit runs at low priority; adjust its `ExecStart` to your checkout. ## Web UI & Dashboard ### Lightweight Local Web UI (`rdsh serve`) A lightweight status and token estimation page running on localhost (default `:38080`, does not conflict with DSH `:3080`): ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # enable the server feature rdsh serve # launch (bound to localhost, protected with a one-time token) ``` ### Product language rdsh-owned CLI diagnostics and the native local page support English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese. Choose one run with `--language`, or persist it in `rdsh.json`; the default `auto` reads the first nonblank locale environment variable, falling back to English when it is absent or unsupported. ```sh rdsh --language ja settings show rdsh settings set general.language zh-CN ``` Precedence is `--language`, `RDSH_LANG`, `general.language`, then `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`, and `LANG`. An explicitly invalid `general.language` stops the command without rewriting the settings file. Delegated `dsh` arguments, model output, JSON fields, files, and protocol identifiers are not translated. Interactive setup prompts and settings/policy validation use the selected language too. Authentication decisions and skipped-provider notes localize only the CLI presentation; their existing JSON strings remain unchanged, including malformed or oversized guard-input reasons. Native search continues to refuse unsupported non-Unix platforms before accessing the requested directory. `worker-scope validate` and `worker-scope policy` also localize their help and CLI diagnostics. These pure commands and their help ignore unrelated corrupt settings; ordinary commands and root help still report the settings error. Canonical JSON, policy codes and supplied paths stay unchanged. ### Protected delegated tools The opt-in agent tool sandbox supports Linux x86_64 with bubblewrap, prlimit, and unprivileged user namespaces. Its audited DSH/tool-runtime pairs are `0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1`, and `0.2.1-alpha.3`, with matching versions in each pair. It verifies package metadata, runtime bytes and the loaded module, then limits inspection to explicitly shared files. Unknown, mixed, modified or unexpectedly resolved runtimes stop before delegation. macOS and Windows refuse protected delegation; ordinary delegation keeps the original tools. This matrix applies to the Rust launcher. Project-pinned dashboard releases retain their separate [supported tuple](docs/STAGED-UPDATES.md#capture-trusted-runtime-code). ### Extended Dashboard (`rdsh-dashboard`) Optional Node.js dashboard for p

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # rdsh-ui-comfort Make Enter deliberate in the DSH Web chat, bundled with [rdsh](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh). ## What it changes Two DOM-level hooks, both registered on `window` in the capture phase so the shell's own React and Lexical handlers see a decision before they act. ### Composer: Enter twice sends A plain Enter no longer sends. The first Enter inserts a line break, and a second Enter inside 1.5 seconds sends the message. The line break is the shell's own Shift+Enter path and the send is its own Enter path, so chips, attachments, streaming and the send button behave exactly as before. ### Goal strip: Enter never commits While the goal editor is open, Enter no longer commits the edit — including the Enter that confirms an IME conversion, which upstream passes to the same `onKeyDown` handler as a typed Enter. The editor stays open, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter (or the check button) commits, and Escape cancels as before. ## Keys | Key | Composer | Goal editor | | --- | --- | --- | | Enter | line break; a second Enter within the window sends | nothing (the edit stays open) | | Shift+Enter | line break (stock) | nothing | | Ctrl/Cmd+Enter | send (stock) | commit the edit | | Escape | stock | cancel the edit (stock) | | IME confirmation Enter | left to the shell | never commits | Enter inside a completion menu (`[data-trigger-menu]`), Enter while composing (`isComposing`, `keyCode 229`), key auto-repeat and every modified Enter are left untouched, so the slash menu, the `@` mention menu, the workspace picker and Ctrl+Enter keep their own meaning. The queue-dock textarea (`[data-queue-dock]`) is not a composer input and is not hooked. ## Settings The plugin reads `localStorage["rdsh-ui-comfort:v1"]` on every key press, so a change applies without a reload. The **rdsh 入力** section in DSH Settings edits the same store; `window.__rdshUiComfort` exposes it from the console. | Member | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `doubleEnter` | `true` | Enter twice sends; `false` restores stock Enter-to-send | | `goalGuard` | `true` | protect the goal editor from Enter; `false` restores upstream | | `windowMs` | `1500` | how long the first Enter keeps the "second press sends" arm open (200–5000) | Both behaviours default to on, so the plugin is useful with no configuration. An unknown or unreadable value falls back to the defaults. ## Install `./plugins/install.sh` installs this plugin when it is listed among the bundled plugins. For one profile: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add "$(pwd)/plugins/rdsh-ui-comfort" ``` Refresh the Web UI afterwards; a profile with live patch reload picks the client half up without a service restart. Remove it with `dsh plugin --profile web remove rdsh-ui-comfort`. ## Verification - `node --test plugins/rdsh-ui-comfort/test/logic.test.mjs` drives the shipped bundle in a VM and checks the pure decision tables: first/second/expired Enter, the window boundary, another composer, `isComposing`, `keyCode 229`, Shift/Ctrl/Meta/Alt, auto-repeat, an open completion menu, and both switches off. - `node --test plugins/rdsh-ui-comfort/test/dom.playwright.test.mjs` loads the real bundle into a fixture page in Chromium, presses Enter from the keyboard and asserts the fake shell's own handlers: line break on the first Enter, send on the second, stock send for Ctrl+Enter, and no goal commit on a plain or composing Enter. The test skips when no Chromium is available. - The anchors were read from the shipped DSH client: `[data-composer-input]` is the contenteditable in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation`, `[data-goal-bar]` and its `input[type=text]` are in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-goal`, and `[data-trigger-menu]` is in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-input-trigger`. ## Caveats - Upstream ships hashed CSS-module class names; this plugin matches only the stable data attributes above. A DSH rename removes the hook and leaves the stock Enter behaviour in place (fail closed), so re-check the three packages after a DSH upgrade. - The goal strip is a single-line ``, so Enter cannot insert a newline there; it is a no-op rather than a commit. - The plugin changes what Enter does, not how a message is sent: it never calls the send path itself. The second Enter is the shell's own key. # rdsh — a fast, safe Rust launcher for `dsh` [![ci](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![dashboard](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml) [![docs](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rdsh.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rdsh) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [日本語](README.ja.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) An independent community project; not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness project. `rdsh` is a fast, safe launcher for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond process launch**: `rdsh --version` starts in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak RSS, versus ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh --version`. This is process launch only: a booted agent profile still runs upstream Node.js, so conversation startup and session memory match upstream. See [Benchmarks](#benchmarks). - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` Or install the crate from crates.io (needs Rust 1.85+): ```sh cargo install rdsh ``` `cargo install` builds from source and installs the same binary as the release archives. Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL users can also install the release [`.deb`/`.rpm`](#native-packages-deb--rpm) with `apt`/`dnf`. ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Native Packages (`.deb` / `.rpm`) Linux x86_64 users on Debian/Ubuntu (and WSL) or Fedora/RHEL can install the same release binary with the OS package manager. Download the `.deb` or `.rpm` from the [latest release](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest) and install that file directly; no extra repository is configured. ```sh sudo apt install ./rdsh__amd64.deb # Debian, Ubuntu, WSL sudo dnf install ./rdsh--1.x86_64.rpm # Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux ``` `` is the release tag without its leading `v` (`0.6.0` for `v0.6.0`). The package installs `/usr/bin/rdsh` together with the licence and README, so `rdsh --version` works right after installation: no Rust toolchain, no `install.sh`. Like `rdsh-linux-x64.tar.gz`, both packages carry the glibc build, so the musl archive and `install.sh` stay the fallback for older distributions. ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ### Package Managers (Homebrew / Scoop / winget) Advanced users on macOS and Windows can let a package manager own the installed `rdsh` binary. The manifests in [packaging/](packaging/README.md) pin the exact release archives and their SHA-256 values; [docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md](docs/PACKAGE-MANAGERS.md) lists the install commands and the update procedure. **macOS (Homebrew)** — installs the Apple Silicon or Intel archive: ```sh brew install --formula ./packaging/homebrew/rdsh.rb ``` **Windows (Scoop)**: ```powershell scoop install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/main/packaging/scoop/rdsh.json ``` **Windows (winget)** — winget 1.6 or newer reads the three manifests directly; submitting them to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` stays a manual step: ```powershell winget install --manifest .\packaging\winget ``` These channels track one release at a time, so a new tag is not served until `python3 scripts/update-packaging-manifests.py --version vX.Y.Z` refreshes them. ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. To invalidate the credential itself, revoke the OAuth grant or rotate the API key at its provider. That may also disconnect the source CLI. This controls rdsh copying, not DSH's own refreshes, inherited environment access or an OS sandbox. **Migration:** existing DSH credentials are retained. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=0 disables automatic imports while keeping the selection; an explicit auth --import still works. Invalid/unreadable policies fail closed instead of falling back to legacy sync. Consent changes and rdsh credential writes share a lock, so a completed unselect cannot be bypassed by a queued rdsh import using an earlier policy. After a crashed writer, check that no rdsh auth/setup writer is active before removing $DSH_HOME/.rdsh-auth-sharing.lock; the launcher skips copying while it is locked. setup --web issues a new local access key at startup in its #key=... URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features and the privacy-sensitive switches (`discord`, `telemetry`) stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast, telemetry-free dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | Needs SearXNG. | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Anything a provider changes afterwards is absent from the picker until that dependency is upgraded — and a profile that lists `models:` explicitly replaces the bundled catalog for the route anyway. `rdsh models` reads the provider's own catalog (the local Codex CLI, or Kimi Code's `/v1/models` endpoint with the profile's API key) and folds it into the profile: ```sh rdsh models # read-only: missing ids and stale names rdsh models --provider kimi-coding # one provider only rdsh models sync # add missing entries, refresh stale names rdsh models sync --profile web --dry-run # preview one profile ``` Nothing is deleted, an existing entry keeps every other byte (a name the provider's current one already contains is left as written), and a profile the command does not recognize is refused instead of rewritten. The harness picks the changes up on the next config reload or restart. ### Agent Tool Isolation Delegated agent tools keep normal file access by default: the model reads and writes the project like any other tool. `--share-file` isolates **`rdsh_inspect` only**. On Linux (with bubblewrap and prlimit) that tool sees just the files you explicitly share: ```sh rdsh --share-file README.md --share-file src/main.rs --profile tui ``` From `rdsh_inspect`, only the shared files are mounted read-only, host files stay out of reach and the sandbox has no network. Turn the same boundary on for every run with `rdsh features on agent_tool_sandbox` (off again with `rdsh features off agent_tool_sandbox`, or force it with `RDSH_SECURITY=1`). Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals. Startup prints `[rdsh security] rdsh_inspect is isolated; other DSH tools use upstream permissions`. ### Hook Guard (`rdsh guard`) Integrates with DSH `hooks.json` to inspect and block dangerous commands before execution: ```sh echo "$input" | rdsh guard --deny "rm -rf /*" --deny "*token*" ``` For an opt-in structured check of supported file tools, pass a policy file. This example permits `Read` only under one existing project directory: ```json { "schema": 1, "rules": [ { "id": "project-read", "tool": "Read", "access": "read", "roots": ["/absolute/project/path"] } ] } ``` ```sh echo "$hook_json" | rdsh guard --policy-file ./hook-policy.json --json ``` The structured classifier supports the `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` file-path schemas. It canonicalizes the working directory and target, checks the selected tool and read/write scope against existing policy roots, and reports `allow`, `deny`, or `unknown` with a non-sensitive reason. In JSON mode an `allow` is classification only and omits `decision`; the host still owns permission and approval. Unknown tools, shell commands, malformed input, and unsupported tool arguments fail closed. Shell parsing and network destinations are not implemented. Path checks are advisory and can race with later filesystem changes; this hook is not an OS sandbox. Use the actual execution sandbox for enforcement. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "rdsh guard --deny \"rm -rf /*\"" }] } ] } } ``` ### Context Injection (`rdsh context`) `rdsh context inject` assembles this turn's context — goal, constraints, decisions, working set, git state, retrieved code, and curated memory — and emits it in the DSH `UserPromptSubmit` hook contract, so the model sees it without any copy-paste: ```sh rdsh features on context_engine # the engine is opt-in rdsh context hook install # merges $DSH_HOME/hooks.json (idempotent) rdsh context hook status --json ``` The hook is fail-open: it never blocks a prompt and always exits 0. Only an unreadable settings document or an unparseable payload inject nothing at all; a corrupt index or a missed deadline drops just what depends on them — the graph or the code search — and still injects goal, constraints, and memory. Injection has its own budget (`context.inject_budget`, default 1200 tokens) and deadline (`context.inject_deadline_ms`, default 1200 ms); once the deadline passes the code search is skipped and only memory, goal, and constraints go out. Memory holds curated items, not a transcript dump: ```sh rdsh context remember "Keep the API compatible" --kind constraint rdsh context distill --session ~/.dsh/sessions///session.v4.jsonl.zstd --apply rdsh context memory --json # active and superseded entries rdsh context forget mem_ab12cd34ef56 ``` `distill` reads user turns only (zstd session logs included) and extracts decisions, constraints, and retractions with deterministic markers, superseding an older overlapping entry instead of guessing. `rdsh context build --require-stable` exits 3 unless the snapshot is provably stable: a file or git state that changed during assembly counts, and so does a git state it cannot read, so a stale or unknown snapshot is never reported as fresh. ### Dependency Graph and Change Impact (`rdsh deps`) ```sh rdsh deps build # incremental index under $DSH_HOME/rdsh-index rdsh deps query engine_score # where a symbol is defined and referenced rdsh deps impact src/context.rs # direct/transitive dependents + affected tests ``` The extractor covers Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Go and records imports, definitions, and static call sites per file. Unchanged files (same size and mtime) are reused, so repeated runs stay fast. It is a static approximation: dynamic dispatch, indirect calls, macros, and generated code remain explicitly `unknown` and are reported as unresolved counts rather than guessed, and a missing index means "no information", never "no dependencies". When the index exists, `rdsh context build` and `rdsh context inject` also pull in the graph neighbours of the files their search matched, so a retrieved excerpt arrives with the files it actually depends on. Native execution overhead is ~1 ms per invocation. ## Low-end hosts Default profile: `RDSH_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, then `general.default_profile` in rdsh settings, then local `tui`, else a guided error. Set the saved default with `rdsh settings set general.default_profile web`; an explicit `--profile ` keeps its precedence. rdsh aims to remain useful on modest machines: older x86-64 CPUs, older Linux distributions, and hosts without Node.js installed. - **Faster Node startup.** When rdsh launches dsh, it sets `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to `~/.cache/rdsh-node-compile-cache`, letting Node reuse compiled code across launches (Node 22.1 or newer; older versions ignore it). An existing `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` value is preserved. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=0`, or use `--passthrough` / `RDSH_PASSTHROUGH=1`, to opt out. - **Broad CPU support.** Prebuilt x86-64 binaries do not require AVX or BMI; the static musl build also runs on systems with older glibc. - **Session token estimates.** `sessions --tokens` reads a decompressed size from the zstd frame header when available. Most streaming frames need the `zstd -dc` fallback. Results are cached under `~/.cache/rdsh/sessions-tokens.json` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` takes precedence); set `RDSH_TOKENS_CACHE=0` to disable the cache. A `?` marks an estimate that could not be read, for example when the zstd CLI is unavailable. - **Bounded parallel work.** Search and session scans use at most eight worker threads. The zstd CLI fallback uses 8 to 32 parallel processes. - **Native commands without Node.** Commands such as `tokens`, `search`, and `sessions` keep working without Node. To delegate conversations, install `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or set `DSH_ORIG_BIN` (or `RDSH_ORIG_BIN`). - **Low-priority updates.** `sync-dsh.sh` updates dsh and rdsh, verifies archive bytes against that registry, and rolls back a failed update candidate. By default it uses the stable release selected by the reviewed repository digest registry; set `RDSH_SYNC_FROM_SOURCE=1` to build from `main` under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c3` when available. The systemd unit runs at low priority; adjust its `ExecStart` to your checkout. ## Web UI & Dashboard ### Lightweight Local Web UI (`rdsh serve`) A lightweight status and token estimation page running on localhost (default `:38080`, does not conflict with DSH `:3080`): ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # enable the server feature rdsh serve # launch (bound to localhost, protected with a one-time token) ``` ### Product language rdsh-owned CLI diagnostics and the native local page support English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese. Choose one run with `--language`, or persist it in `rdsh.json`; the default `auto` reads the first nonblank locale environment variable, falling back to English when it is absent or unsupported. ```sh rdsh --language ja settings show rdsh settings set general.language zh-CN ``` Precedence is `--language`, `RDSH_LANG`, `general.language`, then `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`, and `LANG`. An explicitly invalid `general.language` stops the command without rewriting the settings file. Delegated `dsh` arguments, model output, JSON fields, files, and protocol identifiers are not translated. Interactive setup prompts and settings/policy validation use the selected language too. Authentication decisions and skipped-provider notes localize only the CLI presentation; their existing JSON strings remain unchanged, including malformed or oversized guard-input rea
