evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# LoopX for DeepSeek Harness

`dsh-loopx-plugin` is one independently versioned DSH package with three
separate Loader rows:

- the init row automatically installs or upgrades the LoopX CLI, installs the
  packaged workflow skills into `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills` (default
  `~/.agents/skills`), and verifies the DSH-native `loopx` entry before DSH
  finishes loading it. `/loopx-init` remains the explicit repair command.
- a passive same-session Driver becomes eligible only after the exact current
  Session successfully invokes the exact `loopx` skill. It then asks LoopX
  whether another turn may run and queues the authoritative heartbeat task
  into that live DSH Agent.
- the package-root Host registers GoalBar at the authenticated
  `/api/loopx.goalbar` route required by DSH 0.1.5. Its web Client adds a compact
  GoalBar between DSH's native GoalBar and Queue dock rows, visible only for one
  exact live `(goalId, loopxAgentId)` binding.

Installing the plugin and starting DSH load and prepare these capabilities;
neither creates a binding nor activates the Driver. The GoalBar
does one bounded read when a browser row mounts, then watches exact-Session
`step/end` and `turn/end` boundaries. It rereads LoopX only when the opaque
revision of the authoritative binding or active Goal state changes; a watch
lease also detects changes written outside that Session. DSH Agent-status
events update an existing row without a LoopX business read. Until one exact
Session contains valid typed `loopx` invocation evidence, its Driver makes no
LoopX CLI, binding, quota, or heartbeat call, creates no timer, and queues no
followup.

The package does not expose LoopX model tools, a binding sidecar, or its own
Goal/Todo state. Models use the installed LoopX skills and call the LoopX CLI
directly. LoopX remains the only authority for Goal, Agent, Todo, quota,
activation, and durable thread-binding data. The GoalBar protocol and its
deferred atomicity limit are specified in the versioned
[DSH native LoopX design](../../docs/plans/2026-08-20-dsh-native-skill-driver.md).

## Install

Requirements are Node.js 22.19+, `pnpm`, Python 3.11+ with `pip`, and network
access for the first DSH start when no compatible LoopX CLI is already
installed. LoopX itself is deliberately not a prerequisite. The initializer
honors an explicit `PYTHON_BIN`; otherwise it tries `python3`, then discovers
`python3.<minor>` executables on the supplied `PATH` in descending numeric
order, then tries the bare name `python`. The last name is what a python.org
Windows install registers, so it keeps that host reachable when `python3` is
absent or is the `WindowsApps` App Execution Alias that never starts Python.
Unlike the versioned names it is not a `PATH` scan result; it is resolved when
the candidate runs. Installation still checks the Python version and pip;
reopening the managed runtime uses the same discovery and validates the LoopX
CLI. No hard-coded minor-version list is maintained. When selecting Python for
installation, an invalid explicit interpreter fails instead of falling back.
Managed-runtime readback keeps the existing CLI fallback behavior. If the
plugin must install or upgrade LoopX, it writes an isolated
copy under `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/runtime/dsh-loopx-plugin` (default
`~/.agents/runtime/dsh-loopx-plugin`) and never mutates the system Python
environment. This works with externally managed Python distributions that
enforce PEP 668; the plugin does not use `--break-system-packages`.
This version requires LoopX 1.2.4 or newer, the published release that
includes the Windows peer-file fix. Bootstrap, Driver and GoalBar use the same
version floor; an older global or managed CLI is upgraded or rejected before
business commands run. An explicit outdated `LOOPX_BIN` must be upgraded by its
owner. Older plugin releases retain their original CLI requirements.
Install the prebuilt release into the web profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add \
  "https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/releases/download/dsh-loopx-plugin-v0.1.1-beta.6/dsh-loopx-plugin-0.1.1-beta.6.tgz"
```

The beta.6 package targets the qualified DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 API and retains the
qualified frozen 0.1.5 and 0.1.7-rc.2 compatibility ranges. The exported legacy
RPC registration remains available to explicit callers, but plugin startup
always uses the shared API.

For a compatible DSH source build, use:

```bash
cd packages/dsh-loopx-plugin
./install.sh
```

Start DSH on loopback (port `0` asks the OS for a free port) and open the
printed URL. The plugin finishes its idempotent LoopX CLI and skill bootstrap
before DSH publishes the Web URL through its native Loader readiness boundary.
The source candidate gates only LoopX's Host and Driver on `loopxBootstrap`,
so disabling or uninstalling it keeps the shared Web server and runtime alive.
The published beta.6 limitation is described under automatic initialization:

```bash
dsh --profile web --port 0
```

Use `/loopx <task>` immediately. If automatic initialization reports a safe
failure in the DSH log, fix the named Python or package-manager problem and run
`/loopx-init` once to retry; normal installation does not require that command.

Installation is the GoalBar opt-in: there is no separate remote endpoint or
per-session grant. A row remains hidden until the exact DSH Session has one
unique LoopX binding. After invoking the installed `loopx` skill for that
Session, run the minimum authority readback inside that Session's DSH shell
(or replace `$DSH_SESSION_ID` with the exact Session id):

```bash
loopx --registry .loopx/registry.json --format json \
  resolve-agent-thread \
  --host-surface deepseek-harness-native \
  --thread-id "$DSH_SESSION_ID"
```

`status=bound` with one exact pair admits the row; missing or ambiguous results
fail closed and render nothing. `Start` resumes a stopped Goal and asks the
Driver to evaluate only when that exact live Session already contains typed
`loopx` skill activation evidence. It never activates an inactive Session.
`Pause` stops the Goal and retires only future queued/scheduled continuation;
it does not abort a claimed or running turn.

Maintainers can validate the built and packed surfaces with:

```bash
pnpm build
pnpm smoke:artifact
pnpm smoke:profile
pnpm smoke:runtime
pnpm smoke:docker
```

The runtime smoke creates an isolated temporary DSH profile. Its real web
process proves profile composition, automatic initialization before readiness,
immediate skill-catalog visibility, boot-manifest discovery, bundle serving,
Client materialization, and the loopback Connection fence. A
live-disable probe withdraws the bootstrap provider and all package rows while
checking that DSH stays available and LoopX's route retires; a fresh process
also boots with the whole package disabled. Separately, a
packed supported-DSH Context, Connection, and WebServer with a live Host Session fixture
cover same-turn binding discovery, lease-time source reconciliation,
status-only updates, pending-watch cancellation, successful actions, and
handler disposal through the real HTTP carrier. The served Client is then
applied in DSH's real ClientModuleSystem with a VM document harness; that layer
covers slot order and coexistence, Session injection, and ordinary-unload/HMR
style cleanup, but it is not a browser-mounted React interaction. These layers
do not replace the owner-reviewed packed-browser gate: that separate manual
layer mounts the served Client at a real DSH URL and exercises Client-to-carrier
Start/Pause. Focused Client tests cover Session-generation replacement and old
request cancellation without duplicating that matrix in the packed smoke.
The Docker smoke packs the current plugin and builds the current LoopX
release-candidate wheel, then starts both in a clean Debian container with the
DSH 0.1.5-rc.2 release candidate. It proves PEP 668-compatible private installation,
the managed launcher, startup readiness, installed `loopx` skill files, launch-
token authentication, and an authenticated GoalBar read through DSH's shared
API carrier. It requires Docker, `uv`, and network access for base images and
never opens a browser or configures a model provider.

## Maintainer release and marketplace handoff

A DSH plugin release needs an immutable prebuilt GitHub asset and a qualified
install channel in each marketplace named in its closeout. The
[`awesome-dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin)
directory and [DSH Plugin Hub](https://github.com/dshplugin/dsh-plugin-hub)
have distinct published catalogs. Current Hub releases read
`https://api.dsh-plugin.org/plugins.en.json` and `plugins.zh.json`; updating
the awesome directory does not update those consumers. Marketplace maintainers
retain authority over their own catalogs.

Pinned GitHub release installation does not require publishing LoopX on npm.
Release-URL installed-state matching shipped in
[Hub 1.5.0](https://github.com/dshplugin/dsh-plugin-hub/releases/tag/v1.5.0).
Qualification must read the actual marketplace's catalog back, select the
pinned package, install it, recognize the installed row, update it and remove
it successfully. The optional npm channel retains its separate account and
trusted-publisher requirements.

For every DSH plugin release:

1. Update the package version and this README's pinned install URL. Run the
   typecheck, tests, and the built, packed, runtime, profile, and Docker smokes
   listed above, plus `pnpm smoke:registry --tarball <packed-package.tgz>`.
   The registry smoke serves the real packed bytes on loopback and invokes
   DSH's unversioned package-name installer; it publishes nothing. CI repeats
   this installation and removal on Linux and Windows.
   Qualification uses pnpm 10.33.0; use that version for reproducible source
   and isolated-registry checks.
2. Prepare complete bilingual GitHub release notes. Run
   `examples/release/release-readiness-doc-smoke.py` with one `--surface` for
   every optional capability changed by the release.
3. Merge the exact reviewed commit, pack from that immutable tag target, and
   publish both the version tag and `dsh-loopx-plugin-<version>.tgz` asset.
4. Read the remote release body back and rerun the release-readiness smoke.
   Download the remote asset and verify that its SHA-256 matches the local
   package before advertising it. For the npm channel, publish that **same
   tarball**, including its compiled Host, Client, Driver and initializer:

   ```bash
   npm whoami
   npm publish ./dsh-loopx-plugin-VERSION.tgz --access public --tag latest
   node scripts/verify-distribution.mjs --tarball ./dsh-loopx-plugin-VERSION.tgz
   ```

   `latest` intentionally names the qualified plugin candidate, because the
   marketplace installs its unversioned npm name. Do not substitute a
   beta-only tag or publish the monorepo root. The readback checks metadata,
   tag, downloaded bytes and the repository search used by DSH Hub. A missing
   package, wrong artifact or search-index delay fails verification; publishing
   alone does not complete marketplace recovery. npm account authentication
   or configured trusted publishing belongs to the release operator.

   For token-free CI publication, configure the package's npm Trusted Publisher
   with organization `loopx-project`, repository `loopx`, and workflow filename
   `dsh-plugin-publish.yml`, permitting `npm publish`. Then dispatch **Publish
   DSH Plugin to npm** on the existing published plugin tag, using that same tag
   for the `release_tag` input. This keeps npm provenance on the artifact's commit.
   The workflow requires a merged tag, consumes its GitHub asset without
   rebuilding, and verifies npm bytes and discovery. It neither creates a
   GitHub release nor replaces npm account ownership or the release guide gate.
5. For the awesome directory, in a clean fork branch of `awesome-dsh-plugin`, update only
   `data/plugins/loopx-project__loopx--packages-dsh-loopx-plugin.yml` to the new
   immutable asset URL. Confirm the URL resolves, then run
   `node scripts/generate-readme.mjs --check` and `git diff --check`.
6. Open the upstream directory pull request and link it from the release
   closeout. Separately verify the installed Hub's catalog source at the
   released Hub revision. Read both language feeds and the website's install
   command; for the LoopX row, check the `ic` and `igc` targets against the
   immutable release URL. Route stale Hub metadata to its existing
   [data-correction issue channel](https://github.com/dshplugin/dsh-plugin-hub/issues).
   Keep that marketplace's adoption open until its actual consumer resolves
   and installs the released package. A merged directory PR, another catalog's
   listing, or an upgraded Hub cannot establish that postcondition.

## Shadow observer (default off)

`src/observer.ts`, exported as `dsh-loopx-plugin/observer`, is the
`dsh-session-events` provider for the LoopX
[Reliability Diagnostics](../../loopx/capabilities/reliability_diagnostics/README.md)
capability: an L1 shadow observer that consumes read-only harness events and
appends compact, public-safe envelopes plus an observer stats record to
`<loopx-runtime-root>/reliability_diagnostics/by-goal/<sha256>.ndjson`, where
`sha256` is the lowercase digest of the exact UTF-8 Goal id. Upgrade the CLI and
plugin together. An existing legacy filename blocks flushes with
`LegacyDiagnosticLedgerError` until the
[offline upgrade](../../loopx/capabilities/reliability_diagnostics/docs/local-retention-v0.md#upgrading-a-legacy-ledger-offline)
preserves its history; readback never silently migrates it. It is a
separate Cordis row and bundle from the Driver, with no Driver or Agent
injection and no shared send path. It never calls `agent.send`, touches the
inbox, invokes the LoopX CLI, schedules, retries, stops, or resumes anything.
Every hook body and every flush is isolated, so an observer failure is counted
into the receipt instead of reaching DSH. This is module and hook isolation,
not an OS-process-isolation claim.

Before its first append, the producer applies the same recursive local-path,
credential-like value, and credential-field guard as the Python contract.
Unsafe event tokens or ids are counted as `public_safety_violation` and never
reach ledger bytes; CLI ingest independently re-validates persisted records.

It is off unless one exact goal, DSH session, and complete run identity are
declared before DSH starts:

```bash
export LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_GOAL_ID=<goal-id>
export LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_SESSION_ID=<session-id>
export LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_RUN_IDENTITY_JSON='{"worker_id":"<worker>","model_id":"<model>","task_id":"<task>","environment_id":"<environment>","tools_id":"<tools>","budget_id":"<budget>","adapter_revision":"<adapter-revision>","observer_revision":"<observer-revision>"}'
# optional: LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_LEDGER_DIR, LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_BUFFER_BOUND (default 256)
loopx reliability-diagnostics receipt --goal-id <goal-id> --format json
loopx reliability-diagnostics status  --goal-id <goal-id> --format json
```

Unless all required variables are valid, the independent observer row
registers no hook and writes no file. When enabled, it consumes only
`session/created`, `session/event`, and `session/disposed`; it skips the retired
token-level `assistant/chunk` rows older logs still replay, and records tool
names, turn and step numbers, typed end reasons, and ids only, never arguments,
outputs, prompts, or paths. Events for
any session other than the exact configured session are rejected as
`identity_invalid`. The stats record pins worker/model/task/environment/tools/
budget plus adapter and observer revisions, declares source coverage, and
proves count conservation. Sequence gaps, bounded-buffer drops, flush attempts,
declared clock uncertainty, and the empty outbound and influence fields make
the run's admissibility auditable from the receipt.

This is an experimental adapter implementing the RFC's P0 prototype
components. It does not establish the RFC's P0 exit: C0 fidelity, a qualifying
C1 run, and measured observer overhead remain separate evidence gates.

## Optional native operation context (SDK prerequisite)

The independently loaded `dsh-loopx-plugin/native-operation-context` subpath
registers one read-only model tool, `loopx_operation_context`. It is absent from
the default plugin tree and `cordis.patch.yml`; installing the package does not
activate it. An explicit SDK Loader patch can load the built module:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: loopx-native-operation-context
      name: file:///absolute/path/to/dsh-loopx-plugin/lib/native-operation-context.js
```

The tool accepts `{}` only. It derives the calling live session and open Turn
from DSH's agent and session-projection services; caller-supplied identities,
closed Turns, cancelled calls and disposed or shadowed tool registrations fail.
Only provider, model and reasoning-effort options are returned. Other agent
options, including credentials, are excluded. Profile options are observations,
not HTTP wire attestation; `wire_profile_verified` and `execution_allowed` are
always `false`. This module creates no Core actor, grant, binding, approval or
account access, and consumes no approval.

The initial runtime qualification uses the Python SDK and bundled DSH
`0.1.5rc1`: a real native tool call returned the matching SDK session and open
Turn. This does not qualify other DSH versions or the complete managed operation
journey. From a source checkout, build and verify registration using an
interpreter with the selected `deepseek-harness` SDK installed:

```bash
pnpm --dir packages/dsh-loopx-plugin build
"$SDK_PYTHON" packages/dsh-loopx-plugin/smoke/dsh-native-context-sdk-smoke.py \
  --module packages/dsh-loopx-plugin/lib/native-operation-context.js \
  --provider deepseek-official --model deepseek-flash
```

This smoke initializes the real SDK with an isolated temporary home and dummy
credentials, checks the runtime's schema registration, and makes zero model
requests. It does not execute a Turn or test financial operations. Remove the
explicit Loader row to disable the module, then restart the owning SDK runtime;
the default plugin tree remains unchanged. Existing active sessions must be
closed by their owner rather than treated as revoked by editing a patch file.

The read-only module alone delivers no frontend or Lark operation path.

## Optional owned SDK operation connection

`dsh-loopx-plugin/native-operation` is a separate, explicit Loader module for
the internal `OwnedDshOperationHost`. It registers `loopx_operation` with an
absolute, parent-owned Unix socket supplied by the host; it is absent from the
default exports and patch. Installing the package grants no execution access.

The host retains the original SDK stdio connection across separately admitted
Turns. Kernel peer PID, native session/Turn/call ID, exact native arguments and
the observed provider/model/effort must match before dispatch to the existing
Core operation handler. The existing Turn session file and typed operation
store own profile binding, revocation, approval, first consumption and outcome;
there is no second approval store or public actor/proof/consume endpoint.
Changing the module/package JS, model profile or session requires fresh
admission and approval. Transport loss never permits an automatic effect retry.

The real SDK/bundled runtime `0.1.5rc1` qualifies two Turns on one retained
connection with a scripted loopback provider: prepare, reject before approval,
fixture confirmation, inspect, one permitted consumption, rejected repeat and
canonical `not_executed` outcome. Synthetic confirmation is not human approval;
no venue/account effect or paid model call is involved. The read-only real-model
probe above and this integrated synthetic-provider test prove different stages.

SDK `0.1.5rc1` cannot reload persisted sessions (`session already exists`);
a new host still refuses that version's resume before runtime launch.
An isolated candidate uses Python SDK `0.2.1a3`, built with the official wheel
script from [upstream source `2fbf4359`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/2fbf4359b82fb94c03dcce0b831660d87f12ea5c),
and an explicit `runtime_bin` pointing to npm `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-alpha.3`.
The SDK's public `resume_session` restores the same persisted identity without
sending input. The host pins SDK files, the executable/Node and complete npm
closure into the immutable profile; changes require fresh admission/approval.
File/SQLite tests close the first process, restore the original session and
repeat the operation sequence. Missing or unreadable history refuses without
a provider call, replacement binding or reusable failed client. This candidate
does not qualify the default plugin's peer range or a published Python release.

Public CLI/delegation activation, frontend/Lark original-card return and actual
financial execution remain unqualified. The public managed-operation preflight
remains Codex-only until those entry points are integrated. Disable by omitting this explicit
module and closing its owned host; do not interpret patch removal as revoking
an already running process.

## GoalBar authority and privacy boundary

The GoalBar carrier uses Connection's authenticated `/api/loopx.goalbar`
Fetch route. Explicit callers of the deprecated RPC registration can still
register `/loopx`; plugin startup does not select it automatically. Both pass
Connection's Host/Origin trust fence and browser authentication, and this
package adds no second credential of its own. The deployment's reachability
policy — loopback by default, or declared `trustedHosts` — decides which
browsers can reach the host at all; Phase 1 does not support LAN or remote
browsers. The browser supplies only its injected DSH Session id and, for an
action, the last validated Goal/Agent pair. The Host re-derives cwd and thread
identity from the live DSH Agent, freshly resolves the binding, and executes
only fixed LoopX argv.

The wire allowlist contains ids, activation, live Agent status, full-lane
counts, cursors, opaque source revisions, and fixed error codes. It excludes
Todo text, Goal objective, quota, evidence, CLI output, exception messages,
registry paths, credentials, and binding candidates. A source revision is only
a change token, not authorization or a compare-and-swap guard. Installing the
package grants no model tool authority, does not create or repair bindings, and
does not change LoopX core state by itself.

## Automatic initialization and `/loopx-init` repair

When DSH loads the plugin, the init row runs the same typed initialization
routine and publishes the `loopxBootstrap` readiness service only after it
settles. DSH's native Loader wait keeps the printed URL behind initialization;
the service is a dependency only of LoopX's Host and Driver. A safe failure is
logged without raw subprocess output or local paths and leaves `/loopx-init`
registered for an explicit retry. Disabling the package leaves LoopX's
rows unavailable while DSH remains usable. Removing the package's
rows releases its routes without stopping the shared Web server or runtime.
Automatic startup does not create Agent followups or model calls.

The host-isolation repair in this source is pending a new plugin release.
Published beta.6 still adds the shared Web dependency and can disconnect DSH
during hot uninstall, including with Hub 1.6.4. For that published package,
close DSH, remove it with the native plugin CLI, then restart DSH.

The repair command has no arguments. Extra input returns a usage error before any
model work or CLI probe. A valid invocation queues a bounded start followup on
the exact receiving Agent, then probes the current LoopX installation. When the
CLI is missing or lacks the DSH-native skill contract, it runs exactly one
fixed-argv `pip install --upgrade --target <plugin-runtime> 'loopx>=1.2.4'`, writes a
small managed Python launcher beside that target, then uses that same
interpreter and launcher to install and read back the skills. Driver and
GoalBar resolve this same managed runtime, including after an explicit repair.
It never constructs a shell command, mutates the system Python environment,
edits a registry, or retries the install mutation.

Unless the command is cancelled, it queues a second bounded followup for the
typed success or failure result. These are ordinary Agent turns, so a valid,
uncancelled invocation normally adds two model calls; cancellation leaves only
the already queued start turn, while invalid input adds none. The prompts do
not authorize tools, commands, or another installation. Followup delivery is
best effort and is not retried. The native `CommandResult` rendered by the
command UI remains authoritative: a followup failure or model reply cannot
change the installation result or repeat its mutation.

On success, DSH's filesystem skill provider invalidates its catalog and loads
created or updated skills without a restart. Missing or unknown skill status
still fails initialization instead of being guessed as unchanged.

After initialization, invoke the `loopx` skill with the task text. The skill
uses the exact DSH-managed `$DSH_SESSION_ID`, passes
`--host-surface deepseek-harness-native`, and follows the typed commands
returned by LoopX. The historical external connector remains the distinct
`deepseek-harness` / `dsh` surface.

## Driver activation boundary

Activation is per Session, not per plugin, process, Agent, Goal, or project.
The Driver accepts only either of these durable typed Session facts:

- a `user/message` whose source is exactly `skill-invocation`, whose name is
  exactly `loopx`, and whose form is exactly `instructions`;
- a model `tool/call` named exactly `skill`, with JSON object arguments whose
  `name` is exactly `loopx`, paired by call id with a subsequent successful
  `tool/result`.

A skill catalog, ordinary prose, shell text, `/loopx-init`, plugin-authored
init or heartbeat messages, a failed, malformed, unmatched, or superseded
model call, and the presence of a CLI, registry, Goal, binding, or project file
do not activate the Driver. Recovery folds only the current Session's existing
typed event history in memory and performs no external probe. Replacing or
clearing a Session recomputes from the replacement history; activation never
inherits across that boundary and has no plugin-owned durable store.

Existing Sessions upgraded from an older plugin version remain inactive when
their retained history has no recognizable invocation evidence. Invoke the
installed `loopx` skill once in every Session that should continue
automatically. Activation records intent only: it does not create a binding,
select a Goal or Agent, spend quota, or grant tool authority. After activation,
the existing exact binding, fresh quota, scheduler/heartbeat, reservation, and
pre-step revalidation order remains authoritative.

## Driver retry boundary

DSH's LLM retry plugin owns provider-request retries. This Driver retries only
safe fixed-argv LoopX reads and an idempotent `quota should-run` receipt, at
most twice beyond the first attempt. Every retry uses the same
`--turn-instance-id`. Typed authority denials, incompatible schemas,
cancellation, and human input are never retried. There is no cumulative
eight-failure breaker or plugin-owned durable activation state. The small
process-local activation projection is bound to one exact Session and is
reconstructed only from its typed event history. Exhausting the three attempts
stops that evaluation; it does not create a periodic error-retry loop. Only a
typed LoopX local-scheduler plan can schedule another wakeup, and its limit on
unchanged polls is enforced.

For an admitted automatic continuation, that exact turn id is also carried in
the LoopX-owned canonical heartbeat body and the typed DSH continuation source.
The source is attribution for reservation matching, not authority. Before work
enters a model step, the Driver replays the same receipt and the LoopX guard
returns the typed settlement plan for that exact id. Accountable work writes
back and spends through that plan's single deterministic effect identity; it
does not fall back to an unbound generic spend command. Human priority, Pause,
dispose, or a failed pre-step check before work begins does not fabricate a
writeback, spend, or void receipt.

The Driver resolves the current project registry with
`resolve-agent-thread`, requires one exact Goal/Agent match for the live DSH
session, and rechecks binding plus quota before and after downstream pre-step
listeners. A human message removes an unclaimed automatic reservation; a
mixed batch rejects the automatic message and restores the human work.
The Driver queues at most one Driver-owned followup per automatic admission.
Initialization messages use the distinct `dsh-loopx-plugin/init-command`
source and never satisfy a Driver reservation.

## Installation and upgrade recovery

Check `dsh --version` before choosing an artifact. The current source accepts
DSH 0.1.5 release candidates from rc.1, stable 0.1.x from 0.1.5, and the explicitly
qualified 0.1.7-rc.2 and 0.2.0-rc.2 candidates. It excludes earlier 0.2 candidates,
0.2.1 alpha builds and other, unqualified prerelease tuples. A stable-version
range alone does not admit every prerelease.
The immutable beta.5 download above contains the earlier integration; building
this checkout produces beta.6. A source build is not a published beta.6 release.

If a marketplace reports `loopx-repository: entry file missing: index.js`, it
selected the monorepo root instead of this plugin package. Installing
`git+https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx.git` cannot select the nested, built
plugin. The marketplace's npm route requires a published `dsh-loopx-plugin`
whose repository points here and whose keywords include `dsh-plugin`; otherwise

# dsh-tower

[![CI](https://github.com/louifinn/dsh-tower/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/louifinn/dsh-tower/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-tower.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-tower)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[中文说明](README.zh.md)

**Tower** is a multi-agent orchestration plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). It turns one agent session into a small engineering team: the session acts as the *control tower*, worker agents do the implementation inside isolated Git worktrees, and nothing reaches your base branch without an independent review and a hard merge gate.

Tower mode and its mission/review workflow are inspired by the experimental **Tower mode in [Kimi Code](https://www.kimi.com/code)** by Moonshot AI. This is an independent implementation for DSH and is not affiliated with Moonshot AI; see [Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements).

The repository root **is** the DSH bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and `cordis.patch.yml` lives at the root, as the DSH plugin specification expects.

## Features

- **Human-owned Tower mode.** `/tower` toggles a session-level stance that narrows the tool surface and injects the Tower protocol. `/tower on|off <instruction>` also forwards your instruction to the model in the same step.
- **Missions with real isolation.** Every mission gets its own branch and Git worktree; workers never touch your checkout.
- **Review-gated merges.** A reviewer bound to the current branch tip must submit a `clean` / `merge` verdict; the merge gate re-checks scope, staleness, task completion, review history, and worktree ownership before a `--no-ff` merge.

- Git (worktrees are created locally; no network access is required)

|---|---|

| `index.js`, `lib/`, `worker.js` | Host entry, protocol implementation, worker preset policy |
| `locale/`, `icon.svg` | localization and icon |

| `ui-bundle/` | optional Client widget (static `/tower` hint), not installed by default |
| `.github/workflows/test.yml` | CI running the offline suite on Node 22/24 |


# Tower UI (optional Client widget, unverified)

An **optional** Web Client widget that shows a static `/tower` hint in the composer dock. It does not read the live Tower-mode state from the Host.

## Why it is not installed by default

- The Client half targets `conversation.composer.dock`, whose slot API and props have not been verified against a live page in this repository's test setup. Installing an unverified Client bundle can affect the Web UI.
- It is therefore a separate bundle from `dsh-tower` and does not affect installing or running the Host plugin.

## Install

```text
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "<absolute path to this ui-bundle>" })
```

Before installing, confirm in a test-enabled DSH session:

1. The `conversation.composer.dock` slot still exists (`Slots.listSubTree`).
2. `ctx.slots.register` still accepts the options and component signature used in `client.js`.
3. The hint appears in the composer area with no console errors, and disappears after the bundle is removed.

## Known limitations

- No live mode state (there is no Host → Client remote channel).
- A hint only, not a control; mode changes still go through the `/tower` command.

# 按需规划模式介绍

## 1. 一句话概述

**作者从reasonix得到的灵感，实现权限控制+子代理角色分配的agent模板**

**兼容性**：DSH = v0.2.1-rc.2、qqbot 0.5.0(暂未测试)。旧版本兼容详见Releases

## 2. 核心优势

通过设定 主会话、探查者、pro规划、执行者、验收者 五个角色，让DSH工作时按照明确的流程进行分工
  - 主会话：作为与用户直接交互的入口，负责日常沟通、需求接收与任务分派。它是整个工作流的发起者和协调者，确保用户意图被准确传达
  - 探查者：承担后台批量数据探查与线索回传工作。主动运行，将原始信息预处理后再转交主会话，有效避免主会话上下文过载，保持对话轻量与高效
  - pro规划：调用高级模型对用户需求进行深度分析与结构化规划，输出包含实施方案和验收标准的正式文档。为后续执行与验收提供权威依据
  - 执行者：严格按照规划方案进行机械式执行，并在每一步操作中持续对照验收文档，确保过程与预期一致，最大限度降低人为偏差
  - 验收者：严格按照验收方案进行机械式执行，确保最终交付物完全符合既定质量要求

并合并了DSH Agent预设模式中的 PTC模式、创造模式 包含的功能，可以直接在本模式同时体验
  - PTC模式：将多个工具调用合并为一次执行，大幅减少与模型的交互轮次，显著降低了重复传输的冗余开销。手动切换开关
  - 创造模式：创建自定义Agent preset时自动遵守DSH规范。手动切换开关

## 3. 安装及卸载方式（面向 DSH 环境用户）

### 核心安装

1. dsh web - 插件 - 添加插件 - https://github.com/luca3xxvsoo/dsh-extra-plan#path:/plugins/dsh-extra-plan 或 [解压路径]/dsh-extra-plan-main/plugins/dsh-extra-plan - 允许脚本并重试 - 立即启用
2. **重启 DSH 进程**使插件生效
3. 新建会话，在预设列表中选择「按需规划模式」

### qqbot兼容插件安装

1. 安装
```powershell 7+ 在线
$repo='luca3xxvsoo/dsh-extra-plan'; $q="$repo#path:/plugins/dsh-extra-plan-qqbot"; $allow='dsh-extra-plan-qqbot@git+https://github.com/luca3xxvsoo/dsh-extra-plan.git'; dsh plugin --profile qqbot add $q --allow-build="$allow"; $exitCode=$LASTEXITCODE; if($exitCode -ne 0){dsh plugin --profile qqbot approve-builds --all; dsh plugin --profile qqbot add $q --allow-build="$allow"; $exitCode=$LASTEXITCODE}; if($exitCode -eq 0){dsh plugin --profile qqbot approve-builds --all; if($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0){$profileDir=Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.dsh\profiles\qqbot'; Push-Location $profileDir; try { node -e "const fs=require('node:fs'),p='package.json';if(!fs.existsSync('node_modules/dsh-extra-plan'))throw new Error('缺少 qqbot 到 web 的 dsh-extra-plan 链接');const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8'));j.dsh=j.dsh||{};j.dsh.profile=j.dsh.profile||{};const b=j.dsh.profile.bundles=Array.isArray(j.dsh.profile.bundles)?j.dsh.profile.bundles:[];let changed=false;for(const n of ['dsh-extra-plan-qqbot','dsh-extra-plan'])if(!b.includes(n)){b.push(n);changed=true};if(changed){fs.copyFileSync(p,p+'.bak');fs.writeFileSync(p,JSON.stringify(j,null,2)+'\n')}" ; $nodeExit=$LASTEXITCODE } finally { Pop-Location }; if($nodeExit -eq 0){Write-Host '完整安装并激活成功，请重启 QQBot'}else{Write-Error 'bundle 激活失败'}}}else{Write-Error '插件安装失败'}
```
或

## 4. 可配置项

DSH web界面 -> 插件 -> 按需规划模式配置

**通用设置**：
  - anchored开关：首轮极简工具 + 提示词
  - 创造模式开关：是否开启dsh官方创造模式
  - web_fetch开关：是否开启web_fetch
  - 工具呈现模式：工具呈现方式切换（默认/PTC模式）
  - run_code 容错检查：PTC模式下，增加每个工具调用需要try catch的闸门。通过限制+建议的模式保障仅单个调用报错

**pro规划**：
  - 跨提供方：允许跨提供方选择模型。开启时将以 其他提供方 - 主会话提供方 - deepseek官方 的顺序，获取可用模型。关闭时仅从主会话提供方获取。默认关闭
  - pro规划 | 使用模型：pro规划默认使用模型。未匹配/置空时：使用主会话模型
  - pro规划 | 额外引导：在主会话发送给pro规划的任务结尾，拼接上的内容。可能能增加pro规划的智商（未验证）。可置空
  - pro规划 | 探查额度：允许pro规划调用工具的次数，避免后台无限制调用。同时限制一次runcode内可调用的工具上限数
  - 其他子代理 | 使用模型：其他子代理默认使用模型。未匹配/置空时：使用主会话模型

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# 幸运方块 (dsh-lucky-block)

一个 dsh 插件，同时工作在 dsh web 与 dsh desktop。两件事：

1. **幸运方块选项** —— AI 向你提选择题时，每个问题的选项末尾会自动多出一个「幸运方块」。
   选它，就随机替你挑一个选项、或把几个选项揉成一个新方案，全随机。
   不满意？说一句「回滚」（或打 `/rollback`），立刻回到上一版本。
2. **幸运方块按钮** —— 屏幕角落一个可拖动、可锁定的我的世界幸运方块（16×16 原版方块面贴图）。
   不知道干啥时**长按**它 1.4 秒：方块裂纹满布、碎成像素碎片，**耳边是原版 Minecraft 的敲石头声**，
   接着它会在你的默认工作区自动开一个新会话，**全程不需要你做任何事**地随机干一件事。
   松手时方块若离屏幕边缘够近（48px 以内）会**自动吸附贴边**。

它会说话。所有随机事件都套着一层固定的说话腔调：短句、机器口吻、偶尔损你一句。
这套腔调是纯文本的，参数在 `lib/persona.js` 的 `DEFAULT_PERSONA` 里，
可以用配置里的 `persona` 整段换成你自己写的性格。
它**从不往会话里写东西**，所以绝不会污染你的对话历史。

## 骰子事件一览（共 9 个，按权重随机）

| 概率 | 事件 | 类型 | 会做什么 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16.0% | 随机冷知识闲聊 | AI | 随机抽一种闲聊口味（冷知识 / 硬核概念比喻 / 微型科幻 / 生活技巧 / 造个伪学科 / 假新闻），300 字内写完 |
| 12.0% | 时事新闻速览 | AI | **联网**检索 3 条最近真实新闻，每条一句事实 + 一句点评 + 来源链接；查不到就直说，绝不编 |
| 12.0% | 随机选题写论文 | AI | 随机词条拼出题目（如「边缘计算 × 古籍数字化 × 的鲁棒性研究」），写 4 节正文并落盘到 `lucky-block-papers/<hash>.md` |
| 12.0% | 我的世界概念合成 | AI | 随机抽两个 Minecraft 概念（红石比较器、潜影盒、雪傀儡……），按一张随机「合成表」模板把它们揉成一个新东西 |
| 12.0% | 冷笑话专场 | AI | 抽一条随机的笑话结构（谐音 / 荒谬逻辑 / 反向解读 / 机器视角 / 逻辑错位……）现编一个，讲完解释笑点为什么成立 |
| 12.0% | 抽今日运气 | 本地 | 抽一档签文：鸿运齐天 / 大吉 / 中吉 / 小吉 / 平 / 凶。**不调 AI**，附「无科学依据，仅供参考」 |
| 8.0% | 无害弹窗表演 | 视觉 | 界面上连弹 24 个无意义提示框，再按创建顺序倒序全部关掉 |
| 8.0% | 蓝屏屏保（60 秒） | 视觉 | 全屏显示一份仿 Windows 蓝屏，60 秒后自动恢复，按 ESC 提前结束 |
| 8.0% | 随机整理待办 | AI | 列出工作区最近改的 5 个文件，随机分「紧急 / 不紧急」并明说自己不可信 |

**视觉类（弹窗 / 蓝屏）与「抽今日运气」完全不建会话、不调 AI、零 token、零延迟** ——
点下去立刻有反应。剩下 6 个才会开新会话。

「抽今日运气」的签文权重是刻意偏吉的：**吉类合计 90%**（鸿运齐天 5% / 大吉 26% /
中吉 33% / 小吉 26%），平 9.9%，凶只有 **0.1%**；
而且**「凶」的正文是反着写的**（「从某种角度来说，你运气还挺好 —— 今天该踩的坑都提前踩完了」），
抽到下签也能笑一下。这个插件是用来打发时间的，不是用来给人添堵的。

清单可用 `node tools/list-events.mjs` 随时重新生成 —— 它直接从 `lib/index.js`
的 `buildEvents()` 里解析，不会和代码漂移。

## 设置面板（右键方块 → 设置…）

| 开关 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| 长按挖掘音效 | 循环挖掘声 + 碎裂声。关掉就完全静音 |
| 逐事件「不调用 AI」 | 勾中的事件直接从本地语料库取内容，零 token、瞬时返回 |

只有**自带本地库**的事件会出现勾选框，目前是「随机冷知识闲聊」和「冷笑话专场」：

| 本地库 | 条数 | 位置 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 冷笑话 + 点评 | 353 条 + 30 条 | `lib/jokes-data.json` |
| 冷知识 | 818 条（人体 133 / 动物 139 / 科学 121 / 日常 111 / 历史 111 / 地理 103 / 语言 100） | `lib/trivia-data.json` |

冷知识库里分主题存的 `topic` **只用于统计，永远不显示给用户** —— 显示主题等于
把「这是一条从哪抽的」直接摊开。笑话的 `form` 字段同理。

两个库的**完整内容**可以在 [`lib/语料库总览.md`](<lib/语料库总览.md>) 里逐条翻阅；
那份文件由 `node tools/build-corpus-overview.mjs` 从运行库生成，改动语料后重跑即可
（`--check` 用于回归时校验它没过期）。

「时事新闻速览」必须联网，写进配置也会被忽略并记一条警告 —— 它没有本地库可退。

设置写在 `%DSH_HOME%\plugins\dsh-lucky-block\config.json`，是**手写与界面共用的同一个文件**
（界面保存走读-改-写，不会抹掉你手写的 `model` / `persona`）：

```json
{
  "sound": true,
  "localOnly": ["joke", "trivia"],
  "model": { "provider": "workbuddy", "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash", "reasoningEffort": "low" }
}
```

## 安装（本地开发）

```bash
# 方式一：直接指向本目录（plugin-manager 支持本地 spec）
#   在插件市场里「安装」填本目录的绝对路径

# 方式二：npm 打包后按包装
npm pack
```

装完后**不需要**动 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`：宿主侧条目由本包
`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 自动插入，profile 的 patch 里再加一条同 id 的
`- insert:` 反而会造成组装冲突、让插件加载不上（实测踩过）。

只要确认 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里有
`"dsh-lucky-block"`（插件市场安装会自动加；手动装则加这一行）。

`"patchReload": "live"`（profile 自带）让 `cordis.patch.yml` 热生效；但**改动
`bundles` 列表必须重启 dsh**才生效。

> ⚠️ **改 `lib/` 下的任何 JS 都必须重启 dsh。** 宿主侧插件代码没有热重载 ——
> 正在跑的进程内存里持有旧模块，代码改了行为不会变。这个坑骗过一整轮排查：
> 源码里已经搜不到某段字符串，会话里却还在出现它，最后才发现是进程跑的是旧代码。
> 客户端那半（`lib/client.js`）刷新页面即可，但桌面端要重启宿主才会重新收集注入行。

## 可选配置：给骰子会话单独指定模型

**默认不启用**，骰子会话直接沿用你的默认模型。想让随机事件跑便宜/快的模型时，
在 `%DSH_HOME%\plugins\dsh-lucky-block\config.json` 写（这个字段只能手写，设置面板里没有）：

```json
{
  "model": {
    "provider": "workbuddy",
    "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash",
    "reasoningEffort": "low"
  }
}
```

`reasoningEffort` 可省略。`provider` / `model` 必须**精确匹配**可用目录里的名字
（目录拿不到时会跳过切换、不影响掷骰子），不确定就先用 `/dice` 命令观察日志。

> ⚠️ **为什么默认关着**：宿主只提供会话级 `sessionController.selectModel`，而它
> 成功后会把这次选择**异步写成 profile 的全局默认模型**。也就是说开启本配置后，
> 第一次掷骰子会顺带把你的默认模型也改成这里写的那个。想恢复就把文件删掉，
> 再在界面里手动把默认模型选回来。

## 用法

| 想干什么 | 怎么做 |
| --- | --- |
| 让 AI 给选择题加幸运方块 | 正常提问，选项末尾自动多一项 |
| 抽一次 | **长按**幸运方块按钮（挖掘到碎裂）/ 打 `/dice` |
| 不满意，回去 | 说「回滚」或打 `/rollback` |
| 方块按钮固定住不挡路 | 右键方块 → 锁定（或双击）；锁定后仍可长按触发 |
| 让方块贴边 | 把它拖到离屏幕边缘 48px 以内松手，自动吸附 |
| 改设置 | 右键方块 → 设置… |

长按阈值 1.4 秒（`lib/client.js` 的 `BREAK_MS`）。按住时手指挪动超过 5 像素即判为
「在拖动按钮」并取消挖掘——所以拖位置和挖方块不会打架。松开或移开都会取消挖掘，
纹路和挖掘声**立刻**一起停。

音效从宿主的 `/dsh-lucky-block/sound/*.ogg` 按需取（16 个原版音节，共 142 KB），
**不内联进客户端 bundle** —— `lib/client.js` 是每次页面启动都要下载的入口，
为只在长按瞬间才用到的音效把它撑大 4 倍不划算。挖掘声每 210ms 一个、4 个变体随机轮播
（只听一个会明显「卡带」），挖穿那一刻再叠一声碎裂音；同时最多 6 个 Audio 元素，
页面切到后台自动静音。

松手吸附（`SNAP_THRESHOLD = 48`）只在**真的拖动过**时生效：鼠标只是滑出方块边缘
（会触发 `pointerleave`）不会吸附，按下就松手也不会。锁定状态下完全不吸附 —— 锁定
就是不建拖动状态，自然短路。吸附有 160ms 的 `left/top` 过渡，视觉上是滑过去而不是瞬移。

方块按钮位置与锁定状态存在浏览器 localStorage（键 `dshLuckyBlock.block`），换机器不跟。

## 出错了怎么看

方块头顶的气泡**只在报错时出现**（正常触发的进度、成功、会话 ID 都不写了 ——
有视觉表演的事件自己会演，没表演的由新会话内容承担反馈）。报错时气泡里是宿主
翻译过的**人话**，点一下可以关掉，例如：

| 情况 | 气泡说什么 |
| --- | --- |
| 插件本体没激活（改动 `lib/` 后没重启） | 插件没有注册这个接口，通常是插件本体未激活：重启 dsh 后再试 |
| 登录态过期 | 宿主拒绝了请求（未登录或登录已过期），刷新页面后重试 |
| 默认工作区被删/移走 | 默认工作区目录不存在或已被移动。请在 dsh 里重新确认默认工作区路径后再试 |
| 工作区不可写 | 没有权限写入工作区（被系统或沙箱拦下了） |
| `config.json` 里的模型不在目录里 | 模型不可用：config.json 里指定的 provider/model 不在可用目录中 |
| 都不是 | 意外错误：<宿主的原始信息> |

想看完整堆栈就翻宿主日志（`dsh` 标准输出）——那边始终打的是原始错误。

> 音效**不会**报错。拿不到音效文件、浏览器拦截自动播放、没有可用音频设备 ——
> 这些一律静默忽略。音效是锦上添花，为它弹一个红色报错气泡是本末倒置。

## 目录

- `lib/index.js` —— 宿主侧（Node）：选项注入、答案识别、回滚、幸运方块事件、默认工作区会话创建、可选模型切换、人格层与状态机、本地语料库分流、设置读写、音效文件投放、错误翻译。
- `lib/client.js` —— 客户端（浏览器）：可拖拽幸运方块按钮（含边缘吸附、锁定）+ 长按挖掘裂纹 / 碎裂粒子 / 音效 + 弹窗表演 + 蓝屏屏保 + 设置面板 + 台词气泡。
- `lib/persona.js` —— 随机事件的人格层（纯函数，可单测）：默认人格、覆盖合并、人格段拼装、任务正文保护、收尾点评请求。
- `lib/jokes.js` —— 本地笑话库加载器（读 `jokes-data.json`，带 BOM 剥离与只读一次缓存）。
- `lib/jokes-data.json` / `lib/trivia-data.json` —— 本地语料库。
- `lib/sounds/` —— 16 个原版 Minecraft 音效（`.ogg`，共 142 KB），由宿主按需投放。
- `cordis.patch.yml` —— 把宿主侧插件插进插件树（客户端那半由 `package.json` 的 `dsh.client` 自动加载）。

## 素材出处

方块面与裂纹是原版 Minecraft 像素素材，以 base64 data URI 内联在 `lib/client.js` 里
（静态 bundle 的 `require()` 只认包 id、不认相对路径，所以不做成独立模块）：

| 素材 | 尺寸 | 来源 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 方块面 | 16×16 | `alexsocha/luckyblock` mod 的 `lucky_block.png` |
| 挖掘裂纹 10 帧 | 16×16 ×10 | 原版资源包 `PixiGeko/Minecraft-default-assets` 的 `assets/minecraft/textures/block/destroy_stage_0..9.png` |

裂纹用 `image-rendering: pixelated` 保持硬边，长按时按进度切到下一帧，最后一帧之后碎裂。
之所以找原素材而不是手绘：手绘的裂纹再怎么调都像程序生成的线条，和那张像素方块贴图
放在一起会突兀；换成原版的黑褐裂纹 + 白色反光碎屑，才是游戏里挖方块的样子。

音效是 Minecraft 1.20.1 原版 assets（`dig/stone1..4.ogg`、`random/break.ogg`），
经 `tools/build-sounds.mjs` 从 mcasset.cloud 镜像取到 `lib/sounds/`。版权归 Mojang Studios；
本插件只作本地开发期素材镜像，**运行时不依赖网络**。

默认性格是机器客服口吻 + 音量梗 + 人体数据冷知识，靠语气和句式传达。
实现里刻意**不提任何作品名、角色名或制造商**，也不靠名字塑造性格 ——
`persona-check.mjs` 有多条断言盯着这一点。

开发期工具（`tools/`，安装运行不依赖）：
`host-smoke.mjs` 跑宿主侧回归（含音效路由与白名单）、
`persona-check.mjs` 人格层单测（真 import）、
`snap-check.mjs` 吸附纯函数（从 `client.js` 抽源码跑，不会与实现漂移）、
`config-check.mjs` 配置读取（含 BOM 坑）、
`local-check.mjs` 本地语料库与分流、
`verify-sounds.mjs` 音效文件 ↔ 客户端清单 ↔ 宿主白名单三方一致性、
`list-events.mjs` 打印事件清单与概率、
`merge-trivia.mjs` / `merge-jokes.mjs` 语料合并器（`--check` 只体检不写盘）、
`build-corpus-overview.mjs` 重新生成 `lib/语料库总览.md`（`--check` 校验是否过期）、
`build-sounds.mjs` 把原版音效取到 `lib/sounds/`。

端到端探针（需要先起克隆 profile，流程见 `docs/探针流程.md`）：
`probe-sound.mjs`、`probe-settings.mjs`、`probe-visual-ids.mjs`、
`probe-persona.mjs`、`probe-flip.mjs`、`probe-flip-prompt.mjs`、
`probe-local-path.mjs`、`probe-fortune.mjs`。

调研笔记与语料候选文件归档在 `docs/research-notes/`（考据报告、语料来源、
合并器的候选 JSON）。

## 已知边界

- 回滚是「fork 到上一版本」：历史会话保留，新分支继续，不会删任何东西。
- 幸运方块开出来的会话不回滚（随机剧本被回滚会变得没意义）。
- 蓝屏屏保只盖 dsh 自己的窗口，不碰系统、不碰其他插件，60 秒或按 ESC 结束。
- 方块按钮用 pointer 事件实现长按，鼠标左键/触摸都行；键盘 Tab 聚焦后 Enter/Space 直接触发（跳过挖掘动画）。
- 挖掘裂纹用原版 `destroy_stage` 10 帧贴图（透明底），方块碎裂是纯 DOM 的一次白光闪 + 26 个像素碎片；都不受用户主题影响。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-comfyui-web 在 dsh 里直接使用 ComfyUI，让 AI 通过 MCP 操作当前工作流。改提示词、调参数、运行生图，节点变化和生成预览都在同一个页面里看得见。 ## 安装 需要已安装的 [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)、pnpm 和本机 ComfyUI。当前适配 dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`，Node.js 22 及以上。 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:mangfufu/dsh-comfyui-web ```
首次安装时，填写 ComfyUI 前端目录 创建或编辑 `~/.dsh/comfyui/config.json`，将示例中的前端目录替换为本机实际路径。Windows 的 `~` 是用户目录；Linux 同样填写实际路径。 ```json { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8188", "frontendExtensionsDir": "D:/ComfyUI/python/Lib/site-packages/comfyui_frontend_package/static/extensions" } ``` 首次安装或更新后，先保存工作流，再刷新已打开的 ComfyUI 原网页和 dsh 内的面板。 目录未配置或写入失败时，面板的 **MCP 设置**和 dsh 启动日志会提示原因。能看到 ComfyUI 网页，还需等到 **MCP · 共享画布已连接** 才能让 AI 操作。
Docker / WSL 中的 ComfyUI 推荐使用已经持久化挂载的 `custom_nodes` 目录。编辑运行 dsh 的系统中的 `~/.dsh/comfyui/config.json`： ```json { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8188", "customNodesDir": "/mnt/data/ai/comfyui/storage-nodes/custom_nodes" } ``` 上面是 Linux 路径示例。**dsh 在 Windows 运行时，应填写 Windows 能写入的路径**，例如 `D:/ComfyUI/custom_nodes`，或实际 WSL 发行版的共享目录 `//wsl.localhost/Ubuntu/mnt/data/ai/comfyui/storage-nodes/custom_nodes`。 确认对应宿主目录已挂载到容器的 `custom_nodes`，例如： ```yaml volumes: - /mnt/data/ai/comfyui/storage-nodes/custom_nodes:/root/ComfyUI/custom_nodes ``` 启动 dsh 后会生成 `dsh-comfyui-bridge` 扩展。先保存工作流，再重启 ComfyUI、刷新 dsh 面板。扩展保存在挂载目录中，容器重建后仍保留。 `customNodesDir` 与 `frontendExtensionsDir` 二选一。如果沿用前端目录方式，目录同样必须是 **dsh 可写、容器可见** 的持久化挂载路径，不能直接填写容器内的 `/usr/local/...` 路径。 如果 Windows 无法直接访问挂载目录，也可在该目录手动创建 `dsh-comfyui-bridge/__init__.py`： ```python WEB_DIRECTORY = "./web" NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS = {} ``` 再将插件中的 `comfy-extension.js` 复制为 `dsh-comfyui-bridge/web/loader.js`，重启 ComfyUI。从 dsh 面板打开时会自动取得桥接地址，无需编辑脚本。手动安装完成并连接后，可忽略宿主的“尚未配置”日志提示。
## 使用 ### 1. 启动并打开 1. 先启动 ComfyUI。 2. 启动 `dsh web`，打开 `http://127.0.0.1:3080`。 3. 进入对话，点击右上角 **ComfyUI**。 ![ComfyUI 嵌入 dsh 右侧面板](docs/images/comfyui-panel.png) 左边聊需求，右边改节点、看预览。手动编辑和 AI 操作都落在当前工作流上。 ### 2. 确认连接地址 默认连接 `http://127.0.0.1:8188`。如果更换了端口，打开 **MCP 设置**，修改地址后点击 **保存并连接**。 ![连接地址与 MCP 开关](docs/images/comfyui-settings.png) MCP 默认开启，dsh 已自动接入。这里也能关闭 MCP，或复制配置给其他本机 AI 客户端使用。 ### 3. 让 AI 操作工作流 直接在当前对话里告诉 AI： > 读取当前工作流，优化正向提示词，保留现有模型和节点连接，生成一张图并查看效果。 ![AI 修改提示词并生成图片](docs/images/comfyui-ai-preview.png) 提示词直接写入当前节点，右侧查看生成预览，左侧查看出图结果。AI 做了哪些修改，画布上实时可见。 通过插件提交生成后，图片和视频会自动显示在发起任务的回复正文下方，不需要 AI 额外调用显示工具；收起工具过程后仍可查看。 多张图片同样按原比例显示，空间不够时自动换行，不会缩成小方块。 同一路图片同时接标准保存和 Preview 节点时，对话只展示保存版；不同分支的图片和只有 Preview 的结果仍正常展示。 已有历史结果也可以让 AI「用插件显示这个图片或视频」。 也可以直接说「列出工作流标签页，切换到 XXX」，或「复制当前工作流，另开一个叫测试的标签页」。已保存的工作流也能打开或复制，源工作流和未保存修改会保留。 更多操作直接在对话里说： - 「用我刚上传的参考图做图生图，填入图片节点。」 - 「加一个放大节点，接到输出前面。」 - 「保存当前工作流」，或「另存为视频测试」。另存遇到同名文件会提示换名称。 - 「列出修改快照，恢复到这次修改之前。」撤销、重做和快照在同一浏览器刷新后仍可使用；最多保留 20 份，实际数量受浏览器存储空间限制。 - 「查看我的生成任务，取消还没开始的那一个。」排队任务可按任务取消；中断正在生成的任务会影响整个实例当前生成。 生成完成会自动通知原对话，正在进行的回复不会被强行中断。 在 ComfyUI 手动停止后，AI 会收到“主动中断”通知；同一对话收到你的新消息前，插件会拦截再次提交。想继续时，明确告诉 AI「继续生成」。 极简预设也支持完成通知：缺少后台任务控制器时，插件会在当前会话内自动启用，无需手改配置。 插件重启会恢复原任务跟踪和结果；原对话的 AI 恢复运行后，会重新接上尚未送达的完成通知，不会重复提交生成。 想撤销就说「撤销刚才的修改」。界面大小用顶部 `− / +` 调整，点击 **刷新** 可重新加载 ComfyUI。 顶部 **图片对话中模糊** 开关默认关闭，同时适用于视频。开启后，点击模糊图先显示清晰图片，再点可查看大图；视频先解除模糊，再用播放按钮播放。鼠标悬停时，左上角的灰色小眼睛可切换模糊/清晰。关闭开关后，不出现模糊提示和小眼睛。只影响本插件返回到对话中的图片和视频，开关会记住。 ## 友情链接 [LINUX DO](https://linux.do/) · [插件介绍帖](https://linux.do/t/topic/3009797) ## Star History [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=mangfufu/dsh-comfyui-web&type=Date)](https://www.star-history.com/?repos=mangfufu%2Fdsh-comfyui-web&type=date)

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-llm-cli

Model routes for **DeepSeek Harness** served by **agent CLIs installed on the
host** instead of an HTTP provider API — plus a charted usage dashboard that
reads what those CLIs record about themselves.

[![CI](https://github.com/Mans230/dsh-llm-cli/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Mans230/dsh-llm-cli/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20.11-brightgreen.svg)](package.json)

| Route | CLI | Turn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opencode` | OpenCode CLI | `opencode run --model <m> --format json` |
| `grok` | Grok Build CLI | `grok -p <prompt> -m <m> --output-format streaming-json` |
| `codex` | OpenAI Codex CLI | `codex exec --json -m <m> <prompt>` |

Each CLI owns its own authentication and its own agent loop, so the adapter
declares a **text-only** stream: a turn on these routes is a finished answer from
that CLI. The CLI cannot call harness tools and cannot see harness files; it runs
in `config.cwd`.

## Requirements

- Node.js **20.11+** (the plugin itself has **no dependencies**; the peer
  `@deepseek-ai/*` packages come from the harness).
- At least one of the supported CLIs on the host, signed in:
  - OpenCode — `opencode` (the `opencode/*-free` model ids need no account)
  - Grok Build — `grok` (sign in with `grok login --device-auth`)
  - OpenAI Codex — `codex` (sign in with `codex login --device-auth`)

On Windows the plugin reads an npm `.cmd` shim and launches its real target
instead of handing the shim to a shell, so prompt text never reaches a command
line. A bare command name is looked up on `PATH` with `PATHEXT`, which is how a
globally installed CLI that ships only a shim stays reachable.

## Install

The package is a plugin **bundle**: `package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.patch` (the bundled `cordis.patch.yml`, which mounts the host plugin)
and `dsh.client.platform: web` (the browser half at `./client`, discovered from
the manifest).

Wire it into a profile by adding it as a dependency and selecting its bundle:

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "dsh-llm-cli": "git+https://github.com/Mans230/dsh-llm-cli.git" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["dsh-llm-cli"] } }
}
```

Use the `git+https` form rather than the `github:` shorthand. npm resolves the
shorthand over SSH, which fails on a host with no GitHub key even though the
repository is public. The update button retries over https when the shorthand
fails, but starting from https avoids the round trip.

or, in the Web UI, **Plugins → Add plugin** with this package's path. See
[MOUNT-EXAMPLE.md](MOUNT-EXAMPLE.md) for the junction-based local install.

## Configuration

The bundle mounts the entry with defaults; a profile patch overrides it by `id`:

```yaml
- id: llm-cli
  config:
    cwd: '/path/to/agent/workspace'
    usageFile: '/path/to/.dsh/llm-cli-usage.json'
    # Optional "usage plan" gauges. The CLIs publish no quota for Grok/OpenCode,
    # so a budget gauge is only drawn against numbers you set here; without them
    # the dashboard shows plain measured usage. `resetDay` is the day of month
    # the period starts on (1-28).
    plan:
      grok:
        # The grok.com "Weekly Premium Limit" (the CLI exposes it only behind a
        # private RPC, so copy it here): used percent + reset time.
        weeklyPremium:
          usedPercent: 1
          resetAt: '2026-10-23T15:13:00Z'
        monthlyBudgetUsd: 20
        resetDay: 1
      opencode:
        monthlyBudgetTokens: 100000000
        resetDay: 1
    providers:
      opencode:
        models: [opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free]
      codex: {}
      grok: {}
```

- `cwd` — where the CLI agent runs a turn.
- `usageFile` — the usage ledger (JSON). Counts only: never prompt or reply text.
  Writes take a lock and merge with what is on disk, so two profiles can share
  one file without losing each other's turns.
- `providers.<id>` — `false`/`{enabled:false}` to disable a route; `models` to
  offer an explicit list (otherwise whatever the CLI lists); `bin`,
  `defaultModel`, `displayName`, `contextWindow` to override.
- `timeoutMs` — per-turn timeout.
- `plan.<route>` — optional monthly budget for the dashboard gauges:
  `monthlyBudgetUsd`, `monthlyBudgetTokens` and `resetDay`.
- `grokUsageDir` — where the Grok CLI keeps its session stores (default
  `~/.grok/sessions`); the dashboard sums the per-session `usage.json` files.
- `codexUsageDir` — where the Codex CLI keeps its session rollouts (default
  `~/.codex/sessions`); the dashboard reads the newest rate-limit and token
  snapshot from them.
- `codexModelsCache` — Codex's own model catalog (default
  `~/.codex/models_cache.json`); the route offers the entries it marks `list`
  (pin `providers.codex.models` to override).
- `opencodeStats.args` — override the `opencode stats` arguments the dashboard
  runs (default `stats --json --all --models --cost`).
- `includeSystemPrompt` — also forward the harness system prompt to the CLI.
- `dashboardToken` — required for a dashboard request from another machine.
  Loopback needs no token. A token shorter than 16 characters does not count as
  configured, so a stray `token=1` cannot unlock remote reads.
- `signInTtlMs` — how long a device-code sign-in may wait for a human before the
  plugin closes it (default 10 minutes).
- `autoUpdate` — `false` (default) makes no network calls. `'check'` looks for a
  newer published version on a timer, `'apply'` installs it too.
- `updateIntervalMs` — how often an auto-updating install checks (default 24
  hours, minimum one minute).
- `updateSource` — the URL the check reads a `package.json` from (default this
  repository's copy on `main`).
- `updateInstall` — `{ method: 'npm'|'git', dir, spec }` for a copy whose install
  the plugin cannot work out by itself.

## What it adds

- The three route groups in the model picker.
- `provider_signin` / `provider_signin_status` tools, and an automatic
  device-code error when a route's CLI is signed out.
- `/llm-cli/usage` (HTML) and `/llm-cli/usage.json` (JSON) on the harness's own
  web server, backed by the ledger and the CLIs' own usage. A `?days=`/`?hours=`
  query (or the on-page 5h/7d/30d/90d/all buttons) scopes the charts to a
  trailing window. The two endpoints answer this machine only; another host
  needs `dashboardToken`, presented as `?token=`, an `x-llm-cli-token` header,
  or the `llm_cli_token` cookie the page sets from a query token.
- The plugin's page in **two places** in the Web client, both rendering the same
  charted dashboard:
  - **Plugins → Grok + Codex + OpenCode (CLI)** (`client.js`, slot
    `plugins.item`), and
  - **Settings → LLM usage** (slot `settings.section`).

  Each shows every route and model with the limits its CLI publishes, plus
  charts: daily tokens per CLI, an activity heatmap and token mix, cost by model,
  per-model usage tables, the real Codex 5-hour and weekly subscription-limit
  gauges, and — when `plan` budgets or `plan.grok.weeklyPremium` are configured —
  used-vs-budget gauges. It also carries a **Check for updates** button and, when
  a newer version exists, **Update now**.
- `GET /llm-cli/update.json` and `POST /llm-cli/update` for the same two actions
  from the server-rendered page. Both answer this machine only, and the POST
  needs the action token the page or the JSON carries. The POST runs `npm install
  <the spec your profile declares>` for a dependency install, or `git pull
  --ff-only` in the checkout for a git install. **A restart of the profile is
  what loads the new code**, so the update reports `restartRequired` rather than
  pretending the running process changed.

## Usage data sources

Two independent usage views are shown, and they answer different questions:

- **This harness** — the turns *this* DSH instance recorded, from the ledger.
- **CLI-recorded** — what each CLI accounts for itself, including sessions
  started outside this harness:
  - **Grok** — the CLI persists per-session token and cost accounting at
    `~/.grok/sessions/<workspace>/<sessionId>/usage.json`; the dashboard sums
    those files (per model, per day, per session). Cost is stored as ticks of
    `1e-10` USD. The CLI writes that file when it runs a session itself, so a
    host with no CLI-run session yet reports the view as unavailable instead of
    showing zero.
  - **OpenCode** — the dashboard runs `opencode stats --json --all --models
    --cost` (cached) for lifetime totals, per-model usage and a daily activity
    series.
  - **Codex** — the CLI writes a rollout per session under
    `~/.codex/sessions/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/rollout-*.jsonl`; the dashboard reads the
    newest `token_count` event for cumulative tokens per model and the account
    `rate_limits` (a **5-hour** `primary` window and a **weekly** `secondary`
    window, each with a real used-percentage and reset time).

Each CLI is read from the source that suits it, and every view carries
`available`, `source`, `note` and `capabilities`. A figure a CLI does not report
is a dash, not a zero. Codex cost is always a dash. Only OpenCode reports usage
per agent step, so only its turns sum their steps.

The two views can split the same total differently. Grok's session file counts
cached input inside `inputTokens`, while the turn's own usage event reports it
separately, so one turn reads as 16,404 input in the CLI view and 14,740 input
plus 1,664 cache reads in the ledger. Both add up to 17,492.

Each view also carries `mix`, three slices that add up to its own `totalTokens`,
built where the CLI's counting rule is known: OpenCode counts cache beside
input, Grok and Codex count it inside. Reasoning is reported separately and is
named under the chart rather than drawn as a slice.

`opencode stats --days` takes whole days, so a sub-day window is served at one
day. That view carries `scopeDays` and the page says so, instead of a `5h` label
covering a day of data.

## What each CLI can and cannot report

- **Grok** — caches its model catalog at `~/.grok/models_cache.json`
  (`context_window`, `context_windows`, `max_completion_tokens`); the plugin reads
  it and also hands the context window to DSH. For usage it persists real
  per-session token and cost accounting — but it exposes **no subscription
  quota** (the weekly premium limit shown on grok.com is fetched only behind a
  private auth RPC), so the Grok weekly gauge uses `plan.grok.weeklyPremium` (or a
  `~/.grok/subscription.json` snapshot, if one exists).
- **Codex** — records its own usage **and its real subscription limits**: the
  dashboard shows the 5-hour and weekly used-percentages and reset times straight
  from the rollout files, plus the context window from the same turn. Codex has
  no `models` listing command, so the route reads its own catalog.
- **OpenCode** — prints model ids only; those rows say so and use the harness
  default window. The `opencode/*-free` ids need no account; `magpie/*` ids need
  an authenticated OpenCode account.

## Development

```bash
npm test        # runs every test/*.test.mjs in its own process
```

The suite has **no dependencies and makes no network calls**: it drives stub CLIs
(`test/stubs/stub-cli.mjs`) that emit the exact JSON shapes the CLIs emit, and it
builds synthetic Codex rollouts for the usage reader.

| Suite | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `test/adapter.test.mjs` | route registration, the Codex catalog reader, a `codex exec --json` turn |
| `test/ledger.test.mjs` | a successful and a failed turn, and the usage ledger |
| `test/signin.test.mjs` | device-code parsing, `SignInManager`, the auto sign-in error |
| `test/usage.test.mjs` | Codex rollout reading (tokens, models, days, 5h/weekly limits) and windowing |
| `test/client.test.mjs` | the browser half rendered against a real payload, and the update button's gate and both outcomes |
| `test/failures.test.mjs` | CLI error events, timeouts, plain-text answers, a bad `cwd`, block indices |
| `test/views.test.mjs` | per-CLI usage rules (step summing, single totals), capabilities, dashes |
| `test/dashboard.test.mjs` | dashboard authorization (loopback, token, cookie), the page refresh, and the recent-turn cells |
| `test/update.test.mjs` | version compare, install detection, a real local git pull, a stub npm |
| `test/contract.test.mjs` | the manifest and both halves' public exports |

Every test mount passes its own scratch ledger path; most use
`test/_harness.mjs`. A test run therefore never writes into the ledger of a
profile that is running the plugin.

`node test/_audit.mjs probes`, `suites` and `mutations` run the extended audit
checks. `real` reads host usage and runs one real turn per CLI; `real-sanity`
cross-checks the source files and runs a raw Codex turn; `clone` downloads and
tests `origin/main`. Those modes intentionally use host data or the network.
Logs are written under the system temporary directory in
`dsh-llm-cli-audit-20261017` (override with `AUDIT_DIR`). Run `real` before
`probes` to provide its dashboard snapshot. All audit mounts isolate their ledger
and assert the live ledger remains absent. They refuse to run if it exists.

CI runs the syntax check and the suite on Node 20, 22 and 24
([`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml)).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-enter-keymap

[![ci](https://github.com/MeadalFlute/dsh-enter-keymap/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MeadalFlute/dsh-enter-keymap/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

给 DSH Web GUI 换一套编写器键位：**Enter 换行 · Ctrl+Enter 发送 · Shift+Enter 插队发送**。
可在 **设置 → 通用 → 编写器键位** 里随时开关，关掉即刻恢复 DSH 原生键位。

| 按键 | 行为 |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` | 在草稿里换行（不再直接发送） |
| `Ctrl` / `Cmd` + `Enter` | 发送。完全沿用 DSH 原生语义：空闲时直接发送；Agent 忙且队列非空时按 DSH 的加速手势插队 |
| `Shift` + `Enter` | 插队发送。等价于按 `Ctrl`/`Cmd` + `Enter`：忙时 steer（把队列里的消息插进当前回合），空闲时就是普通发送 |
| `Alt` + `Enter`、输入法组合中的回车、`/` `@` 菜单打开时的回车 | 一律放行，保持 DSH 原生行为 |

## 安装

走官方插件通道（会自动登记 profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 并插入 Loader 行，无需手改任何 profile 文件）：

```sh
# 从 GitHub 装
dsh plugin --profile web add github:MeadalFlute/dsh-enter-keymap

# 或从 npm 装
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-enter-keymap
```

装完**重启 DSH 实例**（Host 只在启动时扫描一次 Loader 条目），然后整页刷新。
卸载：`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-enter-keymap`，同样重启。

> 本机（DSH Launcher 布局）实测 `dsh plugin` 会因 pnpm store 探测失败报
> `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE`；那种情况下手工等价安装见文末「本地开发装法」。

## 为什么会有这个插件

DSH 自带 **设置 → 通用 → Composer Enter**（`ui-conversation.busyEnter`），但它只决定
「Agent 忙时普通 Enter 是排队还是插队」，**改不了「Enter 到底发不发送」**——原生 Enter 永远直接发送。
社区另有一个 [SA1992X/dsh-ctrl-enter-submit](https://github.com/SA1992X/dsh-ctrl-enter-submit)（MIT），
它实现了「Enter 换行 + Ctrl+Enter 发送」，但明确**不支持** Shift+Enter（它的注释写着
「Shift+Enter 不是提交，DSH 键位表把带 shift 的 Enter 当作换行」）。
本插件在同样的思路上补上了 Shift+Enter 插队，并加了设置开关。

## 实现原理

DSH 0.1.6-alpha.2 的编写器是 Lexical 编辑器，键位注册在 `KEY_ENTER_COMMAND` 上，处理顺序是：

```
if (event.shiftKey === true) return false          // 交给 Lexical 插入换行
if (isComposing(event)) return true                // 输入法组合中
if (arbitrate('enter') !== 'pass') return true     // 菜单拦截
event.preventDefault()
if (!canSubmit()) return true
submit(event.ctrlKey === true || event.metaKey === true)   // accelerated = Ctrl/Cmd
```

于是：

1. **Enter → 换行**：只要把事件对象的 `shiftKey` 读成 `true`，DSH 就会走换行分支，
   浏览器原生换行插入照常发生，编辑器再把它归一化进自己的模型。
   （`Object.defineProperty(event, 'shiftKey', { value: true })`，与 dsh-ctrl-enter-submit 在 0.1.2+ 上的做法一致。）
2. **Shift+Enter → 插队**：光改字段做不到（改 `shiftKey` 变换行、改 `ctrlKey` 又挡不住 Lexical 插换行）。
   所以拦下原事件（`preventDefault` + `stopImmediatePropagation`），再往同一个编辑器
   `dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: 'Enter', ctrlKey: true, bubbles: true, cancelable: true }))`
   —— composer 的 gate 处理器收到后会走 `accelerated` 分支：`canSteerQueue` 时 `steerQueue()`，
   否则 `submit(resolveSubmitMode(...))`。
   React 18 的事件委托挂在 `#root` 的捕获阶段，所以从编辑器元素派发、带 `bubbles` 的合成事件能被 composer 收到。
3. **监听位置**：挂在 `window` 的**捕获阶段**。事件传播是 `window → document → … → 编辑器`，
   因此一定早于 ui-conversation 挂在 `document` 上的捕获监听器和 React/Lexical 的监听器，
   不受客户端插件加载顺序影响。
4. **不越界**：只在 `[data-composer-card]` 内的可编辑元素上生效；Agent 提问卡片的输入框与选择按钮
   （`[data-question-key]`）一律不碰。

## 结构

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json` | 包声明：`main`（Host 半）、`./client`（浏览器半）、`dsh.client`、`dsh.bundle.patch` |
| `lib/index.js` | Host 半：向 settings 服务注册 namespace `enter-keymap` 与 schema，使开关持久化到 `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml` |
| `lib/client.js` | 浏览器半：`window` 捕获阶段键位拦截 + 「设置 → 通用」开关行（手写 bundle，出口为 `name`/`inject`/`apply`） |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | bundle patch：往 Loader 树插入 `enter-keymap` 行 |
| `test/keymap.test.mjs` | 键位路由 + 文案渲染单测（零依赖，直接 `node` 跑） |

## 自检

```sh
node test/keymap.test.mjs
```

18 条用例：12 条键位路由（Enter 换行、Ctrl/Cmd+Enter 放行、Shift+Enter 合成 Ctrl+Enter、
开关关闭、非 composer 目标、菜单打开、输入法组合、事件已被处理、非 Enter 键、导出形状），
外加 6 条文案渲染回归（字典注册、`label` 返回真实文案、设置行渲染不含原始 key、
说明只有一行不重复、双语 key 一一对应、关闭态文案）。

测试**零依赖**（自带极小断言壳，不需要 `npm install`），所以 CI 只做语法检查 + 跑这个脚本，
不装依赖也不构建：`lib/` 是手写的产物，仓库里提交什么，装上以后跑的就是什么。

## 说明与已知限制

- **文案用自己绑定的翻译函数**。DSH 的 locale 字典是**扁平的点号 key → 字符串**
  （`{"settings.enter.title": "…"}`），查找就是 `dicts[locale][key]` 一次取值：
  写成嵌套对象会永远查不到，`t()` 按设计回显 key，设置行就会显示成 `row.title`。
  所以这里用扁平表，并在 `apply` 里 `ctx.locale.bind('enter-keymap')` 自己绑定，
  以 `label` 这个自有 prop 名传进组件（组件闭包持有），避开 slot 宿主的 props 合成规则；
  回归用例会断言渲染结果里不出现 `row.title` 这类原始 key。
- Host 半是**必需**的：没有它，`ctx.settingsScope.bind()` 拿到的是 `unavailable` 快照，
  开关仍能在当前页面生效，但刷新后回到默认（已启用），不会写进 `settings.yaml`。
- Shift+Enter 在「Agent 忙但草稿为空」时，会像 DSH 的 Ctrl+Enter 一样**冲刷队列**（steer 队列里已有消息），
  而不是发送空消息 —— 这是 DSH 原生加速手势的语义，插件刻意保持一致。
- 验证环境为 DSH `0.1.6-alpha.2`。插件依赖三个客户端服务 `slots` / `locale` / `settingsScope`
  与 `settings.general.item` 槽位；`settingsScope` 是较新版本才有的，更老的 DSH 上设置行不会出现
  （键位拦截仍会工作）。
- 若 DSH 以后把 Shift+Enter 改成别的语义，或把 `busyEnter` 改成三态，本插件需要同步更新；
  拦截点全部集中在 `lib/client.js` 的 `routeEnter`，单测可直接覆盖改动。

## 本地开发装法

`dsh plugin` 不可用时，用 `scripts/install.mjs` 手工完成等价的三件事
（在 profile 的 `node_modules` 建 junction、登记 `link:` 依赖与 `dsh.profile.bundles`、
给插件自己建 `schemastery` junction —— Cordis 加载器 import 的是插件的真实路径，
Host 半的裸模块导入要从插件目录往上找）：

```sh
node scripts/install.mjs --profile web
```

测试与源码都在仓库里（npm 包的 `files` 只含 `lib` 与 patch，测试不进包）。

## 附：OpenCode Go 的 session 头（与本插件无关，但顺手留了材料）

同一个作者在排查 **OpenCode Go 要求 `x-opencode-session`** 的问题时做了抓包验证，
结论与复现脚本一并放在仓库里，跟本插件的键位功能互不影响：

- [`docs/opencode-session-header.md`](docs/opencode-session-header.md) —— 根因（含 pi-ai / dsh-llm

# dsh-session-manager

Agent tools and a loopback REST API for DSH session housekeeping — list, move across workspaces, delete with an optional backup, tag, archive and unarchive.

DSH's own GUI covers only part of this surface (it can archive, but not unarchive; it has no tags; cross-workspace moves need a restart). This plugin puts the whole surface on two rails that share one implementation:

- **Agent tools** — six tools the model can call directly.
- **Loopback REST API** — the same six operations over HTTP, so a browser plugin can drive them without an IPC bridge. [`dsh-session-tree`](https://github.com/minhaoli/dsh-session-tree) uses this to render tags, drag-and-drop and the archive menu in the sidebar.

## Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| DSH | `0.2.1-rc.2` (developed and tested against it) |
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `~4.0.5` |
| Runtime | Node.js 22+ (ships with the DSH desktop runtime) |

Earlier DSH releases are untested. The plugin reads `workspaceRegistry`, `sessionPersistence`, `storageDomain` and `webServer`; a release that renames or removes any of those will make the corresponding feature fail soft (logged as a warning) rather than crash the host.

## Install

```bash
# from git (recommended)
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add github:minhaoli/dsh-session-manager

# or from a local checkout
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add /absolute/path/to/dsh-session-manager
```

`<your-profile>` is the profile you actually boot — `desktop` for the Electron app, `web` / `headless` / `node` for the CLI modes. The `desktop` profile is managed by the Electron app and refuses `dsh` CLI writes while the app is running; install into it from the app's own plugin manager, or close the app first.

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` also appends it to `dsh.profile.bundles` and the loader mounts it on the next start. If you installed by hand, add the row yourself:

```yaml
# ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml
- insert:
    - id: session-manager
      name: 'dsh-session-manager'
```

## Agent tools

All six take JSON arguments and return `{ ok: true, ... }` or `{ ok: false, error }`.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `session_list` | Enumerate persisted sessions with workspace, archive state, tags and title. Filters: `workspaceId`, `path`, `archived`, `tag`. |
| `session_move` | Move sessions across workspaces. Rewrites the log header `cwd` and renames the directory on disk, then updates the registry live — the GUI reflects it without a restart. |
| `session_delete` | Permanently delete sessions and their log directories. Pass `backupDir` to copy each directory first. |
| `session_tag` | `set` / `add` / `remove` / `clear` / `drop` / `list` tags. Stored in `~/.dsh/session-tags.json`. |
| `session_archive` | Hide a session from every grouping surface; log and workspace slot preserved. Idempotent. |
| `session_unarchive` | Restore an archived session to its original position — the direction the GUI is missing. |

Live sessions (the conversation the model is currently running in) are refused by `session_move` and `session_delete`.

## REST API

Registered only when the `webServer` service is present (the `web` and `desktop` modes). Every handler funnels through the corresponding tool's `execute`, so both surfaces behave identically.

Every request is fenced by `isLoopbackRequest(req)` — a non-loopback peer gets `403 {"error":"forbidden: loopback-only"}`. There is no token; the fence is the transport, not a credential. Do not expose the DSH web server beyond localhost while this plugin is mounted.

| Method | Path | Body / query |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/dsh-session-manager/sessions` | — |
| `GET` | `/api/dsh-session-manager/tags` | — |
| `PUT` | `/api/dsh-session-manager/tags` | `{ "sessionId": "...", "tags": ["a","b"] }` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/dsh-session-manager/tags` | `{ "tags": ["a"] }` — drops those tags from every session |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-session-manager/sessions/move` | `{ "sessionIds": [...], "targetWorkspaceId": "..." }` or `{ ..., "targetPath": "...", "createIfMissing": true }` |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-session-manager/sessions/delete` | `{ "sessionIds": [...], "backupDir": "..." }` (`backupDir` optional) |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-session-manager/sessions/archive` | `{ "sessionId": "..." }` |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-session-manager/sessions/unarchive` | `{ "sessionId": "..." }` |
| `POST` | `/api/dsh-session-manager/projcache/warm` | — (diagnostics: returns the title warm-up report) |

Status codes: `200` when the tool returned `ok: true`, `400` for a business failure or a malformed body, `403` off-loopback, `405` wrong method, `500` unexpected throw.

Request bodies are capped at 1 MB and must be JSON objects.

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3080/api/dsh-session-manager/tags
curl -s -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:3080/api/dsh-session-manager/tags \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"sessionId":"abc123","tags":["research","todo"]}'
```

## Behaviour worth knowing

**Moves keep three things in sync.** The physical move (zstd header rewrite plus directory rename) is followed by a registry header re-index and the public `attachSession` / `detachSession` calls, and the projection cache's `identity.cwd` is updated through the storage-domain table handle. Skipping any of the three leaves the GUI showing a stale path.

**Titles are pre-warmed at startup.** `session.list` carries no title for a cold session; the durable title lives in the projection-cache checkpoint, which is only written when a session was attached in some process. After a restart every unopened session is cold and the sidebar falls back to the directory basename. 800 ms after mount the plugin walks persisted sessions lacking a title row and calls the official `coldSnapshot(meta, inheritedEventCount, events)` to write the checkpoint back.

The tail probe that validates an existing title row is **off** (`WARM_TAIL_PROBE = false` in `lib/index.js`). With it on, every start re-read the log tail of all sessions — the dominant cost of a slow sidebar after a restart, at roughly 620 sessions. The trade-off: a rename that happened during a projection-cache write failure window is no longer corrected at startup; the official cold-read ladder still heals it when the session is opened. Set the constant to `true` to restore the old behaviour.

**Archive goes through the registry.** Archiving funnels through `archiveSession()` — the same add-only API the GUI uses. The plugin never rewrites the archive set except on an explicit delete or unarchive, and even then it goes through the registry's public `enqueueOperation` / `setState` write chain so the registry's cached state stays coherent.

**Zero imports by design.** `lib/index.js` uses only `node:` builtins. The file plugin is loaded by native dynamic import, so a bare specifier would have to resolve from the profile's `node_modules`; the builtin-only rule keeps it loadable as a standalone file plugin (the same shape as `zen-useragent.js`).

## Companion plugins

- [`dsh-session-tree`](https://github.com/minhaoli/dsh-session-tree) — the sidebar UI (tags, grouping, drag-to-move, delete) that consumes this REST API. It replaces the official `ui-workspace` bundle, so disable that row when both are installed.
- [`dsh-session-query-vector`](https://github.com/minhaoli/dsh-session-query-vector) — semantic session search backend.
- [`dsh-session-search`](https://github.com/minhaoli/dsh-session-search) — in-conversation find bar.
- [`dsh-ui-reload`](https://github.com/minhaoli/dsh-ui-reload) — one-click frontend reload button.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).
