# ds-bot

The DS Bot plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh). It turns dsh into a team of long-lived Bots that talk to you, to each other and in group chats. See the [project page](../README.md) for an overview, install steps and screenshots.

> Early release (v0.1). Features, tools and the saved data format can still change.

Tested with dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` (Web and Desktop) on Linux.

## Features

- **Long-lived Bots**: each Bot is a dsh Session in the "DS Bot" workspace, with its own name, role, instructions and model.
- **Working folders**: a Bot can work in a folder you choose instead of the team workspace, and a group chat can set one folder for all its members there. Pick it in the Bot's settings or details panel or in the group's settings, or ask a Bot (`update_bot`, `update_group`). After a change, the chat goes on in a fresh part that starts in the new folder. When a Bot sets a folder outside the team workspace, or adds a Bot to a group that works in one, it asks for your approval if those Bots can only write in their folder. Folders that hold dsh data (`$DSH_HOME`, the team's data) are refused.
- **Bots work together**: `message_bot` sends a message to another Bot, `create_bot` and `update_bot` add and set up Bots, and `ask_user` asks you a question without blocking the other Bots.
- **Group chats**: members speak one at a time, and each one reads the latest messages first. A message can `@Name` a member to pass the turn on; type `@` to pick one from a list. **+ → Reference a chat** adds another Bot's chat to a message as context, and in a group the members who answer get it. A member with nothing new to add stays quiet (`[PASS]`). Each member has its own hidden Session per group, so a group never reads a Bot's private chat.
- **Roles and permissions**:

  | Who | Can do |
  |---|---|
  | You | Everything |
  | Main Bot (there can be more than one) | Manage every group; change and delete Bots |
  | Group admin | Manage its own group only (name, notice, members, reply mode) |
  | Member | Speak in the group and `@` another member |

- **Long chats stay inside the model's window**: dsh's own compaction never runs on a Bot's Session. When a turn ends past the check line (a share of the model's context window), a small separate model call, the context steward, reads the latest messages of the chat and decides once. If the work is still under way, the chat is condensed in place into a checkpoint: a handoff summary plus your recent messages word for word. If the work has reached a stopping point, the Bot writes a handoff note and continues in a new part. Either way you still see one chat, with no marker. Earlier parts and condensed messages stay searchable in a full-text index (`node:sqlite` FTS5) through `read_own_chat`.
- **Memory**: each Bot keeps notes across all its conversations, and the team shares one more. See [Memory](#memory).
- **Web search**: see [Web search](#web-search).
- **Bot browser (dsh Desktop only)**: see [Bot browser](#bot-browser).
- **Images**: for a model that cannot read images, a vision model first turns the image into text.
- **Secrets**: a Bot asks for an API key or token with a card in its own chat and never sees the value. See [Secrets](#secrets).
- **Usage**: Settings → Usage shows token usage by time (24 hours to 12 months, or days picked on a calendar), by Bot and by model, with a page for each Bot and each model. Calls that a Session logs are read from the logs, so older chats count too. Calls that leave no log (checkpoints, handoff notes, the steward, image readings, dsh titles and compaction) are counted while they stream, from the time the plugin runs. Tokens only, no cost.
- **Make it yours**: name, role, instructions, model and look (20 characters and 12 colors, or your own photo) for each Bot; a theme, an accent color and an avatar animation level (quiet, normal or lively) for the team. A pinned Bot or group chat shows a small pushpin in the sidebar. Settings has these pages: General (look), Bots (Main Bots and each Bot's settings), Group chats (each group's settings), Connectors, Capabilities, Scheduled tasks, Usage, Secrets, Feedback and About DS Bot (versions, updates and links).

## Install

The [project page](../README.md#install) has the full steps for dsh Desktop and dsh Web. In short:

- dsh Desktop: Settings → Plugins → add `ds-bot` (npm), a `.tgz` file, or `github:Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot#v0.1.5&path:/ds-bot`.
- Command line: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add ds-bot` (or `--profile web`).

To work on the plugin from a checkout, add it to a dsh profile as a linked dependency and a bundle:

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "ds-bot": "link:/path/to/ds-bot" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "ds-bot"] } }
}
```

Run `pnpm install` in the profile folder, then start dsh from the deepseek-harness repository:

```sh
pnpm -s dsh --profile web --no-open
```

The first time the team opens, the plugin creates a Main Bot called Chief.

**Upgrading from the legacy `dsh-bot` package**: earlier builds used the package name `dsh-bot`. Remove `dsh-bot` from the profile before you add `ds-bot`, because both use the plugin id `bot`. Your team, chats and secrets stay where they are (see [Data and backups](#data-and-backups)); saved browser settings, the theme and Bot colors move over the first time DS Bot opens.

## Configuration

Options go in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, under the `bot` entry. All of them are optional.

```yaml
- id: bot
  name: ds-bot
  config:
    workspace: /path/to/workspace   # where the Bots work; default <home>/workspace
    home: /path/to/bot-data         # where the team is saved; default $DSH_HOME/bot
    checkRatio: 0.8                 # share of the model's usable window where the steward decides
    browser: true                   # force the Bot browser on or off; default on in Desktop only
    memory: true                    # false turns memory off: no memory tools, section or panel
    memoryReview: true              # false leaves memory to the Bots' own remember calls
    diagnosticsFile: false          # keep the error log in memory only; default <home>/logs/diagnostics.jsonl
    updateCheck: true               # look for a newer DS Bot when a window opens; default true
    updateRegistry: https://registry.example/   # ask only this npm registry for updates
    github: false                   # hide the GitHub connector; default shown in Connectors
```

**Updates**: when a window opens, DS Bot asks where it was installed from for a newer release: the npm registry (the one the DSH plugin manager installs from, then its fallbacks), or the latest GitHub release for a `github:…#vX.Y.Z` install. A newer version shows a cloud button at the top right of the sidebar; **Update** reinstalls DS Bot through the DSH plugin manager, and the new version runs from the next DSH start. A linked or local checkout is never offered an update. Settings → About DS Bot shows the same state, with **Check for updates** to ask again at once.

The same card can carry DSH itself: a DS Bot release may name the DSH release it was verified against (`dsBot.verifiedDsh` in its `package.json`), and only that version is offered — running something newer is a downgrade offer too. A release that names no version offers no DSH update. A DSH installed from npm is swapped by `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>`. DSH Desktop installs the newest release its own updater finds, so the card shows DSH there only when that release is the verified one, and **Open updates** opens the app's update panel. A release may raise the floor with `dsBot.minBot`: until the bot itself is that new, the DSH row waits.

## Models

Model providers are set up with dsh's `llm-pi-ai` plugin in `cordis.patch.yml`. Every Bot runs on one model of its own, from the models DSH serves. A new team's first Main Bot has none: its chat opens on a model card and it greets the user only after a pick. The Create Bot form starts on the DSH default model. The Bot's details panel and settings (or a Main Bot's `update_bot`) change it; a Bot whose model is no longer served shows the card again. A team saved by an older version keeps the model each Bot last ran on.

- Give every model a `contextWindow`. DS Bot takes its lines from it: the usable window is the window minus the reply reserve (`maxTokens`), the hard line is 95% of that, and the check line is `checkRatio` of it. A model without `contextWindow` gets the adapter's default (262,144 tokens for `llm-pi-ai`), which may be wrong for that model; a model that reports no window at all counts as 500,000.
- To send images, the provider needs `defaultInput: [ text, image ]`.
- Keep API keys out of the repository. Use dsh's own key storage or environment variables.

## Memory

A Bot remembers what should last beyond one conversation: your preferences, decisions, corrections and facts it should not ask again. Memory is plain Markdown in the [Agent Memory Repo](https://github.com/AgentMemoryRepo/agentmemoryrepo) format: one entry per line, ending in `[source: …; added: …]`.

After each turn, a memory review reads what is new in the Bot's chat (and in each group, per member) and keeps, updates or removes entries itself, so memory does not depend on the Bot deciding to call `remember`. It keeps only what you say, writes entries in your language, and refuses keys, passwords and ID numbers.

- **Two scopes**: each Bot has its own memory, and the team memory is read by every Bot. A Bot writes its own. Main Bots and group admins (of any group) also write the team memory; a Main Bot can read and change another Bot's memory when you ask.
- **Tools**: `remember` saves an entry or replaces one (`replace`), `forget` removes one, and `recall` searches every entry, reads a topic whole, or lists what is saved. The Bot adds the source (a part anchor such as `part 2 #1234`, which `read_own_chat` opens) and the date; a Bot that writes for others is named with `by:`.
- **Files**: `MEMORY.md` holds what every conversation needs, and details go in topic files linked from its `## Index` as `[[topic]]`.
- **In the prompt**: both `MEMORY.md` files go into the Bot's system prompt. The section is frozen when a Session starts, so the provider's prompt cache holds; a change shows from the next part or checkpoint, and `recall` finds it at once.
- **Fixed sizes**: an entry has at most 300 characters, a `MEMORY.md` 4,000, a topic 16,000, and a scope 40 topics. A save past a limit fails and says how to make room.
- **Safety**: memory is data, not instructions. An entry that looks like a key or token is refused, and a Bot is told not to save what a web page, file or tool result asks it to remember.
- **History**: files change in place, and `journal.jsonl` keeps every change with the line before and after. When a Bot is deleted, its memory moves to `archive/`.

**The memory panel**: the Bot's details panel has a Memory row with the entry count; Manage opens the memory panel.

- **Memory summary**: the Bot's model writes a short summary in prose from every entry, in the interface language. It is written again when the entries change, and the ⋯ menu can regenerate it.
- **All entries**: the ⋯ menu lists every entry by scope and topic, with its date and author, and the size of each `MEMORY.md`. Remove takes two clicks.
- **Ask or update**: ask what the Bot remembers, or tell it what to add, correct or remove. One model call answers from the entries only, and its changes go through the same checks as the tools.
- A line in the chat ("Memory updated") shows when a Bot changes memory and opens the panel. When memory changes in the background, the Bot's capsule at the top of its chat stretches to say "Memory updated" for a moment; clicking it opens the memory panel.

A read-only dsh (see [Data and backups](#data-and-backups)) shows memory but cannot change it.

## Web search

The package includes a second plugin, `ds-bot/web-search`. It registers the search provider `auto`, and `cordis.patch.yml` makes it the default. Each search goes in this order:

1. If the profile names another `searchProvider`, that one is used.
2. The current model route's own search, with that route's key and host. The plugin knows the Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses and Gemini protocols, and a few search APIs (Ollama, Kimi, Zhipu, MiMo). Add more with `searchApis`.
3. A fallback without a key: the public result pages of Bing and DuckDuckGo.
4. If nothing works, the search fails and tells the model not to guess addresses.

Each result starts with a `Search backend: …` line that names the path it took.

## Bot browser

In dsh Desktop, a Bot's chat header has a globe button. It opens that Bot's own browser panel.

- **One partition per Bot** (`bot:<id>`): logins and cookies belong to that Bot only.
- **The Bot can read the page**: the `read_browser` tool reads the page's DOM, not a screenshot. The text becomes Markdown with headings, nested lists, tables, code blocks and quotes. Links and form controls are marked `[#n]` in place and listed below with their targets and values. The tool also reads the text you selected. Long pages are read in parts (`from`). Page content is treated as data, never as instructions.
  - It reads open Shadow DOM (with `<slot>`) and same-origin iframes up to 3 levels deep.
  - It reads only what is visible: `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, zero-height and closed `<details>` content is skipped.
  - It never reads the values of password, credit card (`autocomplete="cc-*"`) or one-time code fields.
  - Limits: 400,000 characters, 150,000 nodes, 5,000 rows per table, 3,000 links and controls, 1.5 seconds. A cut result says so.
  - It cannot read cross-origin iframes (one line with the address), closed shadow roots, canvas content (online editors, maps), or text in CSS `::before` / `::after`. On pages that render on demand, only the rendered part is read.
  - Read only: the Bot cannot click, type, scroll or open addresses yet.
- **Addresses**: http and https only. localhost and LAN addresses are allowed; cloud metadata addresses (such as `169.254.x.x`) and dsh's own ports are not.
- The browser panel and the details drawer share the right column; opening one closes the other. Switching chats switches the panel to that Bot. Deleting a Bot clears its browser and saved address.

dsh Web has no browser panel and no `read_browser` tool.

## Secrets

When a Bot needs an API key, token or password, it calls `request_secret`, and a secret card shows in its own chat. The Bot never sees the value.

- **Fill in**: the field hides what you type, is not part of a form and is not autofilled. Choose "All Bots" or "Only this Bot" and select Save. A value must have at least 4 characters (a 4-digit PIN works). A value of 8 characters or more is hidden wherever it appears; a shorter one only where no letter or digit touches it, so ordinary words stay intact.
- **Allow**: if the secret is already saved but this Bot is not allowed to use it, the card only asks whether to allow it. You can also replace the value there.
- **Use**: the value goes only into the Bot's shell environment as `DSH_SECRET_<NAME>` (`$DSH_SECRET_NAME` in bash, `$env:DSH_SECRET_NAME` in PowerShell). `list_secrets` lists the names a Bot can use.
- **Masking**: before a tool result is saved and before each request goes to the model, every copy of a secret value is replaced with `[secret:<NAME>]`.
- **Manage**: Settings → Secrets lists every secret by name, purpose, the Bot that asked and the last use. You can change who may use it, replace the value, delete it or add one. Deleting a Bot removes it from every secret.
- **Storage**: `<DSH_HOME>/bot/secrets.json`, file mode 600, written atomically. Values are never in `state.json` or logs.

Limits:

- On Windows, the file mode has no effect; the file is protected by your user folder only.
- Only exact copies of a value are masked. A Bot that encodes, splits or reverses a value can still print it. Do not give important secrets to a Bot you do not trust.
- On a page that is not HTTPS (for example dsh Web opened over http on a LAN), the value crosses the network in clear text. The card warns you.
- Group chats show no cards; a Bot asks in its own chat.

## Data and backups

The plugin saves its data in `config.home`. Without it, the folder is `$DSH_HOME/bot`, or `~/.dsh/bot` when `DSH_HOME` is not set.

| System | Default folder |
|---|---|
| Linux, macOS | `~/.dsh/bot/` |
| Windows | `C:\Users\<user>\.dsh\bot\` |

- To move all dsh data (Sessions, profiles and plugin data), set `DSH_HOME`.
- To move only the plugin data, set `home` in the configuration (see [Configuration](#configuration)).

Files in `bot/`:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `state.json` | The team: Bots, groups, Bot-to-Bot messages, preferences and open questions |
| `state.lock` | The dsh that is using this data (pid and host). It is removed when that dsh exits. |
| `chat-index.sqlite` | Full-text index of older chat parts (`read_own_chat`); rebuilt if deleted |
| `usage.sqlite` | Token counts for the Usage page; rebuilt from the Session logs if deleted, losing only the calls outside the logs and the names of deleted Bots |
| `memory/` | Memory (see [Memory](#memory)): `bots/<id>/` and `team/` (`MEMORY.md` and topics), `journal.jsonl` (every change), `snapshots/` (the section each Session froze), `summaries/` (the panel's summary; safe to delete), `reviewed.json` (how far the memory review has read) and `archive/` (deleted Bots) |
| `ocr.json` | Cache of image text; safe to delete |
| `workspace` | The team workspace: the working folder of every Bot without one of its own (`config.workspace` changes it) |
| `secrets.json` | Saved secrets. Treat backups of it like passwords. |
| `logs/diagnostics.jsonl` | Recent errors and warnings, with keys, tokens, saved secrets and the home folder removed. It moves to `diagnostics.jsonl.1` past 1 MB. Safe to delete. |

The chats themselves are dsh Sessions and are not in `bot/`: they are in `~/.dsh/sessions/`. dsh keeps its workspace list in `~/.dsh/storages/workspace.json` and profiles (with model settings) in `~/.dsh/profiles/`. Bot browser logins are not saved: Desktop keeps each Bot's partition in memory only.

**Back up and restore**

1. Quit dsh completely (both the Web server and Desktop), so `state.json` is current.
2. Copy all of `~/.dsh/` (at least `bot/`, `sessions/` and `storages/`). A copy of `bot/` alone loses the chats.
3. To restore, quit dsh, put the folder back in the same place, then start dsh.

**Move to another computer**: `state.json` has no absolute paths except the working folders you set for Bots and groups, but dsh's `storages/workspace.json` and the Session folder names contain the workspace's absolute path. If the path is the same on the new computer, copy the folder. If it is different (another user name or system), it is not yet tested whether dsh finds the old Sessions.

**dsh Web and Desktop at the same time**: by default both use the same `~/.dsh`. The dsh that loads the team first takes `bot/state.lock` and can change the team. The other one is read-only: it shows the team and follows changes to the file, but refuses changes (`bot/read-only`, "open in another dsh"), and its Bots cannot start new Sessions. When the first one exits, the other one takes over on its next request. To change the team from both at once, give one of them a different `DSH_HOME` (two separate teams).

## Development

You need Node 24, pnpm and a deepseek-harness checkout with its dependencies installed, next to this repository (`../deepseek-harness`, or set `DSH_HARNESS`). The Desktop test bench also needs `xvfb-run` and `ffmpeg`. Web screenshots need Chrome or Chromium (`CHROME_BIN`; by default `google-chrome` or `chromium`).

```sh
npm ci                                   # esbuild, for the client build
npm run build                            # src/client → client.js
npm test                                 # unit tests
npm run lint                             # oxlint from the dsh repository (.oxlintrc.json)
dev/bench.sh dev 3100 8800 start         # Web test bench: mock model + dsh Web, data in ../.dsh-test-dev
dev/desktop-linux/desktop.sh dev start   # Desktop test bench: mock model + dsh Desktop in Xvfb
CONTEXT_WINDOW=100000 CHECK_RATIO=0.45 dev/bench.sh smoke 3101 8801 reset && node dev/smoke.mjs smoke 3101
dev/check.sh                             # all checks (see below)
```

- `client.js` is built from `src/client/` and committed, so `link:` and Git installs need no build. Do not edit `client.js` by hand; `npm test` checks that it matches the source. After a change in `src/client/`, run `npm run build` and reload the page. After a change in `index.js` or `src/host/`, restart dsh.
- **Web test bench** `dev/bench.sh <name> <web port> <mock port> [start|stop|reset|status]`: a scripted mock model (`dev/mock-llm.mjs`, no real tokens; its commands are listed at the top of the file) and a dsh Web server. Data goes in `../.dsh-test-<name>/`; `reset` clears the team and Sessions first. The login address with its token is in `../.dsh-test-<name>/web.log`.
- **Desktop test bench** `dev/desktop-linux/desktop.sh <name> [start|stop|reset|status]`: dsh does not run Desktop on Linux; `launch.mts` runs the unpackaged Desktop in Xvfb. The first start downloads Electron and a Linux runtime (a few minutes). `start` returns when the team shows in a 1400×860 window.
- **All checks** `dev/check.sh [--skip steps] [--only steps] [--out dir]`: `unit`, `build`, `lint`, `smoke`, `web` (screenshots of the sidebar, a chat, a group, Bot settings, the Bots page and group settings) and `desktop` (the same screenshots, then the Bot browser checks). It stops everything it started. On failure it names the step and its log and exits non-zero. A full run takes about 3 minutes after the first download.
- **Ports**: every script takes `SLOT=n` (0-9, default 0) so that several people or sessions on one machine do not collide: Web bench `31n0` and mock `88n0`, smoke `31n1` and `88n1`, Desktop mock `88n2`, and so on. A Desktop uses about 1 GB of memory; stop it when you are done.
- **Real models** (these cost tokens): `dev/steward-eval.mjs` sends hand-written conversation endings through the context steward's own prompt to an OpenAI-compatible route (or, with `--api messages`, an Anthropic Messages route such as DeepSeek's official one) and checks each decision. `dev/llm-tap.mjs <port> <upstream base URL> <log.jsonl> [body dir]` is a logging pass-through for either format: point a provider's `baseURL` at it, and it writes one JSON line per call (steward, checkpoint, handoff note or main turn, the Bot's name, token usage, the answer, and where the request first differs from the same Bot's previous one, which is what a provider's cache can reuse; never headers). With a body dir it also saves every request body. Each file explains its use at the top.
- **Screenshots**: `dev/ui-shots.mjs` works for both apps (`desktop <dsh repo> <dir> <renderer port>` or `web <dsh repo> <dir> <bench name> <web port>`).
- `npm test` loads the `@deepseek-ai/*` packages from the deepseek-harness checkout.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host entry: installs the `src/host/` modules in order |
| `src/host/` | Host: team and storage (`roster`, `store`), tools (`tools`), turns and delivery (`turns`, `delivery`), group chats (`groups`), chat parts, the context steward and the index (`parts`, `steward`, `chat-index`), image text (`images`), secrets (`secrets`), Bot browser (`browser`), the `POST api/bot` route (`channel`) |
| `src/client/` | Browser source: sidebar, chat header, transcript cells, panels and dialogs, themes, Bot browser panel |
| `client.js` | Built from `src/client/` by `scripts/build-client.mjs` (esbuild); committed |
| `web-search.js` | The `auto` search provider; independent of the team code |
| `test/` | Unit tests and fixtures |
| `dev/characters.mjs` | Builds the characters (small 3D models traced to outlines) into the `CHARACTERS` table in `src/client/characters.js` |
| `dev/` | Mock model, test benches, smoke test, Desktop scripts, real-model tools (steward evaluation, logging pass-through) |

FlyBot is two plugins on top of a pinned [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot) core for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness):

- **`@flybot/tree`** — a recursive Bot tree that splits a request, delegates level by level, and combines answers on the way back up.
- **`@flybot/social`** — connect your Bots as friends with other homes and chat through a self-hosted [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server, with owner approvals.

## Features

### Tree plugin (`@flybot/tree`)

Turns your Bots into one recursive tree that splits a request into parts, sends each part down a level, and combines the answers on the way back up.

![Tree plugin: Chief splits a Hangzhou trip across Travel, Food, and Budget](docs/images/demo-tree.gif)

- **One root.** The tree's root is the Main Bot (Chief); no new bot is created for it. A separate `Root` bot is created only if the team has Bots but no Main Bot. Existing local Bots join under the root as its children, up to `maxChildren`.
- **Children on demand.** Any tree Bot (not only the Main/root) calls `create_child_bot(name, role_description)` to make a child directly under *itself*; the tool takes no parent argument. Calls are handled one at a time per parent, so parallel calls never go over the limits or create two siblings with the same name. The rules:
  - names are 1–40 characters, and duplicate sibling names are rejected (case and spaces ignored);
  - depth is at most 5 (the root counts as 1), with at most 8 children per Bot (set in `limits.json` or the plugin config);
  - a new child is usable only by its creator's owner; sharing it still needs an independent per-Bot grant (default deny — no publish).
- **Level-by-level delegation.** Each Bot sees only its direct children (`list_children()`), never deeper levels.
  - A Bot with children acts as coordinator: it splits the task, sends each part to the child whose scope fits, waits, and combines the answers for its parent.
  - A Bot with no children does the work itself.
- **Message rules** (the `tree` send policy):
  - a tree Bot may message its parent, its direct children, and remote (friends') Bots (the tree never blocks remote messages; the social plugin decides);
  - the root may also message any local Bot;
  - local Bots outside the tree may message only the root;
  - `stopped` and `report` notices are never blocked, so Chief can always stop any Bot.
- **Reparenting.** When a Bot is deleted, its children move up to its parent. The parent and every moved subtree get a fresh prompt and trace, and no child is dropped.
- **Trace line.** When a tree Bot answers its *parent*, it starts the answer with its path, e.g. `Chief → Work → Dev`. Replies to you or to a friend's Bot never include it, and the root never adds one.
- **Your prompts are kept.** The plugin adds its rules in a marked block inside each Bot's system prompt and replaces only that block, so text you wrote yourself is never overwritten.
- **Sidebar.** The Bot list is drawn as one expandable tree with Chief on top. Bots outside the tree are shown directly under Chief.

Install (needs the core, `path:/core`):

```bash
npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/tree"
```

### Social plugin (`@flybot/social`)

Every local Bot can chat with friends' Bots through a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server that **you self-host**. Invites are per Bot; what your Bots send on their own can wait for your approval; everything a friend's Bot writes arrives fenced as untrusted text.

![Social plugin: add a friend, chat with their Bot, approve a held reply in Bot Social, and see it arrive](docs/images/demo-social.gif)

*Demo: add a friend, message their Bot, the reply is held by Bot Social because it mentions money, the friend's owner approves it, and it appears in the chat.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-social.mp4)

- **One-click onboarding.** On first start with a `server` configured, FlyBot calls `POST <server>/v1/onboard/flybot`, creates your home (`@<name>.home`), and stores credentials in `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-social.json` (mode 600).
- **Members.** Access is a per-Bot **grant** (default deny, Chief included). A local Bot becomes `@<bot>.<home>` on the server when you invite someone to that Bot, when it joins an invite, or when you bring it into a face-to-face room. The sidebar lists only Bots granted to you. **Manage access

# flybot-social Every local Bot can chat with friends' Bots on a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server. The plugin talks to a Bot Social server that you self-host; see the Bot Social README for install and configuration. Host: `index.js`; browser: `client.js`. Design: see "Social design: homes and members" in the root README. - **One-click onboarding**: on first start, `POST /v1/onboard/flybot` creates the owner, the home identity (`@.home`), and a connector token in one call; credentials go to `credentialsPath` (default `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-social.json`, mode 600). If `@.home` is taken, onboarding retries `Name2`, `Name3`, … so a second install can start without editing YAML. Sidebar **+** → **Copy my handle** copies the connected handle. If start still fails, it shows **Social is not running:** with the reason instead of the host's `Unknown FlyBot endpoint` message. The same failure is written to Settings → Feedback. - **Members**: a local Bot becomes `@.` (`add_home_member`) when it is invited, when it joins an invite, or at face-to-face join, stored as field `social.member`. There is no published flag: access is a per-Bot **grant** (Invite to this Bot → accept). Default deny, Chief included. Deleted Bots are revoked on `bot.removed`. Ungranted Bots are not registered at start and are not polled. **Face-to-face join** of my own Bot is an implicit room-scoped grant: if it has no identity yet, the plugin registers it room-only (`social.member.roomOnly`). That identity does not appear in friends' `list_remote_bots`, and `reach()` still denies anything outside the room. When you leave the last face room or the room closes, the plugin revokes it (`remove_home_member`). A failed join that created a new room-only identity is revoked too. A later person-grant reuses the handle and drops `roomOnly`. **Manage access** on the Bot lists who has it and **Revoke**. - **Remote roster**: `list_remote_bots` → friends' Bots published into the main Bot list (globe mark). Each row uses the published `avatar` / `color` when the server sends them, else a handle-seeded look. Sidebar section `flybot.sidebar.section#social` keeps **N to approve**, + panels, and **Past rooms**. `@` rows via `flybot.composer.mention#social`. Remote Bots never enter `bot.list()`. **Remove this Bot** declines that grant (`decline_bot_grant`) so it leaves the owner's Manage access; an older server hides it locally.

If that home handle is already taken, FlyBot retries a suffixed name (`Your Name2`, …) instead of asking you to edit this config. **Copy my handle** on the sidebar **+** copies your connected handle. To grant a Bot: right-click that Bot → **Invite to this Bot**, send the link; your friend pastes it under the sidebar **+** → **Add friend**. Accepting the invite grants that Bot only. A friend's inbound messages arrive immediately. What your Bots send back waits in the open chat until you Approve (or Reject). Auto-send for a new friend is off until you turn it on. If a friend sees no reply, look for the **to approve** badge. Without a `server`, the social plugin stays idle by design. Tree works without Bot Social. ## Built on FlyBot keeps the upstream DS Bot core byte-identical (`ds-bot/`, pinned in `ds-bot.pin.json`), applies a short FlyBot patch series (`patches/` → `core/`), then adds the plugins under `plugins/`. See [#34](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/issues/34). The web UI (header, About, settings, update popups) says FlyBot; the npm package and update-check still use the upstream `ds-bot` name and repository. ## More - Core options and internals: [`core/README.md`](core/README.md) - Contributing: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md) - Known issues: [docs/known-issues.md](docs/known-issues.md) - Architecture notes: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) ## License [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). Third-party notices in [NOTICE](NOTICE). ## Disclaimer FlyBot is an independent community project. **It is not an official DeepSeek product.** Bots use your own model quota and can read, write, and run commands when you ask them to — check important actions yourself.

# @flybot/tree Recursive bot tree plugin for FlyBot (built on ds-bot / DeepSeek Harness). ## English ### What it does - **Chief is the root.** ds-bot's Main Bot (`BotView.isMain`, i.e. `state.mainBotIds`; the one named `Chief` if there are several) is adopted as the root with `treeRole: 'root'` (no `parent`); no bot is created. Every other tree bot has `parent` (its parent's id) and `treeRole` (its role). Adoption runs at startup, a few retries later and on every `bot.created`, so a Chief created after startup is picked up. Only if the team has bots but no Main Bot is a separate `Root` created. `config.rootBotId` picks the root explicitly. - **Migration:** a separate `Root` auto-created by earlier versions (parent `null`, not a Main Bot) hands its children to Chief, loses its tree fields and tree prompt, and gets `fields['flybot-tree'].retired = true` so adoption skips it. The bot itself is **never** deleted (bot-im / the user decide). Idempotent. - **Adoption (`adoptExisting`, default true):** every local bot with no tree fields that is not retired and not another Main Bot (e.g. existing 研究员, 数据分析师, 文案, 程序员) becomes a child of Chief at startup and on `bot.created` when the creator set no `parent`. Chief's `maxChildren` is respected: extra bots stay unattached and a warning is logged. Adopted bots keep their own prompt; the tree block is added. Message rules apply to them like any tree child (Chief ↔ them; they → only Chief and their own children). - **Prompt injection:** the tree text sits in a marked block (`…`) inside each bot's `systemPrompt`; only that block is replaced, so Chief's own prompt text is never overwritten. Chief gets the coordinator rules for its direct children. - `bot.send` middleware `tree`: inside the tree a bot may message only its parent and direct children (`deny` otherwise). A non-root tree bot may not message local bots outside the tree; the root (Chief) may message any local bot. Local bots outside the tree may message only the root. Remote targets and outside-to-outside sends get no opinion (`undefined`, social decides). **Granted Bots (#90):** a friend's (remote) sender reaches a tree bot only if the core says it has a person-grant (`flybot.bot.hasAnyGrant`): new and adopted bots and the Chief start with none. A granted bot is reached directly at any depth, never redirected through the root; an ungranted one is denied (`tree: this bot has not been granted…`). Granted bots on both sides are not the tree's call across trees or to non-tree bots (the core's owner policy decides); inside one tree the parent/child rule is unchanged, as are `stopped` / `report` notices. A granted child's prompt tells it to answer outside senders directly, without a trace line, and to delegate only to its own children. On a core without `hasAnyGrant`, the remote-sender rule gives no opinion. - **Control notices bypass tree policy:** `role: 'stopped'` (stop_bot) and `role: 'report'` are never denied by the tree middleware, so a Main Bot can stop any tree bot. - **Deleting a bot:** its children re-attach to its parent and every moved child (and its subtree) gets a fresh prompt/trace. `maxChildren` is not enforced on reparenting (no child is dropped); an overflow is logged as a warning and `create_child_bot` refuses new children there until it is back under the limit. - **`create_child_bot` is serialized per parent:** parallel calls never exceed `maxChildren` or create duplicate-name siblings. - Delegation is level by level: coordinators delegate to direct children whose scope fits and aggregate upward; a bot with no children does the work itself. A one-line trace like `Chief → Work → Dev` is added only to answers a tree bot sends to its parent tree bot; replies to the user or to a remote (friend's, Bot Social) bot never carry it, and the root (Chief) never adds one. - Tools (visible to every tree bot, not only Main/root — #16 Option B): `list_children()` and `create_child_bot(name, role_description)`. The parent is always the calling bot. Limits: depth 5 (root = 1), 8 children per node; duplicate sibling names (case/space-insensitive) are rejected; names are 1–40 characters (ds-bot's roster limit). Every new child gets the same recursive system prompt template (`src/prompt.js`). A new child starts with no person-grant even if its parent is granted; sharing it still needs an independent Invite to this Bot (default deny). - Frontend (`client.js`, bundle id `@flybot/tree`, injects `flybot`): the tree is drawn by ds-bot's own Bot list, so this plugin's separate "Tree" sidebar section is **off by default** (`sidebarSection: true` in the client config brings it back). It always exposes the synchronous helper `ctx.flybot.tree.forest(bots)` (also `globalThis.__flybot__.tree.forest(bots)`), see **Tree data** below. It also registers `flybot.sidebar.structure` (`{ parentOf(botId) }`, parents from `forestOf` over `ctx.flybot.bots()`, refreshed on field changes and every 10 s); ds-bot's sidebar uses it to draw its Bot list as one expandable tree with Chief on top. Retired and non-tree Bots have no parent there, so ds-bot shows them directly under Chief. The entry also has `menuItems({ bot })`, which ds-bot adds to each Bot's right-click menu: two items, `{ id: 'copy-invite', label: 'Copy invite link' }` and `{ id: 'copy-invite-text', label: 'Copy invite with instructions' }` (each with `visible`, `run`). `visible` is `social.canInvite(bot.id) === true` (false without the social plugin); `run` calls `social.createInvite(botId)` (or `flybot.call('social.createInvite', { botId })`). **Copy invite link** copies only the bare URL (`link`), **Copy invite with instructions** the full message `text`; a missing field is an error, never swapped for the other. The clipboard write starts inside the click via `ClipboardItem` with the text as a promise, so it keeps the click's permission while the invite is created; `writeText` then a textarea are the fallbacks. They return "Invite link for copied" or "Invite for copied, with instructions", which ds-bot shows as a toast; a failure throws and shows as the error toast. Right-clicking never opens the Bot's chat. ### Config ```yaml - id: tree name: "@flybot/tree" config: maxDepth: 5 # default from limits.json maxChildren: 8 bypassSocial: false # true: allowed tree edges skip social friend/approval checks rootName: Root # name of the fallback root, only when the team has no Main Bot rootBotId: '' # optional: adopt this bot as the root instead of the Main Bot autoRoot: true # false: do not adopt/create the root at startup adoptExisting: true # false: do not attach existing/new parentless bots to Chief # client side (browser plugin config): sidebarSection: false # true: show the separate Tree section ``` ### Tree data (for ds-bot's sidebar) Everything is synchronous. **Fields** (per bot, `bot.fields['flybot-tree']`; also on every bot in the browser roster, which spreads the stored bot record including `fields` and `createdAt`): | key | value | |---|---| | `treeRole` | `'root'` on the root (Chief); the role text (may be `''`) on other members | | `parent` | parent bot id; absent on the root | | `retired` | `true` on the old auto-created Root: not a member, never re-adopted | A bot is a tree member when it has `treeRole` or `parent` and is not `retired`. **Helper:** `forest(bots)` turns bot records into nested nodes: - browser: `ctx.flybot.tree.forest(roster.bots)` or `globalThis.__flybot__.tree.forest(roster.bots)` - host: `apply(...).tree.forest()` (reads `bot.list()` and the scoped fields) - module: `forestOf(bots)` from `src/forest.js` ```ts type TreeNode = { id: string name: string role: string // 'Main bot · root of the tree' for the root, else treeRole ('' allowed) root: boolean // treeRole === 'root' createdAt: number | null // the record's createdAt, null when absent children: TreeNode[] } forest(bots: Array<{ id: string, name: string, createdAt?: number, fields?: { 'flybot-tree'?: { parent?: string, treeRole?: string, retired?: boolean } } }>): TreeNode[] ``` Top level: roots first, then members whose parent is missing (orphans). Siblings are ordered by `createdAt`; records without it keep their input order; ties go by name. Cycles are cut. Non-members, retired bots and remote bots (never in the roster's `bots`) are left out, so ds-bot draws them as before. ### Plugin format (matches ds-bot) `package.json` has `"type": "module"`, keyword `dsh-plugin`, `exports` `.` (host) and `./client` (browser), and `"dsh": { "client": { "platform": "web" } }`. The host entry exports `name`, `inject`, `apply(ctx, config)` (cordis style). `client.js` uses `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory(require) })` with `react` provided by the shell; it exports `inject: ['flybot']` + `apply(ctx)` and registers its section via `ctx.flybot.slots.register`. ### Interface (ctx.flybot, finalized by bot-im 2026-10-14 — all in `src/adapter.js`) | API | Shape | |---|---| | `ctx.flybot.scope('flybot-tree')` | every call below goes through this scoped handle, so fields land in `fields['flybot-tree']` (never `shared`) | | `bot.list()` | `BotView[]` | | `bot.create({ name, systemPrompt, fields })` | **async**, resolves to the new id (awaited; `create_child_bot` returns the id) | | `bot.setSystemPrompt(id, text)` | text ds-bot appends to the bot's system prompt (`BotView.systemPrompt`); the tree only replaces its own marked block | | `fields.get/set` | **sync**, namespaced by the scope; `null` removes a key | | `on('change' \| 'bot.created' \| 'bot.removed', fn, { all? })` | `change`: `{ botId, plugin, key, value, prev }`, own plugin unless `{ all: true }`; `bot.removed`: `{ botId, bot }` after deletion, parent read from `bot.fields['flybot-tree'].parent`; children re-attach to it | | `bot.send.use({ name, before, after, handle })` | tree bot → parent/direct child only; local non-tree bot → tree root only; non-root tree bot → local non-tree bot **deny**, root (Chief) → any local bot ok; `bypass:['social']` only if `bypassSocial: true` | | `tools.register` | `visibleTo(botId)` sync; `execute(args, { botId })`. JSON Schema `minLength`/`maxLength` are dropped by register, so `execute` validates them (`validateArgs`) | | browser | `ctx.flybot.bots()` items carry `fields: { [plugin]: {...} }` (read `fields['flybot-tree']`); tree built in-plugin | | remote senders | `typeof from !== 'string'` or `bot.isRemote(from)`: denied toward an ungranted tree bot (`bot.hasAnyGrant(id) === false`), else no opinion; never redirected to the root | | remote targets | `target.remote === true` (`{ handle, home }`), fallback `bot.isRemote(to)`; never tree members: passed to social | | `bot.created` | handled by social; tree does not subscribe | | root | ds-bot's Main Bot (Chief) adopted with `treeRole: 'root'` (`ensureRoot`, idempotent); fallback `Root` only without a Main Bot; earlier auto-created `Root` migrated, not deleted | ### Test From `plugins/tree`: `npm test` (Node 24). It runs `test/tree.test.js` and `test/host.test.js`, which boots the real ds-bot core by its public entry (`import { apply } from 'ds-bot'`) in a plugin-local fake Cordis context (`test/fake-cordis.js`), loads tree with `ctx.plugin(tree, config)` and reaches the host only through `ctx.flybot`. `test/resolve.mjs` maps `ds-bot` to `FLYBOT_CORE`, else the repo-root `core/` (the patched core; `ds-bot/` is pristine upstream); the core's `@deepseek-ai/*` peers come from `DSH_HARNESS` or `/dev/harness`. ds-bot's own `npm test` no longer runs tree's tests (#34). `test/mock-flybot.js` is an in-memory mock of `ctx.flybot`. This repo has no pnpm workspace, so there is no `pnpm --filter` command. ### ds-bot integration (already in place) ds-bot needs no changes for this plugin. `src/host/hooks.js` is a module in ds-bot's `MODULES` list (`index.js`, after `dshUpdate`, before `remoteChat` and `channel`), and `index.js` `provideFlyBot()` exposes `rt.flybot` as the `flybot` service, so `inject: ['flybot']` resolves. `scripts/lint.mjs` lints `plugins/`, and `build-client.mjs --check` covers the client bundle. ### Cleanup `apply()` registers its disposer with `ctx.effect(() => dispose, 'flybot-tree')`, so unloading the plugin removes the send middleware, tools, event listeners and root-adoption timers. On a host without `ctx.effect` it falls back to `ctx.on('dispose')`. `apply()` also returns `{ tree, dispose }`.

A team of long-lived AI Bots that can split work down a tree and chat with your friends' Bots.

English | 中文

FlyBot is two plugins on top of a pinned [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot) core for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): - **`@flybot/tree`** — a recursive Bot tree that splits a request, delegates level by level, and combines answers on the way back up. - **`@flybot/social`** — connect your Bots as friends with other homes and chat through a self-hosted [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server, with owner approvals. ## Features ### Tree plugin (`@flybot/tree`) Turns your Bots into one recursive tree that splits a request into parts, sends each part down a level, and combines the answers on the way back up. ![Tree plugin: Chief splits a Hangzhou trip across Travel, Food, and Budget](docs/images/demo-tree.gif) - **One root.** The tree's root is the Main Bot (Chief); no new bot is created for it. A separate `Root` bot is created only if the team has Bots but no Main Bot. Existing local Bots join under the root as its children, up to `maxChildren`. - **Children on demand.** Any tree Bot (not only the Main/root) calls `create_child_bot(name, role_description)` to make a child directly under *itself*; the tool takes no parent argument. Calls are handled one at a time per parent, so parallel calls never go over the limits or create two siblings with the same name. The rules: - names are 1–40 characters, and duplicate sibling names are rejected (case and spaces ignored); - depth is at most 5 (the root counts as 1), with at most 8 children per Bot (set in `limits.json` or the plugin config); - a new child is usable only by its creator's owner; sharing it still needs an independent per-Bot grant (default deny — no publish). - **Level-by-level delegation.** Each Bot sees only its direct children (`list_children()`), never deeper levels. - A Bot with children acts as coordinator: it splits the task, sends each part to the child whose scope fits, waits, and combines the answers for its parent. - A Bot with no children does the work itself. - **Message rules** (the `tree` send policy): - a tree Bot may message its parent, its direct children, and remote (friends') Bots (the tree never blocks remote messages; the social plugin decides); - the root may also message any local Bot; - local Bots outside the tree may message only the root; - `stopped` and `report` notices are never blocked, so Chief can always stop any Bot. - **Reparenting.** When a Bot is deleted, its children move up to its parent. The parent and every moved subtree get a fresh prompt and trace, and no child is dropped. - **Trace line.** When a tree Bot answers its *parent*, it starts the answer with its path, e.g. `Chief → Work → Dev`. Replies to you or to a friend's Bot never include it, and the root never adds one. - **Your prompts are kept.** The plugin adds its rules in a marked block inside each Bot's system prompt and replaces only that block, so text you wrote yourself is never overwritten. - **Sidebar.** The Bot list is drawn as one expandable tree with Chief on top. Bots outside the tree are shown directly under Chief. Install (needs the core, `path:/core`): ```bash npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/tree" ``` ### Social plugin (`@flybot/social`) Every local Bot can chat with friends' Bots through a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server that **you self-host**. Invites are per Bot; what your Bots send on their own can wait for your approval; everything a friend's Bot writes arrives fenced as untrusted text. ![Social plugin: add a friend, chat with their Bot, approve a held reply in Bot Social, and see it arrive](docs/images/demo-social.gif) *Demo: add a friend, message their Bot, the reply is held by Bot Social because it mentions money, the friend's owner approves it, and it appears in the chat.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-social.mp4) - **One-click onboarding.** On first start with a `server` configured, FlyBot calls `POST /v1/onboard/flybot`, creates your home (`@.home`), and stores credentials in `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-social.json` (mode 600). - **Members.** Access is a per-Bot **grant** (default deny, Chief included). A local Bot becomes `@.` on the server when you invite someone to that Bot, when it joins an invite, or when you bring it into a face-to-face room. The sidebar lists only Bots granted to you. **Manage access** on a Bot shows who has it and **Revoke**. Deleted Bots are revoked. Ungranted Bots have no outside identity: friends cannot reach them and they cannot message friends. - **Friends in the Bot list.** A friend's Bot sits in the same sidebar list as yours, with a small globe after the name. Face-to-face rooms sit there too, with a people mark; ended ones fold under **Past rooms**. Click a row to open a normal chat. Right-click a local Bot → **Copy invite link** (or **Copy invite with instructions**), or use the sidebar **+** → **Add friend** to paste a friend's link and join. **Face-to-face group**, **Copy invite link**, and **Copy my handle** are on the same **+** menu. **Auto-send** for a friend is on that Bot's settings. - **Approvals.** Inbound messages from a friend arrive immediately. Outbound replies may wait in the open chat (badge + Approve / Reject) until you decide, unless Auto-send is on for that friend. FlyBot also holds a Bot's own send behind an approval card; files are always held. - **Tools.** Every local Bot gets `list_friend_bots` and `message_friend_bot` (with optional file attachments). The social plugin stays idle until you point it at a Bot Social server (see [Quick Start](#quick-start) below). ## Quick Start ### 1. Prerequisites - **Node.js 22.19+** and **pnpm** (`npm install -g pnpm`, or `corepack enable`). - **Git**, to install from GitHub. - An API key for at least one model provider (for example DeepSeek). ### 2. Install FlyBot (core + plugins) ```sh npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/core" npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/social" npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/tree" ``` The first line is the FlyBot core (package `ds-bot`). The plugins are optional but recommended. On DSH Desktop: **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste one of the `github:` addresses above, then **Install** and **Enable now**. ### 3. Run the web app ```sh npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 web --port 3080 ``` Open the printed `http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=…` link. The first time you open Chief, pick a model (or open **Models and providers…**). ### 4. Self-host Bot Social (for friends' Bots) `@flybot/social` needs a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server. It does not ship one. Deploy Bot Social yourself (see its README), then set a public base URL so invite links work: ```sh # example only — use your own host export PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://your-server.example.com export PORT=8787 # start Bot Social as documented in https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social ``` Point FlyBot at that server in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`, then restart DSH: ```yaml - id: flybot-social config: server: https://your-server.example.com displayName: Your Name ``` On first start FlyBot registers your home. No Bot is shared until you grant it. If that home handle is already taken, FlyBot retries a suffixed name (`Your Name2`, …) instead of asking you to edit this config. **Copy my handle** on the sidebar **+** copies your connected handle. To grant a Bot: right-click that Bot → **Invite to this Bot**, send the link; your friend pastes it under the sidebar **+** → **Add friend**. Accepting the invite grants that Bot only. A friend's inbound messages arrive immediately. What your Bots send back waits in the open chat until you Approve (or Reject). Auto-send for a new friend is off until you turn it on. If a friend sees no reply, look for the **to approve** badge. Without a `server`, the social plugin stays idle by design. Tree works without Bot Social. ## Built on FlyBot keeps the upstream DS Bot core byte-identical (`ds-bot/`, pinned in `ds-bot.pin.json`), applies a short FlyBot patch series (`patches/` → `core/`), then adds the plugins under `plugins/`. See [#34](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/issues/34). The web UI (header, About, settings, update popups) says FlyBot; the npm package and update-check still use the upstream `ds-bot` name and repository. ## More - Core options and internals: [`core/README.md`](core/README.md) - Contributing: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md) - Known issues: [docs/known-issues.md](docs/known-issues.md) - Architecture notes: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) ## License [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). Third-party notices in [NOTICE](NOTICE). ## Disclaimer FlyBot is an independent community project. **It is not an official DeepSeek product.** Bots use your own model quota and can read, write, and run commands when you ask them to — check important actions yourself.

# dsh-plugin-codex-login 在 DSH Desktop 或 Web 的「设置 → 模型」中给 `openai-codex` 提供商增加 ChatGPT OAuth 登录、进度、验证码输入、取消和本地退出。插件调用宿主已经注册的 `llm-pi-ai` 授权流程；OAuth 端点、令牌存储与刷新由 DSH 和模型适配器负责。它不是 OpenAI API Key 登录，也不会复制令牌到浏览器。 ## 前提与安装 需要提供 `authorization`、`credentials`、`llm-pi-ai` 的 DSH Desktop 或 Web profile，以及支持 `settings.models.provider-card` 的模型设置页。插件 Host 使用 Typert Remote，界面通过已有的鉴权 `/api` 连接调用；不开放额外 HTTP 路由。与发行版使用兼容的 DSH 版本（参见 `package.json` 中的 peer dependencies）。 在 DSH 可执行文件所在的环境中，选择实际使用的 profile 安装本目录： ```powershell dsh plugin --profile desktop add "link:D:\program\dsh-plugins\dsh-plugin-codex-login" # 如果使用的是 Web profile，改用： dsh plugin --profile web add "link:D:\program\dsh-plugins\dsh-plugin-codex-login" ``` bundle 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 插入 `codex-login` 行；安装、卸载或更新本目录代码后，完全退出并重新打开 Desktop（Web 则重启对应 profile 并刷新网页）。本目录不会自动修改正在运行的 profile 或读取任何现存的登录凭据。 在「设置 → 模型」中添加并保存 `openai-codex`：**API 密钥留空，不配置 `apiKeyEnv`**。保存后该提供商卡片才显示登录按钮。点击「使用 ChatGPT 登录」，按页面上的 HTTPS 链接在浏览器完成认证；需要手动输入验证码时，在插件表单里提交。登录成功后由原来的 `llm-pi-ai` 适配器持有并自动刷新授权凭据；不需要第二份凭据设置。若提供商设置中写了 API 密钥引用，可能覆盖这一 OAuth 路径，应先清除引用。 ## 安全与生命周期 - 宿主只向发起登录的卡片返回一次性的随机 ticket 和长度受限的 OAuth 通知/问题（通知可含一次性设备码）。访问、刷新令牌和已输入的答案不出现在状态响应中。答案仅通过已有的鉴权 Remote 通道回传宿主；不要在浏览器控制台记录验证码。 - 如果浏览器提示授权成功而卡片仍显示“未登录”，表示 DSH 尚未确认保存一条新凭据。失败状态只向持有 ticket 的卡片返回安全类别：`record-not-committed`（本次未提交凭据）、`credential-store`、`network`、`oauth-rejected`、`http-4xx/5xx` 或 `unknown`；宿主日志也只包含这些类别，不包含异常原文、授权链接、验证码或令牌。`unknown` 不能据此判断根因；若需排查，请只提供卡片上的类别，不要发送授权链接或验证码。 - 同一 Codex 凭据同时只运行一次登录；只有持有 ticket 的客户端能查看这次登录的通知或回答问题。关闭卡片会取消它发起的登录；页面断线后最迟 `timeoutSeconds` 秒取消（默认 600 秒，可配置 60–3600 秒）。宿主卸载会中止并等待登录结束。 - “退出登录”仅调用 DSH 凭据服务删除本机 `llm-pi-ai/openai-codex` 记录；**不会在 OpenAI 端撤销已颁发的授权**。如需吊销，在 OpenAI/ChatGPT 的帐号安全页面管理授权。已完成授权但尚在提交中的取消操作可能仍留下一份凭据，卡片状态以宿主 `describeRecord` 为准。 - 本地 Web 界面的帐号安全性继承 DSH 的 Connection/Gateway 鉴权；不要把 DSH Web 暴露为未受保护的公共站点。 ## 验证 在本目录运行 `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`。测试以替身授权流覆盖 ticket 隔离、通知 URL 协议、问题回答、取消、卸载、本地退出和敏感信息不返回。实际 OAuth 回调需使用自己的 ChatGPT 帐号手动验证；测试不触发真实登录。 # TOFU BOX 自己日常用的一组 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) 插件，都在这个仓库里，从 npm 安装（源码在 GitHub）。 [中文](#中文) · [English](#english) --- ## 中文 把下面命令里的 `--profile web` 换成你自己的 profile。 **一键全套**（推荐，桌面端同理——插件管理页的安装框里直接粘贴 `tofu-box`）： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add tofu-box ``` `tofu-box` 是伞包：不含代码，以依赖拉入下面五个子包并用一个 patch 层注册全部插件行（dsh-base 同款 bundle 模式）。装伞包**或**逐个装子包，二选一，不要混装；伞包装完后在插件管理页是一个整体条目，不能单独禁用其中某一个。 | 插件 | 说明 | 支持的 dsh 版本 | 平台 | 安装 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **model-tuning** | 只补官方没有的两块：①**官方「设置 → 模型」卡片里的兼容补丁**——系统提示角色 `compat.supportsDeveloperRole`、Anthropic 思考格式 `compat.forceAdaptiveThinking`、内置目录路由的推理档位 `modelOverrides..reasoningEfforts`，官方 Models 页没有这些控件；经官方 `settings.models.provider-card` --profile web add dsh-plugin-read-image-preview` | | **shell-selector** | 「设置 → Shell」里选 AI 执行命令用哪个 shell：PowerShell 7 / Windows PowerShell 5.1 / 自定义路径。只写宿主 `pwsh-sandbox` 条目本来就支持的 0.1.7-rc.1；0.2.0-rc.2 单测通过 | Win11 实测；Linux/macOS 未测 | `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-shell-selector` | | **computer-use** | 13 个 `computer_*` 工具：截图/元素树、鼠标、键盘、开应用，写操作有审批弹窗；v2 基于 Cua Driver 进程内 SDK（无守护/MCP/PowerShell），v2.3 起「打开应用」先在窗口表里复用已有窗口（含唤醒最小化），**绝不重复启动**已登录的应用，详见 [README](dsh-plugin-computer-use/README.md) | ≥ 0.1.5-rc.1（peer 声明），实测 0.1.7-rc.1 与 0.2.0-rc.2（0.2.0 需 ≥ 标记块并热生效（官方暂不提供 MCP 配置界面），详见 [README](dsh-plugin-mcp-ui/README.md) | ≥ 0.1.6-alpha.1（依赖 typert 网关，旧版不可用）；**0.2.0 需 ≥ 1.0.3**——旧版 peer `^0.1.6` 不覆盖 0.2.0，会被 profile 启动直接拒载；MCP 增删路径尚未实机验证 | Win11 实测；Linux/macOS 未测 | `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mcp-ui` | computer-use **v2.5 起自动开启原生 Wayland**，并内置 Ubuntu/GNOME 的 WinRects 扩展安装与诊断入口。GNOME 用户须安装扩展并注销登录一次；键鼠操作还需系统 portal 授权。安装步骤和实测范围见 [docs/RELEASE-model-tuning-v3-20261017.md](docs/RELEASE-model-tuning-v3-20261017.md)。 装完重启 dsh 就能用。注册配置打进包里了（`dsh.bundle.patch`），不需要动 cordis 文件。卸载把 `add` 换成 `remove`。也可以从 git 直装（未发版 / 想追 HEAD `link:`，改完不用重装。要发版：`./publish.ps1 -Publish`（会先跑伞包同步校验，未入库的插件目录自动跳过）。 上表的版本区间为实测范围，未标注下限的插件不保证能在更早版本上运行。本轮迁移（0.1.7-alpha.2 → 0.1.7-rc.1）改动了 model-search、model-tuning、read-image-preview 三个插件，新增 shell-selector；image-generation 与 title-model 曾并入 model-tuning（v2）；**v3 起标题生成交还官方，绘图能力保留在 model-tuning 内**（不再单独发包，升级指引见其 README）；computer-use 与 mcp-ui 不需要改动，两者都在跑着 0.1.7-rc.1 的实际 profile 里加载通过：computer-use 的 13 个 `computer_*` 工具全部注册且被持续调用（截图 + 元素树、后台 element 点击、sequence、唤醒最小化窗口），mcp-ui 只到「加载与 compose 通过」这一步——它托管的 profile patch 里没有 MCP 块、当前 0 个 server，所以增删改的读写路径至今没有实机跑过，跟 dsh 版本无关。dsh 版本更新频繁，可能影响稳定性。并且插件均由 AI 完成，肯定会有很多潜在 bug。 > **v3 边界收缩（2026-10，基线 0.2.1-rc.1）**：model-tuning 3.0.0 删掉「用途（标题生成）」页，不再 `disabled` 官方 `session-title-llm` 行——需要独立标题模型就在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 覆盖该行（字段见其 README）；「模型参数」页的上下文窗口 / 最大输出 / 输入模态 / 模型发现交还官方「设置 → 模型」页；只保留官方没有的兼容开关、内置目录路由推理覆盖与绘图。官方可选组合包「随对话更新的标题」不再与本插件互斥。重叠盘点见 [docs/PLUGIN-SCOPE-dsh-0.2.1-rc.1.md](docs/PLUGIN-SCOPE-dsh-0.2.1-rc.1.md)，**发布、下线插件清单与迁移/安装说明见 [docs/RELEASE-model-tuning-v3-20261017.md](docs/RELEASE-model-tuning-v3-20261017.md)**。 dsh 0.2.0 这一轮（详见 [docs/UPGRADE-dsh-0.2.0-rc.2.md](docs/UPGRADE-dsh-0.2.0-rc.2.md)）：四个契约面（bundle 机制 / 注入包 / slot / 服务方法）全部未变，唯一破坏点是 **peer 版本门禁**——`^0.1.6` 这类 caret 范围在 0.x 上不覆盖 0.2.0，运行时会直接拒载对应插件行。已发布的修复版：model-tuning 2.0.1、computer-use 2.4.1、mcp-ui 1.0.3（伞包 tofu-box 1.0.2 同步）。仍在 0.1.x 的用户升级 dsh 前先把这三个包升到上述版本即可。 升级 dsh 后起不来？多数是某个插件在新版本下坏了，而 dsh 默认一个插件崩就整个不启动。仓库自带一个启动急救工具（clone 本仓库后运行）： ```sh node tools/doctor/doctor.mjs --profile web ``` 它会自动定位是哪个插件的问题（报错没点名也能靠二分测试查出来），先尝试 `dsh plugin update` 修复，修不好会问你要不要先禁用该插件让 dsh 跑起来，事后 `enable` 一键恢复。 未来可能新增更多插件。 --- ## English A few [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins I use daily. Install from npm — sources live on GitHub. Replace `--profile web` with your profile. **Everything in one shot** (recommended; on the desktop client just paste `tofu-box` into the plugin manager's install box): ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add tofu-box ``` `tofu-box` is an umbrella package: no code of its own, it pulls the five plugins below as dependencies and registers all their rows in one patch layer (the same bundle pattern dsh-base uses). Install the umbrella **or** pick individual plugins — not both; after the umbrella is installed it shows up as a single entry in the plugin manager and individual pieces can't be disabled from the GUI. | Plugin | What it does | dsh versions | Platform | Install | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **model-tuning** | Fills only what the official build lacks: (1) **compat add-ons inside the official Models cards** — per-model `compat.supportsDeveloperRole`, `compat.forceAdaptiveThinking`, and reasoning-level overrides for installed-catalog routes (`modelOverrides..reasoningEfforts`), none of which the official Models page exposes; registered through the official `settings.models.provider-card` seat, so there is no separate parameters page. (2) **images** — drawing-model config, the `generate_image` / `list_image_models` tools and a direct generation panel, originals kept byte-for-byte. **Since v3 the title route belongs to the shipped `session-title-llm` row and model parameters to the official Models page**; the old title fields are gone from the Config, though existing profiles still load ([README](dsh-plugin-model-tuning/README.md)) | baseline **0.2.1-rc.1** (tested); the provider-card seat exists since 0.1.2-alpha but this package is verified on the rc line only | Tested on Win11; Linux/macOS untested | `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-model-tuning` | | **read-image-preview** | One viewer for every image in a session (read_image, computer-use screenshots, message images): zoom, pan, annotate, crop, then Enter puts it into the composer; one-click screen capture with region select next to the composer | 1.6+ fills the official gallery slots and needs ≥ 0.2.0-rc.2; verified on 0.2.1-alpha.4 | Tested on Win11; Linux/macOS untested | `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-read-image-preview` | | **shell-selector** | A "Settings → Shell" page for picking which shell the AI runs commands in: PowerShell 7 / Windows PowerShell 5.1 / a custom path. It only writes the `pwshPath` field the host's own `pwsh-sandbox` entry already supports, so the next command uses your choice — no restart, no swapped executor, and sandboxing, approval, timeouts and exit codes stay exactly as shipped; when 5.1 is active it also registers a dialect note so the model knows `&&` and `??` don't exist; Git Bash stays greyed out with the reason shown, because confined execution is unverified ([README](dsh-plugin-shell-selector/README.md)) | ≥ 0.1.7-alpha.2, tested on 0.1.7-rc.1; unit tests pass on 0.2.0-rc.2 | Tested on Win11; Linux/macOS untested | `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-shell-selector` | | **computer-use** | 13 `computer_*` tools: window screenshots + accessibility tree, mouse, keyboard, launching apps; input actions require approval; v2 runs on the in-process Cua Driver SDK (no daemon/MCP/PowerShell); since v2.3 "open app" reuses an existing window (restoring it when minimized) and **never starts a second instance** of an app that is already running ([README](dsh-plugin-computer-use/README.md)) | ≥ 0.1.5-rc.1 (peer dep), tested on 0.1.7-rc.1 and 0.2.0-rc.2 (0.2.0 needs ≥ 2.4.1: approval probing no longer touches private APIs) | Cross-platform (tested on Windows 11; macOS/Linux untested) | `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-computer-use` | | **mcp-ui** | "Settings → MCP Servers" page: add/edit/remove stdio & streamable-http servers; writes them into the profile patch and hot-applies (the official build ships no MCP UI yet) ([README](dsh-plugin-mcp-ui/README.md)) | ≥ 0.1.6-alpha.1 (needs the typert gateway; won't work on older dsh); **0.2.0 needs ≥ 1.0.3** — the old `^0.1.6` peer doesn't cover 0.2.0 and profile startup rejects the plugin outright; add/remove-server path not exercised yet | Tested on Win11; Linux/macOS untested | `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mcp-ui` | computer-use **v2.5 automatically enables native Wayland** and includes a WinRects installer and diagnostics for Ubuntu/GNOME. Install the extension, log out and back in once, and allow the system portal prompt for input. See the [computer-use setup guide](dsh-plugin-computer-use/README.md). > `model-search` (model picker search box) was removed in 2026-10: the official picker has had search since 0.2.0-rc.2, and this plugin replaced the whole official menu at priority -1, hiding whatever the official menu gains later (such as the reasoning levels in 0.2.1-alpha.4). Run `dsh plugin --profile

remove dsh-plugin-model-search` to get the official menu back; the tofu-box umbrella drops it from 1.1.0. > > `team-task-route` (pinning one specific agent-team session's teammates to a chosen model) was removed in 2026-09: it hardcoded a session id in `index.js` and only made sense for one throwaway debugging session. It can be recovered from git history if ever needed. > **v3 scope cut (2026-10, baseline 0.2.1-rc.1)**: model-tuning 3.0.0 drops the "purposes (session titles)" tab and no longer disables the shipped `session-title-llm` row — set a custom title route by overriding that row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (fields in its README). Context-window / max-output / input-modality editing and model discovery are back on the official "Settings → Models" page; only the compat add-ons, installed-catalog reasoning overrides and image generation remain. The official optional "titles that update with the conversation" bundle is no longer mutually exclusive with this plugin. All plugins at once (npm names; the `tofu-box` umbrella is equivalent): ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add \ dsh-plugin-model-tuning \ dsh-plugin-read-image-preview \ dsh-plugin-shell-selector \ dsh-plugin-computer-use \ dsh-plugin-mcp-ui ``` Restart dsh after installing. Registration is bundled in each package (`dsh.bundle.patch`), nothing to wire up. To remove: `dsh plugin --profile web remove `. Git installs still work (`git+https://github.com/tofu-zyc/dsh-plugin-tofu-box.git#path:dsh-plugin-`, or `#path:tofu-box` for the umbrella) when you want unreleased changes; npm installs update via semver, git installs always track HEAD. First-time computer-use installs may fail on koffi's blocked build script — follow dsh's hint and add `allowBuilds: koffi: false` to the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (koffi ships prebuilt binaries), then retry. Hacking on this repo? See [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) — point the profile at your checkout with `link:` and you stop reinstalling after every edit. Publishing: `./publish.ps1 -Publish` (runs the umbrella sync check first and skips plugin directories that aren't committed). The version ranges above are what has actually been tested; plugins without a stated lower bound aren't guaranteed to work on older dsh. This migration round (0.1.7-alpha.2 → 0.1.7-rc.1) touched model-search, model-tuning and read-image-preview and added shell-selector; image-generation and title-model were merged into model-tuning in v2, and **since v3 the title route is back on the shipped row while only the drawing capability (plus the official gaps listed above) stays in model-tuning** — none of them are published separately anymore (its README has the migration steps); computer-use and mcp-ui needed no changes and both load in a live 0.1.7-rc.1 profile — all 13 `computer_*` tools register and are in continuous use (screenshots with accessibility trees, background element clicks, sequences, restoring minimized windows), while mcp-ui is only verified as far as loading and composing: its managed patch block is absent and 0 servers are configured, so its add/edit/remove path has never been exercised, on any dsh version. dsh updates frequently, which may affect stability. All the plugins are completed by AI, so there will certainly be many potential bugs. The dsh 0.2.0 round (details in [docs/UPGRADE-dsh-0.2.0-rc.2.md](docs/UPGRADE-dsh-0.2.0-rc.2.md)): all four contract surfaces (bundle mechanics / injected packages / slots / service methods) are unchanged; the only breakage was the **peer-version gate** — a `^0.1.6` caret range doesn't cover 0.2.0 on 0.x, and the runtime rejects the plugin row outright. Fixed releases: model-tuning 2.0.1, computer-use 2.4.1, mcp-ui 1.0.3 (umbrella tofu-box 1.0.2). If you're still on 0.1.x, bump those three packages before upgrading dsh. dsh won't boot after an upgrade? Usually one plugin broke under the new version, and dsh takes the whole process down with it. This repo ships a boot-recovery tool (clone it first): ```sh node tools/doctor/doctor.mjs --profile web ``` It figures out which plugin is at fault (via bisection, even when the error names nobody), tries `dsh plugin update` first, and if that fails asks whether to disable the plugin so dsh can start. Re-enable anytime with `enable `. More plugins may be added in the future.

fullManifest.name: dsh-plugin-computer-use
fullManifest.description: computer-use v2.5：Ubuntu/GNOME Wayland 自动检测并启用原生后端；内置 WinRects 扩展安装与诊断命令，驱动最低 0.28.3。基于 Cua Driver 进程内 SDK 的跨平台桌面操作。13 个工具（截图/窗口列表/缩放/光标/移动/点击/拖拽/滚动/输入/按键/打开应用/连续动作/等待）。v2.4.1 适配 dsh 0.2.0：审批探测改走公有 overrideOf/session 覆盖 + 部署默认策略，任何探测形状失效时保守放行，杜绝 danger-full-access 会话因私有 API 变动而自锁全部工具。v2.4 修「宿主闲置后窗口/应用枚举静默变空」：全部驱动调用统一挂命名 session（查询也不例外），session 卡死按 end→start→重试→重建运行时分级自愈，list_windows 报错不再吞成『无窗口』；computer_type 桌面输入遇非 ASCII 自动改走剪贴板粘贴（绕开 IME 对 CJK/emoji 的损坏，事后恢复用户剪贴板）；桌面坐标给成物理分辨率时自动映射进截图坐标系；computer_screenshot 新增 save= 同时存盘+进剪贴板。v2.3 系列能力保留：open 先查进程表绝不启动第二实例、识别启动即退出的假成功、托盘态应用默认只报告不代启。Windows 宿主进程自动切 Per-Monitor-V2 DPI 感知，默认后台注入不抢焦点，元素树+element_token 精确操作。无需守护进程/MCP/PowerShell。写操作走原生 tools/pre-execute 审批。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-computer-use 让模型**看见窗口和桌面并操作鼠标键盘**——v2 起整个后端换装 [Cua Driver](https://cua.ai) 的**进程内 SDK**（`@trycua/cua-driver`，Rust 原生运行时随 npm 包按平台分发，直接加载进 dsh 宿主进程）：**无守护进程、无 MCP、无 PowerShell**，装上即用，跨 Windows / macOS / Linux。 ## v2.5：Ubuntu 26.04 / GNOME Wayland 旧版没有开启驱动的原生 Wayland 开关，即使 `DISPLAY=:0` 存在，它也可能只是 XWayland，无法代表整个桌面。v2.5 在加载原生库前检测 `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` / `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`，自动设置 `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`；驱动依赖最低升到 npm 已发布的 0.28.3。环境中显式设置的 `0` / `false` 会保留，行配置 `wayland: on` / `off` 可覆盖。 GNOME/Mutter 还需要 **WinRects Shell 扩展**提供窗口几何、截图和精确激活；输入通过 Remote Desktop portal/libei 获取系统授权。npm SDK 没带 CLI 发行包中的扩展，因此本插件随包附带上游 WinRects v8（支持 GNOME 45–50；含来源与 MIT 许可证），并提供安装和检查入口。无需另装 Cua 守护进程。 **从 npm 安装/更新**（在 Ubuntu 的图形桌面终端运行，替换自己的 profile）： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-computer-use@2.5.0 npx --yes --package=dsh-plugin-computer-use@2.5.0 dsh-computer-use-wayland install # 注销并重新登录一次后： npx --yes --package=dsh-plugin-computer-use@2.5.0 dsh-computer-use-wayland status ``` 如果已经使用 `tofu-box`，通过 `dsh plugin --profile web update tofu-box` 更新依赖，再执行上面的扩展安装/检查命令。伞包现有 `^2.4.1` 范围覆盖 2.5.0；无需另外添加单独的 computer-use 插件行。更新与安装扩展后重启 dsh。 **从本仓库试用：在 Ubuntu 的图形桌面终端运行**（把路径和 profile 换成自己的）： ```sh cd /path/to/dsh-plugins node dsh-plugin-computer-use/scripts/wayland.mjs install ``` 安装只写当前用户的扩展目录，保留已启用的其他扩展。之后需要**注销并重新登录一次**，让 GNOME 加载扩展；Wayland 下不能用 Alt+F2 → r 重启 Shell。 ```sh cd /path/to/dsh-plugins node dsh-plugin-computer-use/scripts/wayland.mjs status dsh plugin --profile web add "link:$(pwd)/dsh-plugin-computer-use" ``` 重启 dsh，然后先试 `computer_windows` 和 `computer_screenshot`。第一次需要前台输入时，允许系统弹出的远程桌面/键鼠控制授权。此授权属于驱动运行时，重启后可能再次询问。插件安装不会自动授予它。 **用本地 tgz 安装**：下载/复制 `dsh-plugin-computer-use-2.5.0.tgz` 到 Ubuntu 后运行： ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-plugin-computer-use-2.5.0.tgz npx --yes --package=./dsh-plugin-computer-use-2.5.0.tgz dsh-computer-use-wayland install # 注销并重新登录后： npx --yes --package=./dsh-plugin-computer-use-2.5.0.tgz dsh-computer-use-wayland status ``` 如果通过 `tofu-box` 安装，应更新伞包中的依赖；不要叠装单独的 computer-use 行。也可直接对该 profile 下已安装包的 `scripts/wayland.mjs` 运行 `install` / `status`。 `status` 检查实际加载的扩展版本、Remote Desktop portal 的键鼠能力、无障碍总线与会话变量；缺项时返回非零退出码。Ubuntu 缺少组件时可以安装： ```sh sudo apt install libglib2.0-bin at-spi2-core xdg-desktop-portal xdg-desktop-portal-gnome ``` 请从同一个图形用户会话启动 dsh，并保留 `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`、`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`、`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`。不要用 root 或另一条不带桌面环境的 SSH 会话启动。若 GNOME 的 Extensions 总开关关闭，请先在扩展管理器开启，再运行检查。 Wayland 的后台能力取决于应用的 AT-SPI 支持，像素/键盘输入可能需要临时前置窗口；不保证与 Windows 一样能操作完全遮挡的窗口。缺少扩展、portal 或权限时，驱动错误和空窗口表会附带安装提示。Sway/KDE 等沿用驱动各自的原生支持范围，WinRects 安装器只用于 GNOME。参见[上游平台支持说明](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-driver/concepts/platform-support)。 当前开发机为 Windows；本版已做会话检测、安装器、诊断与插件接入回归，**尚未在 Ubuntu 26.04 实机完成截图/输入验收**。 ## 打开应用的行为（v2.3 起） `computer_open` 只做一件事：**能复用就复用，确认没在跑才启动**。它按下面的顺序判断，顺序本身就是设计——"有没有进程"比"有没有窗口"可靠得多： 1. **进程在跑、窗口也在** → 直接复用那个窗口；窗口最小化时先唤醒它再截图； 2. **进程在跑、但没有任何窗口**（微信/企业微信/QQ/钉钉这类应用的托盘态很常见）→ **不动它**，把情况报给你，请你从托盘图标点开。让这类应用重走一遍自己的启动流程，可能把本地登录态弄丢（要重新扫码）； 3. **进程确实不在** → 按应用的启动入口（UWP 用 AUMID，桌面应用用快捷方式里的完整命令行）启动；启动后进程立刻退出、或窗口始终不出现，会明确报出来，不会假装成功。 要让它对第 2 种情况也去试着激活（部分应用点了就恢复），传 `activate_running=true`，或用行配置 `activateRunning: true`。 窗口句柄只当线索用：驱动给的窗口 id 可能在你操作前就失效了，插件会按 pid / 应用名重新取一次。 ## v2.4：闲置后的窗口枚举、中文输入、截图存盘 一条真实会话记录（"操作微信给联系人打招呼"）暴露的三个问题，都在这一版修掉： - **宿主闲置 ~5 分钟后，窗口/应用枚举静默变空。** 驱动的隐式会话闲置即报废，而 `list_windows` / `list_apps` / `launch_app` 之前**不带**命名会话标签——它们挂在隐式会话上，报废后报 "session has ended"，又被插件吞成"没有匹配的窗口"，模型被误导去乱试应用名、最后弃用插件改走 pwsh。v2.4 起**所有**驱动调用统一挂命名会话（查询也不例外），session 卡死按 `end_session 清尸 → start_session 复活 → 重试 → 整个运行时重建` 分级自愈（0.28.1 的 watchdog 数据竞争能把传输层卡死一整个进程生命周期，上游 0.28.2 已修，建议升级）。查询报错也**不再吞成"无窗口"**，原样抛给模型。 - **桌面打字输中文/emoji 必乱码。** 前台 SendInput 要过当前输入法，CJK 与代理对会被损坏（实测：这→！！、👋→🙏）。v2.4 起 `computer_type desktop=true` 遇到非 ASCII 文本自动改走**剪贴板 + ctrl+v**（驱动的 clipboard 工具），打完把你的剪贴板恢复回去（纯文本可恢复；图片等无法保存的剪贴板会被替换，结果里注明）。窗口内打字走 UIA/WM_CHAR，本身就是 Unicode 原生路径，不受影响。 - **桌面坐标给成了物理分辨率不再报错重来。** 模型经常按截图的原生尺寸（如 3200×2000）读坐标，而动作校验的是发给它的缩放帧（1568×980）——v2.4 自动按轴映射进帧坐标并在结果里注明，真正超出物理桌面才报错。 - **`computer_screenshot save="路径.png"`**：把截图写盘（桌面截图保**原生分辨率**，窗口截图保帧上限）并同时放进系统剪贴板，随后 `computer_key desktop ctrl+v` 即可把图贴进聊天框——"发一张证明截图"不再需要 pwsh 绕路（那条路还得自己重新发现 DPI 感知）。 ## v2.2：高 DPI 截图与长时间空闲 - **高 DPI 屏幕的截图与坐标。** Windows 上驱动要求宿主进程已是 Per-Monitor-V2 DPI 感知，而 node.exe 不是：缩放屏上桌面截图只覆盖主屏一部分、坐标也随之偏移。v2.2 在驱动启动前把宿主进程切过去，之后所有数字都是真实物理像素（日志里会打印 `host process DPI awareness = per-monitor-v2`）。开关：行配置 `dpiAware`（默认开）。 - **放一会儿再用不再全体报错。** 驱动的会话闲置 5 分钟即报废，且普通调用不会复活它——v2.2 起固定使用命名会话，并在 `session_ended` 时自动复活重试一次。 ## 范式：窗口为中心 · 元素优先 · 后台优先 - **元素优先。** `computer_screenshot(app=…)` 返回窗口截图**加**无障碍树元素表（带 `element=` 令牌）；`computer_click(element=令牌)` 走 UIA/AX 直调——对后台、最小化甚至移出屏幕的窗口同样有效，指针全程不动。 - **不抢焦点。** 一切输入默认 `delivery_mode: "background"`（PostMessage/UIA 注入，不动你的鼠标、不前置窗口）。个别拒收后台输入的表面（某些 Chromium/Electron 面）由插件**自动升级一次前台投递**，驱动随后把前台还给原窗口。 - **XAML 组合键兜底。** 现代 XAML/WinUI 应用的快捷键藏在收起的菜单后（如记事本 Ctrl+A），驱动的 UIA Accelerator 路由找不到时，插件自动降级为 `press_key + modifiers` 的**前台 SendInput 真实按键**。（若前台被系统前台锁抢占——比如 dsh 就跑在当前前台终端里——会原样抛回驱动的指引文本，模型改走"点开菜单再点元素"。） - **KEYBOARD-FIRST 依然。** 所有描述继续引导模型优先 `computer_open` / `computer_key` / `computer_sequence`，像素点击是兜底手段。 ## 13 个模型可见工具（全部 `computer_*`） | 工具 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `computer_screenshot` | 截**窗口**（默认：上一个操作对象；`app=` 任意应用，含最小化/其他显示器）或主桌面总览；窗口截图附带元素表（`element=` 令牌）；`save=路径.png` 额外存盘（桌面为原生分辨率）并放进剪贴板 | | `computer_windows` | 列全部顶层窗口：pid / window_id / 应用名 / 标题 / 边界 / z 序 / 是否可见 | | `computer_click` | 元素令牌 / 窗口内坐标 / 桌面坐标三选一；`button` `clicks` `keys`（修饰和弦） | | `computer_drag` | 窗口内或桌面拖拽（标题栏拖拽自动升前台） | | `computer_scroll` | 窗口滚动（后台投递，指针不动） | | `computer_type` | 后台文本注入（字段元素令牌走 UIA SetValue 最稳）；`desktop=true` 打给当前前台应用，非 ASCII（中文/emoji）自动改走剪贴板粘贴，事后恢复剪贴板 | | `computer_key` | 按键/组合键（XAML 应用自动走前台 SendInput 兜底，见上），`repeat` 1-10 | | `computer_open` | **打开应用但绝不重复启动**：先在窗口表找已有窗口→复用/唤醒（最小化时 `bring_to_front`）；进程在跑却没有窗口（托盘态）时只报告、请你从托盘点开；确认没在跑才按 `launch_path`/`aumid` 启动 | | `computer_sequence` | 多步 DSL 一气呵成：`key: / type: / wait: / click:x,y / scroll:dir,n / open:name`，全步先校验后执行，**一次审批一张终图** | | `computer_zoom` | 窗口区域原生分辨率放大（读小字）；配 `from_zoom=true` 可在放大图上直接点 | | `computer_cursor` / `computer_move` | 读 / 移动**真实**指针（桌面坐标；后台窗口操作根本不经过指针） | | `computer_wait` | 等待动画/加载并回一张新截图 | ## 坐标系约定 - 窗口动作：x,y = **该窗口上一次截图**的窗口内像素（顶左原点）。 - 桌面动作（`desktop=true`）：x,y = **上一次桌面截图**的像素；桌面帧由驱动按物理像素捕获（`dpiAware` 生效时即真实分辨率），插件缩到 `maxDim` 以内并自动换算回驱动坐标。给成**物理桌面像素**（截图的原生尺寸）时自动按轴映射进帧并在结果里注明，超出物理桌面才报错。 - 元素令牌只活到**同窗口的下一次快照**——报过期就重新 `computer_screenshot` 再取。 - 驱动对窗口截图自行缩放（`set_config max_image_dimension`）且保持坐标/zoom 映射一致；桌面截图**只覆盖主显示器**——其他显示器上的窗口用 `computer_windows` + `app=` 直接操作窗口，别走桌面坐标。 - Windows 桌面目标当前仅支持 `display_id:"primary"`（驱动上游限制，非主屏没有桌面级截图/点击）。 ## 审批 8 个动作类工具（move/click/drag/scroll/type/key/open/sequence）挂在原生 `tools/pre-execute` 审批水路上，默认 `askPolicy: once-per-agent`——**同一会话第一次写操作弹一次批准，之后整轮免批**；行 config 可改 `always` 每次一询、`never` 完全撤掉本插件闸门。截图、列窗口、读光标、zoom、wait 是只读，不审批。审批理由文案会说明"后台注入，不动鼠标不抢焦点"。 闸门**自动跟随会话审批策略**：会话本身处于"不弹审批"模式时（如完全权限下 `approval: never`——此时任何 ask 都会被自动拒绝），本闸门直接放行、由全局权限策略把关，不会自己把自己锁死。 ## 行配置（可全部省略） ```yaml - id: computer-use name: dsh-plugin-computer-use inject: [tools, attachments] config: maxDim: 1568 # 模型帧长边上限（px） settleMs: 600 # 动作后到结果图的等待（毫秒） askPolicy: once-per-agent # 或 always / never telemetry: false # Cua Driver 运行时的无内容产品遥测，默认关 dpiAware: true # Windows：驱动启动前把宿主进程切到 Per-Monitor-V2 DPI 感知 wayland: auto # Linux：自动启用原生 Wayland；on/off 显式覆盖环境开关 restore: true # 允许把已运行应用的最小化窗口唤醒到前台（false = 永不抢焦点） activateRunning: false # 应用在跑但没窗口（托盘态）时，是否让它的启动入口去激活（默认否，只报告） ``` 包内 `cordis.patch.yml` 经 `dsh.bundle.patch` 自 wiring，安装即注册这一行，不用手改 profile 配置。 ## 图像显示在哪 本包**不带 client 半区**。结果图以 `{type:'image', attachment}` 进入工具结果，由 [`dsh-plugin-read-image-preview`](../dsh-plugin-read-image-preview/README.md) 的通用图像卡渲染（缩略图、点击放大、Ctrl+滚轮缩放、拖动平移；`computer_*` 键已在其 `TOOL_LABELS` 注册）。 ## 平台与限制 - **Windows 11 实测**（自测脚本见下）；macOS / Linux **未实机验证**。Linux Wayland 从 v2.5 起自动开启原生后端，GNOME 的安装与诊断见上；macOS 需给运行 dsh 的宿主进程授予"辅助功能/屏幕录制"（TCC）权限，且驱动的 macOS 前台叠加层在进程内形态不可用。 - Windows 高 DPI：启动日志会打印 `host process DPI awareness = …`；正常为 `per-monitor-v2`。若显示 `UNAWARE`（宿主 manifest 或他方抢先固定了感知级别），桌面截图/坐标在缩放屏上不可靠，插件会在每张桌面截图摘要里带显式警告——优先改用 `app=` 窗口操作。 - 桌面截图仅主显示器（窗口级截图不受限）；被最小化的窗口**读树可以、截图不行**，插件会先唤醒它再截——这是唯一会短暂占用前台的动作，`restore: false` 可关掉。 - **窗口枚举可能失灵**：长生命周期的宿主里可能出现 `list_windows` 恒返回 0 窗口（此时桌面截图、光标读取、指定窗口的截图都还正常）。这种情况下按进程判断的部分仍然可靠（不会重复启动应用），但没法定位/点击那个窗口——重启 dsh 可重建枚举。 - 无法向"以管理员权限运行"的窗口注入（Windows UIPI）；前台被终端等前台锁持有者抢占时，需要前台的兜底路径会带回驱动的指引。 - 原生包**没有构建脚本**（纯预编译 DLL/.node/.dylib），pnpm 安装即成功，不需要编译链。 ## 自测 无需图形桌面的 Wayland 回归测试（检测、扩展安装与诊断）： ```sh node --experimental-test-module-mocks --test tests/*.test.mjs ``` ```sh node selftest/run.mjs ``` 在真实桌面上跑：启动记事本（**只操作它自己**，全程后台注入），验证 PNG 编解码、弹性坐标映射、13 工具注册、审批闸门、桌面/窗口截图、`save=` 存盘（原生分辨率）+ 剪贴板、元素输入与 UIA 回读、sequence 预校验与执行、zoom、卸载后运行时拒绝，最后自动回收它启动的那个记事本。会动**真实**指针/前台焦点的桌面域工具（桌面点击/拖拽/移动/桌面粘贴）刻意不测。 ## 安装 / 卸载 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web
